purpose: svapaṭhanārtham (copied by the scribe for his own study)
notes: The two eras conflict. 'śaṃvat 18017' is corrupt. Read as VS 1817 (the catalogue's reading) it gives c. 1760 CE, but ŚS 1691 gives Nov/Dec 1769 CE. VS 1826 would match ŚS 1691, so the 0 in '18017' may be a stray digit or a miswriting of 2. The catalogue has 'ŚS 1681', which looks like the cataloguer amending the śāka toward VS 1817 (1681+135 = 1816, still off by one). The month, ayana and season agree with each other (Mārgaśīrṣa, dakṣiṇāyana, Hemanta). The father's name 'rāvalaharibhā itasya' is most likely 'Rāvala Haribhāī, tasya ātmaja'. Rāvala is a western Indian (Gujarati/Rajasthani) brahmin surname. Vāripura is unidentified; it is the father's residence and is taken as the place of copying only by inference (catalogue). 'lakṣmyaṃke' is the poem's signature word (lakṣmī-aṅka), not a person.
review: p3 Ānandarāma: roles changed from scribe+reader to scribe+owner (svapaṭhanārtham = own study); residence removed (only the father is called vāripuranivāsī)
p2 father: name reread as Haribhāī ('haribhā itasya' = haribhāī tasya), confidence lowered to low; 'rāvala' kept as caste/family title
Date: era/year/ce made consistent. The ŚS 1691 figure is clean and gives c. 1769 CE; VS '18017' is corrupt (1817 → 1760 CE; 1826 would match ŚS 1691). Era set to ŚS and the conflict recorded in notes
Place: as_written now gives the full form 'vāripuranivāśi'; the colophon names it only as a residence, not explicitly as the place of copying
Purpose rephrased

notes: The chronogram rasa (6) agni (3) haya (7) bhū (1), read right to left, gives Śaka 1736. This matches the catalogue field. Caitra of Śaka 1736 falls around March–April 1814 CE. The cataloguer's restoration [ra] of the first syllable is needed to read rasa = 6. The cataloguer marked '†guṇāṃ ya svādhvi pramito†' as corrupt. It stands just before 'vyalikhal' ('wrote') and needs a subject, so it probably hides the scribe's name or a self-description (e.g. a name beginning Guṇa-?). title: Ugratārākavaca
subject: Stotra
date_raw: rasārasābhū isa bhū śake mārge site śanau || dvādaśyāṃ
colophon: iti rudrayāmale ugratārākavacaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ || || rasārasābhū isa bhū śake mārge site śanau || dvādaśyāṃ malikhaḍgaṃ gāviśṇu………… || || śubhaṃ || || (fol. 4r8-9)
notes: The text 'malikhaḍgaṃ gāviśṇu…………' is probably a corruption of '…m alikhad Gaṅgāviṣṇu…' ('Gaṅgāviṣṇu wrote'). The name may be truncated because a lacuna follows it. The bhūtasaṃkhyā chronogram 'rasārasābhū isa bhū' is corrupt. It seems to contain rasa (6), rasā (earth, 1), ibha? (elephant, 8) and bhū (1). Possible readings, taken right to left, are: rasa-aṣṭa/ibha-ibha-bhū = 1886, or rasa-rasa-ibha-bhū = 1866. That would give ŚS 1866/1886 (c. 1944/1964 CE), but these are speculative. The date is Mārgaśīrṣa śukla 12, a Saturday, and a correct year reading could be checked against it. The era word is 'śake'. It is taken here as Śaka, but in Nepalese usage 'śake' is sometimes used loosely.

notes: The catalogue gives 'Jayasiṃha Malla (mahāpātra)' as king. That is wrong: Jayasiṃhamalla(varman) is the mahāpātra who owns the book. title: Nepālarājavaṃśāvalī
subject: Itihāsa
colophon: jādṛśī (!) pustakaṃ dṛṣṭ[v]ā tādṛsī(!) liṣitaṃ mayā || yadi suddham asuddhaṃ vā mama doṣo na dīyate || śrīharinārāyana (fol. 51r9) saṃ 806 sāla jeyṣṭha vadi 12 thva kuhnu śrīnivāsa malladeva śrīyogndumalladeva śrīlalitapaṭṭanayā rājā, śrīpārthipendamalladeva, vañayā rājā śrīugramalladeva … saṃ 807 sāla māghaśukla11 roja6 thva kuhnu śrīśrīnivāsa mallarājā mṛtyu juva, sa tihma 9 vala parama sathasyaṃ cāhusa ye na julo || (fol. 51r5–51v11, I have to check it)
notes: 'śrīharinārāyana' comes straight after the scribal verse 'liṣitaṃ mayā … mama doṣo na dīyate'. It is most likely the scribe's signature, as the cataloguer assumes, but it could also be an invocation of Viṣṇu (Harinārāyaṇa), so confidence is medium. The following passage is in Newari. It gives two dated entries: 'saṃ 806 sāla jyeṣṭha vadi 12' (NS 806, about 1686 CE), which names Śrīnivāsa Malla, Yoganarendra Malla (king of Lalitapattana, i.e. Patan), Pārthivendra Malla and Ugra Malla; and 'saṃ 807 māgha śukla 11 roja 6' (NS 807, early 1687 CE), which records the death of Śrīnivāsa Malla. These read as historical memoranda added at the end of the chronicle, not as the copying date or as patrons of this copy. If the scribe wrote them as current events, the copy dates to about NS 806–807 (1686–87 CE), but this is not certain. The cataloguer says the folio range still needs checking. 'vañayā rājā' is probably a corruption of Newari 'yeñayā' (of Kathmandu). Pārthivendra Malla was king of Kathmandu at that time, so the epithet more likely belongs with him than with Ugra Malla. The royal names are not listed as persons because nothing ties them to the making of this copy.
review: Persons, roles, date and place are kept as in the first reading.
Notes expanded: the NS 806/807 entries are appended historical memoranda. If they are contemporary, they give c. 1686–87 CE as an approximate horizon for the copy. They are not a copying date.
Notes: 'vañayā' is probably a corruption of Newari 'yeñayā' (Kathmandu), and 'pārthipenda' is a corruption of Pārthivendra.

title: Adbhutasāgara
subject: Jyotiṣa
colophon: iti śrīmahārājādhirājaniḥśaṅkaśaṅka(4)raśrīmadvallālasenadevaviracite śrīadbhutasāgare gajadāntanirūpanaṃ || || ❁ || samvat 803 māghavadi, ṣaṣṭhī || śrīratnākareṇa likhitaṃ, adbhutasāgaram iti || || śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ (5) ❖ raṇe paryyaṭantaṃ jitāmitramallaṃ, nirīkṣyāribhūpāḥ kurupā babhūvuḥ | bhayabhrāntacittāḥ paritrāṇaheto,s tvadīyaṃ padāmbhojayugmaṃ praṇemuḥ || || śubhaṃ bhavatu || oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya || ○ || (6) thva kunhu śrīśrīsumatijayajitāmitramalladevasana, bhāgirāmapradhānāṅgayā velaśa adbhutasāgara cocakā, saṃpūrṇna yāṅā dina guro || || thva adbhutasāgala mahāyatnana dayakā , anaherā (7) yāyamateva, yatnapūrvvakana nidānayāya māla (fol. 189v3–7)
notes: The era is not named, but year 803 under Jitāmitra Malla of Bhaktapur (r. c. 1673–1696) fits NS, so NS 803 Māgha = c. January 1683 CE. The catalogue lists Bhāgirāma Pradhānāṅga as a scribe, but the colophon names only Ratnākara as scribe ('śrīratnākareṇa likhitaṃ'). The Nevārī says the king had the book written ('cocakā' = causative of 'co-', to write) 'bhāgirāmapradhānāṅgayā velaśa', i.e. in the time or under the supervision of Bhāgirāma Pradhānāṅga. 'Pradhānāṅga' is a ministerial title, so Bhāgirāma is taken as the minister in charge, possibly the overseer of the copying. No place is stated; Bhaktapur is likely because of the king, but this is not certain. The bhujaṅgaprayāta verse praising Jitāmitramalla is eulogistic and names no further persons. The final sentence is a request to others to look after the book carefully.

title: Mahābhārata
subject: Mahābhārata
colophon: iti śrīmahābhārate śatasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ vaiyāsikyāṃ śalyaparva samāpta[m] || || śrīkṛṣṇārpaṇam astu mārgaśīrṣe tathā kṛṣṇe jayo bde bhaumavāsare || likhitaṃ śalyaparva〈ṃ〉 ca bhīmenaiva mahāpuro(!) || 1 || || ❖ || saṃvat || 1788 || || (sa me yamāc ca) vadi || 7 || †pāyāṃ† śalyaparva〈ṃ〉 †samādā† || ||❁ || (fol. 33r2–4)
notes: The era is not stated. VS is assumed from 'saṃvat 1788' in a Devanagari MS, giving c. 1731 CE (NS 1788 is impossible). The verse names the year 'jaya' (Jaya saṃvatsara). In the southern 60-year cycle ŚS 1653 / VS 1788 is Virodhakṛt, not Jaya, so the year name may follow another reckoning, or year or name may be wrong; this has not been checked against tables. 'mahāpuro(!)' may be a corrupt locative 'mahāpure' (place of copying, unidentified) or simply 'mahāpuraḥ'. '(sa me yamāc ca)' before 'vadi' is unclear; it may be a garbled restatement of the month or year. '†pāyāṃ† śalyaparva †samādā†' probably means 'śalyaparva samāptam'.

title: Mantrarājasamuccaya
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: || iti śrīmat śrutismṛtimatapramāṇapārāvārapārīṇasarvataṃtradakṣiṇācārataṃtradhurīṇaśrīmaddakṣiṇāmūrtticaraṇāraviṃdamiliṃdena śrījayarāmabhaṭṭabhaṭṭātmajakāśīnāthena viracite maṃtrarājasamuccaye uttarārddhe paṃcaviṃśatimaḥ paṭalaḥ || 25 || || śrīdakṣiṇāmūrtticaraṇaṃ bhajet || || śrīsadāśiva kṣamasvaḥ (!) || śubhm || candrāṅke nandavarṣe nepāle pakṣa śukle tṛtīyāṃ parato maśleṣā yoga vajre āṣāḍhe saumyavāreṣu liṣidiṣva tathā śubhaṃ maṃtrarājam idaṃ sarvaṃ duttarāddhe miti śrutī || (!) ādarśeti mayaṃ divyaṃ pustakā (!) nāsti doṣadāḥ || śivaṃ śivamayaṃ devī mohano ropanī tathā tasmā (!) kṣamasva me hikyaṃ (!) likhitaḥ śubham (!) (fol. 164r2–5)
notes: The chronogram is candra (1), aṅka (9), nanda (9). Read right to left (aṅkānāṃ vāmato gatiḥ), it gives NS 991, i.e. 1871 CE. That matches the second value in the catalogue field. Nothing in the colophon supports the catalogue's alternative 'NS 884?'. 'nepāle' marks the era (Nepāla saṃvat), not the place of copying. The closing scribal verses are badly corrupt ('liṣidiṣva' = likhita?; 'likhitaḥ śubham'), and they name no scribe, commissioner or owner. Kāśīnātha, son of Jayarāma Bhaṭṭa, is the author of the Mantrarājasamuccaya, not a participant in this copy. 'śrīsadāśiva kṣamasva' and the apology to Śiva/Devī are invocations, not persons.
review: Added 'bhaṭṭa' to Kāśīnātha's titles: the compound 'jayarāmabhaṭṭabhaṭṭātmaja' calls him a Bhaṭṭa, the son of Jayarāma Bhaṭṭa.
Normalized the nakṣatra/yoga field to Āśleṣā (written 'maśleṣā', after the tithi 'parato') and yoga Vajra.
Glossed the weekday saumyavāra as Wednesday.
Expanded the notes: the chronogram check, the catalogue's 'NS 884?', 'nepāle' as the era marker rather than the copying place, and the scribe left unnamed.

title: Radhāvinodakāvya / ṭīkā
subject: Kāvya
colophon: iti rādhāvinodasaṭīkakāvyaṃ samāptim agamat rādhāvinodaṃ hi (3)varaṃ saṭīkaṃ tyaktaś ca hyunānayugaiḥ sa dhīmān || hitājñayā śrīghṛṇino gurur vai lulokanyugāthaḥ samāli(4) khadvai || 1 || ... (7) śake 1767 vaiśāṣe māsi aṣṭamyāṃ tithau śravaṇanakṣatre śubhe yoge bhaumāvāre (!) garuḍanārāyaṇād uttara(8)syāṃ diśi campākoṭākhya grāme vāgmatyāḥ samīpe vāsinā ābrahmaparyaṃta sadvaṃśotpannena lokanātha(9)sarmaṇā kovidālpena liṣitaṃ (!) yunā khalu --ṣoḍaśavarṣeṇa idaṃ pustakaṃ paṇḍitaśiromaṇibhir vaiyyākaraṇarūpaiḥ śodhanīyaṃ no vaiyyākaraṇapāśaiḥ śodhanīyam iti bhāvaḥ (fol. 9v2-4, 7-9)
purpose: Copied at the order of his guru (hitājñayā … guror); a request that learned grammarians correct it
notes: The verse is corrupt. 'hitājñayā śrīghṛṇino gurur vai lulokanyugāthaḥ samālikhadvai' probably stands for 'hitājñayā śrīghṛṇino guror vai lokanāthaḥ samālikhad vai': Lokanātha wrote it at the order of his guru, (Śrī) Ghṛṇin. The teacher's name is uncertain, since ghṛṇi- could also be a corrupt epithet. 'tyaktaś ca hyunānayugaiḥ' is unclear and may hide a further chronogram or the scribe's age. The scribe calls himself young and 16 years old (yunā … ṣoḍaśavarṣeṇa), 'kovidālpa', and born of a good lineage (ābrahmaparyanta sadvaṃśotpanna). The paksa is not stated. ŚS 1767 + 78 = c. 1845 CE (Vaiśākha falls in April–May 1845 if the year is expired). Caṃpākoṭa village lies north of Garuḍanārāyaṇa (Changu Narayan?) near the Bāgmatī. It is not securely identified, so it is left unnormalized.
review: Added p2 Ghṛṇin (teacher, low confidence) from the verse 'hitājñayā śrīghṛṇino gurur vai', read as 'guror'; added the relation p1 pupil_of p2
Normalized the month to Vaiśākha (written vaiśāṣe) and the weekday to Bhaumavāra (Tuesday)
Noted that the verse name 'lulokanyugāthaḥ' is a corruption of lokanāthaḥ, and that the year is presumably expired (gata) Śaka
Kept the scribe Lokanātha, the date ŚS 1767 = c. 1845 CE and the place

title: Svaratattvabodha
subject: Jyotiṣa
date_raw: abde gate śaranavācarake (!) vicitraṃ, vaiśākhamāsi dhavale girijātithau tat | vāre ravau

date.year: 795 (śara-nava-acara, read right to left; reading uncertain)

colophon: iti śrījīvanāthena viracitaṃ svaratattvodayaṃ (1) samāptam || || abde gate śaranavācarake (!) vicitraṃ, vaiśākhamāsi dhavale girijātithau (2) tat | vāre ravau pravaralokahitaṃ lilekha, śīghraṃ dvijo gaṇapatiḥ svaratattvabodhakam || || (fol. 13v8–13r2)
notes: The chronogram 'śaranavācarake (!)' is corrupt. Best reading: śara = 5, nava = 9, acara (= acala, 'immovable', i.e. the mountains) = 7. Read right to left this gives 795. The era is not named. In a Newari-script manuscript NS is most likely, which gives c. 1675 CE; if the year were VS 795 or ŚS 795 the date would be implausible. Girijātithi is taken as tṛtīyā (Gaurī's tithi), so Vaiśākha śukla 3 is Akṣayatṛtīyā. The verse is metrically loose. The colophon names the work Svaratattvodaya, while the scribe's verse calls it svaratattvabodhaka; the catalogue title follows the verse. The scribe Gaṇapati matches the catalogue field.
review: Date: resolved the chronogram 'śaranavācarake' as śara (5), nava (9), acara/acala (7). Read right to left this gives 795. Year field set to 795 with a query.
Date: era left as unspecified, but ce_approx set to 1675 (if NS 795). A three-digit year in a Newari-script manuscript points to Nepāla Saṃvat.
Date: tithi narrowed to tṛtīyā. Gaurī/Girijā's tithi is the 3rd (cf. Gaurītṛtīyā), so Vaiśākha śukla 3 is Akṣayatṛtīyā. The 8th is less likely.
Weekday normalized to Sunday (ravivāra).
Purpose rephrased: copied for the good of people (pravaralokahitam); it is not a merit-transfer formula.
Notes: added that the title in the colophon differs from the one in the verse.

subject: Jyotiṣa
colophon: iti (1) mahīntāpanīyasatpaṇḍitaśrīśrīnivāsaviracitāyāṃ śuddhidīpikāyāṃ yātrādhyāyonāmāṣtamo dhyāyaḥ || || (2) ❖ samvat 810 mārgaśiramāse śuklapakṣaḥ || dvādasyān tithau || aśvinanakṣatre (!) || variyānayoge || guruvāle (!) (3) || thva kuhnu maṇḍūyā liṣiti (!) bhavānisaṃkarena samāptayāṅā juro || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || śubhaḥ || (fol. 78r5–78v3)
notes: The Newari 'thva kuhnu maṇḍūyā liṣiti (likhita) bhavānisaṃkarena samāptayāṅā juro' reads as 'on this day Bhavānīśaṃkara completed Maṇḍū's writing'. 'Maṇḍūyā' looks like a genitive personal name. It could mean the copy was written for Maṇḍū, which would make Maṇḍū the owner or commissioner. It could instead mean Maṇḍū started the copy and Bhavānīśaṃkara finished it. It could also be a corruption. For these reasons Maṇḍū is entered with low confidence and the role 'other'. On the date: Mārgaśira śukla 12 of NS 810 falls in Nov/Dec 1689 CE. 'Aśvina' for the nakṣatra Aśvinī is marked (!). The moon in Aśvinī on Mārgaśira śukla 12 is a little early but possible (Bharaṇī/Kṛttikā is more usual). The date has not been verified. 'Mahīntāpanīya' describes the author as 'of Mahīntāpana'; the place has not been identified, and Śrīnivāsa is presumably a Maithil author.
review: ce_approx changed from 1690 to 1689: Mārgaśira falls early in NS 810, which began in Kārttika 1689, so the date is Nov/Dec 1689 CE.
Author's title changed from 'satpaṇḍita' to 'paṇḍita', because 'sat' is only a praising epithet.
Added Maṇḍū as a possible person (p3, low confidence, role 'other') from 'maṇḍūyā liṣiti'.
Notes expanded: the genitive reading, the nakṣatra plausibility, and the residence wording.

title: Saṃjñātantraprakāśikā
subject: Jyotiṣa
colophon: || iti śrīdaivajñadivākarātmajaviśvanāthadaivajñaviracite nīlakaṇṭhajyotiḥkṛta saṃjñātantre sahamādhyāyasya vyā(10)khyodāhṛtiḥ samāptā || || akāri viśvanāthena saṃjñātantraprakāśikā ṭikā tīkākṛtiṃ kuryāt sajjālajjāṃnubandhanam || 1 || candra(11)vāṇaśaravandra1551saṃmite hāyane nṛpatiśālivāhane | mārgaśīrṣasitapañcamītithau viśvanāthaviduṣā samāpitaṃ || 2 || || śrīśāke grahavaktraśambhuvadanādriglaumite śākake tvādyarthau madhumāsaśubhradalake vedhas tithau bhārgake || śrīgaurīśapure mude sukṛtināṃ śrīnīlakaṇṭhīṃ kṛtiṃ | śrīsodāhṛtikāṃbudho 'likhad imāṃ śrīlālaratnākaraḥ || 1 || (fol. 24r9–13)
purpose: mude sukṛtināṃ (for the delight of the virtuous)
notes:
The colophon contains two dates.
1. Composition of Viśvanātha's commentary: 'candravāṇaśaravandra' (read 'candra') = 1551 in Śālivāhana's era, i.e. ŚS 1551 (c. 1629 CE), Mārgaśīrṣa śukla 5.
2. Copying: the chronogram glau(1)–adri(7)–śambhuvadana(5)–graha(9), read right to left, gives ŚS 1759, Caitra (madhumāsa) śukla, Friday. That is c. March/April 1837 CE. 'vaktra' seems to double 'vadana' in the compound.

Other doubtful points:
- 'tvādyarthau' is unclear and may be corrupt.
- 'vedhas tithau' probably means the tithi ruled by Brahmā (pratipad), but this is uncertain.
- Gaurīśapura ('city of Śiva') is taken as Kāśī, following the catalogue.
- The scribe is written 'Lāla Ratnākara'; the catalogue gives 'Ratnākaralāla'. 'Lāla' is treated as an honorific or caste prefix.
- 'budho' may be an epithet of the scribe ('the learned one'); the phrase 'śrīsodāhṛtikāṃ budho' is garbled.
- Nīlakaṇṭha is the author of the root text (Saṃjñātantra, part of the Tājikanīlakaṇṭhī). Viśvanātha, son of Divākara, wrote the commentary (Prakāśikā / udāhṛti).
review: Scribe: name normalized to 'Ratnākara' with 'lāla' moved to titles (catalogue gives 'Ratnākaralāla'). 'budha' kept as an epithet, but its reading is uncertain.
Scribe: residence cleared. Gaurīśapura is stated only as the place of copying, not as where the scribe lived.
Date: tithi 'vedhas' glossed as probably pratipad (Brahmā's tithi), uncertain. Month glossed as Caitra and weekday as Friday.
Chronograms verified: ŚS 1759 for the copy (glau 1, adri 7, śambhuvadana 5, graha 9) and ŚS 1551 for the composition (candra 1, vāṇa 5, śara 5, (c)andra 1). ce_approx 1837 confirmed.

title: Samvatsaraphala
subject: Jyotiṣa
colophon: iti ṣaṣṭisaṃvatsaraphalaṃ samāpataḥ (!) || (fol. 39r2) … svasti sisāke 1482 saṃvat 1617 (8) samaya kārtikasūdi dvādasāṃ tithau || utrabhādravā nakṣatre … (9) mahibolasthāne vāstavya ||| sipāḍe kavara liṣitaṃ pustakaṃ || svasti sirājā indrase(10)ṇapāṭhārtho (!) liṣitaṃ || vivāha rocaya sarvagraṃtha ‥ bhāvasamucayapātha (!) samāpata (!) || … (fol. 39r7–10)
purpose: for the reading (pāṭhārtha) of Rājā Indrasena
notes: The colophon gives two dates, Śaka 1482 ('sisāke' = śrīśāke) and VS 1617 ('saṃvat'). They agree: both fall in 1560 CE (Kārttika śukla 12 ≈ Oct/Nov 1560). Kārttika śukla 12 with the moon in Uttarabhādrapadā is astronomically plausible. The scribe's name is unclear. 'sipāḍe kavara' could be a corruption of 'Pāṇḍe Kaṃvara/Kuṃvara', as the cataloguer suggests, or 'sipāḍe' could be an occupational title such as sipāhī ('soldier'). Mahibola is given as the scribe's place of residence (vāstavya). It is not explicitly the place of copying, and it has not been identified. Indrasena is presumably a Sena ruler (Makwanpur/Palpa line), but he is not identified beyond the colophon. The phrase 'vivāha rocaya sarvagraṃtha ‥ bhāvasamucayapātha samāpata' seems to refer to other texts in the same codex and contains no further persons.

notes: This is the colophon at the end of chapter 5 (sarga 5) and gives no scribe, date or place. The author's name is written 'śrīmanvādhavānandarāja', which most likely reads śrīman-mādhavānandarāja (v miswritten or misread for m). review: Notes refined: the corruption is most likely v for m (śrīman-vādhava- for śrīman-mādhava-); added that '-rāja' may be an honorific rather than part of the name.

notes: The scribe is not named; he refers to himself only as 'likhitaṃ mayā'. Year chronogram: 'khakhaḍāṣṭacaṃde' is probably a corruption of 'khaṣaḍaṣṭacandre' (kha 0, ṣaḍ 6, aṣṭa 8, candra 1). Read right to left this gives 1860, as in the catalogue. The era is not named: the colophon has only 'saṃvatsara'. VS is assumed (Devanagari, Nepal, catalogue 'SAM 1860'). On that basis Pauṣa kṛṣṇa falls around Dec 1803 or Jan 1804 CE. The tithi passage is daggered as corrupt ('ditije dretije dre'); it may be dvitīyā or tṛtīyā. notes: The colophon gives two eras: Śaka 1728 and saṃvat 1863 (Vikrama). They agree: 1728+78 = 1863−57 = 1806 CE. Jyeṣṭha śukla 12 falls around May–June 1806. notes: The era is not named ('saṃvat 802'). The Newari wording (kunhu, the instrumental -na) and the karmācārya scribe point to Nepāla saṃvat, which matches the catalogue. NS 802 + 880 gives 1682. However, the NS year begins with Kārttika śukla, so Kārttika śukla 14 of NS 802 falls in about October–November 1681 CE. 'riṣita (!)' is a corrupt spelling of likhita, and the Newari instrumental -na on nārāyaṇasiṃhana marks him as the scribe. 'saṃpūrṇṇa (!)' stands for saṃpūrṇa. The colophon names no weekday or place.

title: Śivagītā
subject: Vedānta
colophon: iti śrīpadmapurāṇe śivagītāsūpaniṣatsu brahmavidyāyāṃ (5) yogaśāstre śivarāmasaṃvāde sākalyādhyātmayogo nā (!) ṣoḍaśodhyāyaḥ (!) || 16 || śrīśāke (6)1754 śrīsaṃvat 1889 māsottame kauryyārkagatāṃśāḥ 23 śuklacaturddaśyāṃ gurudine || (7)likhitam ḍoṭyāṃ khatrivāḍikāyāṃ śrīlakṣamaṇamiśreṇa || || || || || (fol. 58r4–7)
notes: The colophon gives two eras, and they agree: ŚS 1754 + 78 = 1832 and VS 1889 − 57 = 1832 CE. 'kauryyārka' is a corruption of 'kaurpyārka', meaning the sun in Kaurpya (Vṛścika, Scorpio). 'gatāṃśāḥ 23' means 23 degrees (days) into solar Vṛścika, which falls around early December 1832. That fits a Mārgaśīrṣa śukla caturdaśī, but the date has not been checked exactly. 'lakṣamaṇa' is a scribal spelling of Lakṣmaṇa. Khatrivāḍikā (catalogue: khatrīvāḍikā) is a locality in Ḍoṭī, far-western Nepal; it is the place of copying, not stated as the scribe's residence.

title: Durgābhaktitaraṃgiṇī
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: || iti durggābhaktitaraṃgiṇyāṃ dvitīyaḥ prayoga(6)taraṃgaḥ || || samvat 771 jyeṣṭhaśukratrayodaśī svātinakṣatre parighayogaga (!) bṛhaspativāra (!) || thva kuhnu nhulacchayā balabhadrasiṃhana thva pustaka saṃpūrṇa yāṅā juroṃ || śubham astu || || iṣṭadevatā prasannam (!)astu || (fol. 66r5–6) <<after the colophon date is written in second hand>> 〈〈…〉〉 samvat 1016 miti māghavadi 14 thva kuhnu lāvicchayā †rarasaāṃ ya† ju va śaṃkāṃtiparvvakālasa iyācheyā śrīśaśidhararājajujuyātaṃ dāna viyā
purpose: later donation (dāna) to Śaśidhararāja at saṅkrānti, NS 1016
notes: The main colophon (NS 771 = c. 1651 CE) says Balabhadrasiṃha of Nhulaccha completed the copy. A later hand adds a donation note dated NS 1016 Māgha vadi 14 (= c. 1896 CE), on the occasion of a saṅkrānti. In it someone from Lāviccha, whose name is corrupt (†rarasaāṃ ya†), gave the book to Śaśidhararāja juju of Iyāche. The donor's name reading is very uncertain. 'ya ju va' may be part of a verb phrase and not part of the name.
review: p2 Śaśidhararāja: role changed from 'beneficiary' to 'owner'. He receives the book as a gift ('-yātaṃ dāna viyā'), so he becomes its later owner. This comes from the second-hand note of NS 1016.
Added p3: the donor from Lāviccha. The name is corrupt (†rarasaāṃ ya†), so confidence is low.
Added relation: donor p3 gave the book to p2.
Place emptied. Nhulaccha is given only as the scribe's residence ('nhulacchayā'), not as the place of copying; it stays in p1.residence.
Date for the main colophon confirmed (NS 771 = c. 1651 CE). Normalised nakshatra_yoga. Recorded the second-hand date NS 1016 (= 1896 CE) in notes.

title: Dakṣiṇakālyayutākṣarī-Ugracaṇḍāyutākṣarī-mantroddhāra
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: iti śrīvedasiddhāntatantre śrīdakṣIṇākālyāyutākṣarī (!) samāptā || || || || ❖ brahmavāhāhigatavarṣe āṣāḍhasya śucau ca pakṣe pūrṇātithau gurau ca vāre ayutārṇṇaṃ cākṛṣāt (!) tadā (exp. 72t3–72b2) iti śrīdurggāstiraharyyāṃ (!) mahātantre durggāsarvvasve khaḍgaprastāre saṃgrāmavijayamantroddhāre ugracaṇḍā-ayutākṣarī saṃpūrṇṇaṃ (!) || || ❖ samva[[t]] 888 āṣāḍhasu 3 śukravāra thva kuhnu saṃpūrṇṇaṃ || (exp. +10b: 3–5)
notes: The manuscript has two dated endings. (1) The Dakṣiṇakālī ayutākṣarī section has the chronogram 'brahmavāhāhigatavarṣe': brahma=1, vāha (the sun's horses)=7, ahi=8. Read right to left, this gives 871. The colophon names no era; the catalogue gives NS 871, about 1751 CE. The other date elements are Āṣāḍha śukla pūrṇimā, Guruvāra. The verse 'ayutārṇaṃ cākṛṣāt (!) tadā' records when the ayutākṣarī was extracted or copied, but no agent is named. (2) The Ugracaṇḍā ayutākṣarī section ends with NS 888 Āṣāḍha śukla 3, Śukravāra, about 1768 CE. This record uses that date as the main one. The 17-year gap may mean the 871 date was copied from the exemplar or belongs to the composition, not this copy. Neither colophon names a scribe, owner or any other person.
review: No substantive changes. Checked the chronogram brahma(1)-vāha(7)-ahi(8), read right to left, as 871. This matches the catalogue. Checked NS 888+880 = 1768 CE. Expanded the notes slightly.

notes: The colophon gives two eras. ŚS 1711 (+78 = 1789) and VS 1847 (−57 = 1790) are one year apart. The two can be reconciled if ŚS 1711 counts expired years and the date falls in Caitra at the end of that Śaka year (about March–April 1790). Depending on how the month and year are reckoned, it could also be 1789, so ce_approx 1790 is approximate. In '5 nakṣatre' the nakṣatra name seems to have been left out (or replaced by the numeral), so it is left blank. The scribe's name kaṃvalanañina is corrupt; read as Kamalanayana, matching the catalogue. 'brāhmaṇa' is treated as a caste title.
review: Scribe's name confidence lowered from high to medium: the form kaṃvalanañina is corrupt, and Kamalanayana (supported by the catalogue) is a reconstruction.
Notes expanded: the ŚS and VS years differ by one year; the nakṣatra name is missing after the numeral 5; and the misspelling kṛṣna for kṛṣṇa is recorded.

purpose: for installation in Hemarāja's own library, the Bhāratībhavana
notes: This is a modern copy made in VS 1982 (c. 1925–26 CE). It was copied from an old palm-leaf exemplar kept in the Nepal Royal Library ('nepālarājakīyapustakālayasthitaṃ'). That exemplar is dated NS 180 Māgha śukla 3 (c. 1060 CE) in the reign of Baladeva, so Baladeva is the king of the exemplar, not of this copy. The scribe says he collated other old palm-leaf manuscripts and corrected the text from their variant readings. The colophon also praises events of that year and the year before: Candraśaṃśera abolished slavery, freeing about 51,000 slaves with compensation paid to their owners; he received British, Chinese and French honours; a new Anglo-Nepalese treaty was made; and the roof of Paśupatinātha was regilded. Candraśaṃśera is spelled 'candraśaṃśerevarmaṇo' at the second mention. The closing phrase 'ekatamena bhaktaparamānunedam alekhi' (garbled; it ends 'this was written') is presumably by the scribe Pūrṇaprasāda. The catalogue lists Hemarāja as 'Donor'. The colophon makes him commissioner and owner, not donor.
review: Baladeva (p5): role changed from 'king' to 'other'. He reigned when the palm-leaf exemplar was copied in NS 180, not when this VS 1982 copy was made.
Notes corrected: 'nepālarājakīyapustakālayasthitaṃ' says the exemplar was kept in the Nepal Royal Library. It does not say the exemplar was copied there.
Purpose rewritten as a short English summary.
Added relation p2 servant_of p1 (prime minister under the king).
Hemarāja: the catalogue calls him 'Donor', but the colophon does not support this. He commissioned the copy for his own library, so he is kept as commissioner and owner, not donor.
Added the exemplar date and Candraśaṃśera's second spelling to the notes.

title: Kālikāpurāṇa
subject: Purāṇa
colophon: iti śrīkālikāpurāṇaṃ samāptaṃ || 88 || 89 || ❁ || kāle dyocāraṇavikalite, śuddhanepālaśāke, māghe māse śaśadharadine, kālikākhyaṃ purāṇaṃ | śrīpañcamyāṃ dharaṇi,vibudhaś cakrarājaḥ sudhīraḥ śukle pakṣe vividharacanaṃ lekhayāmāsa kena ||
notes: The year is written as a chronogram, 'kāle dyocāraṇavikalite', which is corrupt as quoted. The only clear element is dyo/dyu (sky = 0). I could not reconstruct 906 from it, so the year rests on the catalogue. 'śuddhanepālaśāke' means the era is Nepāla Saṃvat; the catalogue's 'ŚS ?' comes from the word 'śāke' and is wrong. NS 906 Māgha falls in Jan/Feb 1786 CE. I did not verify the weekday (Monday) against the tithi. The catalogue lists Cakrarāja as scribe, but 'lekhayāmāsa' is causative, so he is taken as commissioner. Newar verse colophons sometimes use lekhayāmāsa loosely, and the trailing 'kena' is odd (perhaps a corruption), so he may in fact be the scribe. 'dharaṇivibudha' (= bhūsura) marks him as a Brahmin; 'sudhīraḥ' is a plain epithet.

purpose: sattvārthahetunā (for the benefit of beings); copied with his own hand and owned by the scribe
notes: The catalogue lists 'King: Jayasiṃha Malla', but the colophon names no reigning king. Jayasīhamallavarman is a pradhānāṅga mahāpātra of the Hnolavihāra family and copied the manuscript himself (svahastena likṣitam). The catalogue seems to have mistaken this nobleman of Patan for a king. Jayasīha is read as Jayasiṃha. The vihāra name Mānīgalottaravihāra is written 'mānīgalottra-' and probably refers to a vihāra at Mangal Bazaar, Patan. NS 496 Māgha kṛṣṇa 5 falls in early 1376 CE; the weekday has not been checked. Hariścandra, Karṇa, Śibi, Jīmūtavāhana and others named in the closing verses are legendary figures and are not included as persons.

colophon: paṃcāgnyaśvaikasaṃyukte śāke śrīśivasannidhau | pakṣe durgāpriye bhaume caturthyāṃ divase (2) tithau || 1 || idaṃ vyutpattikāmena kāmadevātmajāgrajaḥ | śāstraṃ vāgīśvarīprītyai (3) vyalikhad ramaṇaḥ sudhīḥ || 2 || (fol. 11v1-3)
purpose: svārtha: copied out of a wish to learn the text (vyutpattikāmena), to please Vāgīśvarī
notes: The chronogram pañca(5)-agni(3)-aśva(7)-eka(1), read right to left, gives Śaka 1735, which is CE 1813/14. This matches the catalogue. Read literally, 'kāmadevātmajāgrajaḥ' means 'the elder brother of Kāmadeva's son'. This implies Ramaṇa is Kāmadeva's elder (probably eldest) son, with an unnamed younger brother. The son_of relation is inferred from this. 'pakṣe durgāpriye' ('in the fortnight dear to Durgā') probably means the bright half of Āśvina (Navarātri). If so, the date would be Āśvina śukla caturthī, a Tuesday, but the month is not stated, so the month field is left empty. 'śrīśivasannidhau' ('in the presence of Śiva') probably refers to a Śiva shrine, not a named locality, so it is not normalized. 'sudhīḥ' is an epithet ('learned'), not a formal title.

title: Ṣaṭpañcāsikāśloka
subject: Jyotiṣa
colophon: iti ṣaṭpaṃcāśikāyā(!) mī(!)śrakādhyāya (!) || || saṃvat 1917 sāla āsvi(!)kṛṣṇa aṣṭamyā (!) tithau āditya(!)śuṃ(!)nu bhāskaravāsare likhitam pratāpakeśaranātham(!) śubhm śubham astu śivāya namaḥ || || śivāya namaḥ || (fol. 17r5–17v5)
notes: The era is given only as 'saṃvat … sāla'. The year 1917 fits VS (= 1860 CE). With Śaka or Nepal Saṃvat it would be implausible, so VS is assumed. 'āditya(!)śuṃ(!)nu' probably stands for ādityasūnu, 'son of the Sun', i.e. Śani (Saturday). That contradicts the following 'bhāskaravāsare' (Sunday). The weekday is recorded as Sunday from the explicit vāra word, but the date is internally inconsistent or corrupt. The final '-nātha' of the scribe's name may point to a Nātha (yogi) affiliation, but that is not stated. The name is in the accusative form (-nātham(!)) where nominative or instrumental is expected.

notes: The catalogue records the date as NS 321, but the text reads 'samvatsaraśatatraya ekonaviṃśatyadhike' (300 + 19 = 319). The exact relationship between dvija Somadeva and Śirīka is maternal grandfather to daughter's son ('putrītanaya'). The prefix 'pathamodhara' before Somadeva might be an epithet (Prathamadhara/Prathamoddhāra) or a toponymic/family designation.

title: Bhāgavatapurāṇa (saṭīka): skandha 10
subject: Purāṇa

purpose: for the reading (pāṭhārtham) of Jīvanātha Upādhyāya
notes: 'baliāsasaṃ' is read as the Maithil mūla Baliāsa (Baliyāsa) plus the Panjī-style 'saṃ' marker. The catalogue field 'King: Donor Jīvanāthopādhyāya' is garbled. The colophon names no king, and Jīvanātha appears only as the person the copy was written for to read, not as a donor. The place name Korau..grāma has a lacuna and cannot be identified. review: Normalized paksa to 'śukla (śudi)' and weekday to 'Thursday (gurau)'.
Jīvanātha's affiliation now reads 'Baliāsa (Maithil mūla)'. The 'saṃ' after it is taken as the Panjī-style marker for a mūla-grāma, not as part of the name.
Notes now explain that the catalogue's 'King: Donor Jīvanāthopādhyāya' field is garbled. The colophon names no king and no donor.
Added a note that the 'san-' prefix in 'sanmiśra' is honorific sat-.
Owner role kept: it is inferred from 'pāṭhārthaṃ likhitam' (written for his reading).

title: Amarakoṣa
subject: Koṣa
colophon: padmāni bodhayaty arkkaḥ 〇 kāvyāni kaviḥ | tatsaurabhan nabhaścatuḥ(!) santas tanvanti tadguṇān || ○ || likhitam idaṃ pustakaṃ || || ❖ || udakānalacaurebhya muṣikebhyaś ca tathaiva ca | rakṣata〇vyaṃ prayatnena mayā kaṣṭeṇa likhitaṃ || ○ || likhita devajña śrīmantajīvacandreṇa svahastena || saṃ 412 bhāṣā (fol. 106v3–4)
notes: 'devajña' stands for daivajña. 'śrīmanta-' is taken as the honorific śrīmant- in compound with the name (śrīmant + Jīvacandra), not as part of the name; this matches the catalogue's 'Jīvacandra'. The era is not written but is taken as NS: this is a Newari-script manuscript and the catalogue also reads [NS] 412. The word 'bhāṣā' after the year is unclear. It may be the start of a month name or of a vernacular note that was cut off, or something left incomplete by the cataloguer. It cannot be read as any date element. Two stock verses come before the scribal line: 'padmāni bodhayaty arkaḥ…' and the 'udakānalacaurebhyo…' protection verse.
review: No substantive changes. Jīvacandra stays the scribe (svahastena), with the title daivajña (written 'devajña'). NS 412 + 880 = 1292 CE is correct. I expanded the notes on 'śrīmanta' and 'bhāṣā'.

title: Viśvaprakāśakoṣa
subject: Koṣa
colophon: iti sakalavaidyarājacakramuktāśekha[ra]sya gadyavidyānidheḥ śrīmaheśvarasya kṛtau viśvaprakāśābhidhāne nānārthaparicchedo dvitīyaḥ samāptaḥ || || rāmānalavyomarūpaiḥ śakakāle ’bhilakṣite | kośam viśvaprakāśākhyaṃ niramāt śrīmaheśvaraḥ || || saṃ 319 vaiśākha śuklacaturdasyāṃ likhitaṃ (fol. 82r3–5)
notes: The verse 'rāmānalavyomarūpaiḥ śakakāle' is a chronogram for the date Maheśvara composed the Viśvaprakāśa: Śaka 1033, c. 1111 CE. It does not date this copy. The copy is dated only 'saṃ 319' with no era named. Because the script is Maithili (Magadhi), this is taken as Lakṣmaṇa Saṃvat 319, c. 1438 CE, but that is an inference. If the era is Nepāla Saṃvat, the date is 1199 CE, which is also possible since it comes after the text was composed. The colophon names no scribe or commissioner; it says only 'likhitaṃ'.
review: Date era: 'saṃ 319' in a Maithili/Magadhi-script manuscript is most probably Lakṣmaṇa Saṃvat. Era set to LS and ce_approx to c. 1438; flagged as an inference in notes.
Maheśvara's titles: the epithets are now given in their attested forms ('sakalavaidyarājacakramuktāśekhara', 'gadyavidyānidhi') instead of a bare 'vaidyarāja'.
Chronogram checked: rāma 3, anala 3, vyoma 0, rūpa 1, read right to left = Śaka 1033 (c. 1111 CE). This is the date the text was composed, not the date of the copy. The note now says so explicitly.

title: Veṇīsaṃhāraṭippaṇī
subject: Nāṭaka
colophon: iti mahāmahopādhyāyadharmādhikaraṇikaśrījagaddharakṛtau veṇīsaṃhāraṭippaṇikāyāṃ ṣaṣṭho ṅkaḥ samāptaḥ || || śubham astu śrīr astu || || abde lakṣmaṇasenasa〇mmate(!) śatacatuṣṭaye caturvviṃśatau ca likhyamāne | pauṣe py asite pakṣe ’māvāsyānvite ravau likhitaiṣā prayatnena śrīrāmeṇa dvijātmanā || grāme kaṅkapure ramye śobhitopavane kila | tatra ⁅pratya⁆karo vipro jayadevaḥ kila sundaraḥ || || oṃ namaḥ śrīkṛṣṇāya || || || (fol. 66r3–5)
notes: The date is written out in words: śatacatuṣṭaye caturviṃśatau = 424 in the Lakṣmaṇasena era (LS). Using the LS+1119 conversion this is about 1543 CE, but the LS epoch is disputed, so the CE year is approximate. The catalogue's 'pauṣa 30' matches amāvāsyā (new-moon day) of the dark half. Jayadeva is a brahmin (vipra) of Kaṅkapura, the village where the copy was made. His role depends on the uncertain bracketed word ⁅pratya⁆karo. It could perhaps be a corrupt pratyakṣakara, 'one who examined/witnessed', or some patron-like function. Commissioner, owner or corrector cannot be confirmed, so he is entered as 'other'. dvijātmanā is read as 'by the twice-born (brahmin) Rāma'. It could also mean 'son of a brahmin', but no father is named.
review: No substantive changes. Notes now cover the uncertain bracketed word ⁅pratya⁆karo, the reading of dvijātmanā, and the date check.

colophon: ity āgenyapurāṇe rāmoktanītirājadharmma || saṃ 663 dvirāṣāḍhaśuklasaptamyāṃ hastājve(?) lekhi || || (fol. 10v7)
notes: The colophon names no persons. The era is not stated, but the Newari script and the catalogue's NS 663 make Nepāla Saṃvat near-certain: 663 + 880 = c. 1543 CE. 'dvirāṣāḍha' means the second, intercalary (adhika) Āṣāḍha. 'hastājve(?)' is uncertain. It probably stands for the Hasta nakṣatra (e.g. hastarkṣe); a split hastā + jye(ṣṭhā?) is less likely. 'āgenyapurāṇe' is a corruption of āgneyapurāṇe (Agnipurāṇa). The text is the Rāmokta nīti/rājadharma section. 'lekhi' records only that the copy was written, without naming the scribe.
review: Month normalized to 'Āṣāḍha (dvir-, i.e. second/intercalary Āṣāḍha)' rather than the raw form
Notes expanded: intercalary Āṣāḍha in NS 663, corrupt 'āgenyapurāṇe' for Āgneyapurāṇa, uncertain nakṣatra reading

date_raw: vāravyomograviṣvagvadanaparimite lakṣmaṇakṣoṇipālapravyaktābde valakṣe tava hara sutithau drāk tapasyasya rātrau
colophon: ity ārṣe rāmāyaṇe ādikāṇḍe ayodhyāvāsijanapramodaḥ || ādikāṇḍaṃ samāptaṃ || śubham astu || śrīr astu || ○ || vāravyomograviṣvagvadanaparimite lakṣmaṇakṣoṇipāla- pravyaktābde valakṣe tava hara sutithau drāk tapasyasya rātrau | śrīrāmasyaiva pādāmbujayugalamilanmaulir udyatsvakarppo vyālekhīd ādikāṇḍaṃ dhanapatiramaṇaṃ pāpahaṃ lekhakasya || śrutvaivaṃ prathamaṃ kāṇḍaṃ ++buddhyā samāhitaḥ | martyalokaṃ parityajya viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati | ādikāṇḍam imaṃ samyak yaḥ śṛṇoti sadāmaraḥ | āyuḥ kīrttir yyaśaś cāpi varddhate nātra saṃśayaḥ | śrutvā santatikāmaś ca bālakāṇḍaṃ idan naraḥ | aurasaṃ putram āpnoti nānāguṇasamanvitaṃ || || oṃ sakala­duḥṣ(!)kṛti­nivṛtti­duḥkṛtottha­samastāpac­chūnyatva­dāridry­ānutpattīṣṭa­viyoga­­rāhityaputra­pautrādi­vṛddhi­vividhotpātopagama­pūrvvakaihikasakala­saumanasyadhanadhānyasamṛddhitaduttaraviṣṇulokagamanakāmo dyādi yathākālaṃ vālmīkikṛtarāmāyaṇaśravaṇam ahaṅ kariṣye || || śubham astu || śrīr astu || śrī || oṃ namo mahāgaṇeśāya || śrīrāmāya namaḥ || || (141r3-141v4)
purpose: for the merit of the scribe (pāpahaṃ lekhakasya); the closing saṅkalpa is a formula for hearing the Rāmāyaṇa
notes: The era is the Lakṣmaṇasena era (lakṣmaṇakṣoṇipālapravyaktābde). Reading the chronogram from the right: vāra = 7 (units), vyoman = 0 (tens), ugra = Rudra = 11?, viṣvagvadana ('faces on all sides' = Brahmā) = 4?. A Rudra value of 11 does not give a plausible year. If ugra stands for a single digit, the year would be about LS 4x07 or x07; a value around LS 407 (≈1526 CE) would fit the usual range of LS dates, but this is conjectural, so ce_approx is left empty. The date falls on the śukla tithi sacred to Hara in Phālguna, at night. The scribe does not give his name; he describes himself as having his head at Rāma's lotus-feet ('udyatsvakarppo' is corrupt and may conceal a name or epithet). 'dhanapatiramaṇaṃ' qualifies the copied ādikāṇḍa as 'delighting Dhanapati' (a common Maithil name, possibly the patron), but it could also be a pun on Kubera; the person reading is low-confidence. The closing 'oṃ sakala… vālmīkikṛtarāmāyaṇaśravaṇam ahaṅ kariṣye' is a standard saṅkalpa for hearing the Rāmāyaṇa ('dyādi' is probably for 'adyādi'). It does not record who commissioned or owned this copy.
review: p2: the scribe is the unnamed nominative subject of vyālekhīt (…maulir udyatsvakarppo). 'dhanapatiramaṇaṃ' is accusative and agrees with ādikāṇḍaṃ, so it probably means 'delighting Dhanapati' and points to a Dhanapati, perhaps a patron, rather than naming the scribe. Changed the name to Dhanapati and the role to 'other'; confidence stays low.

date.month: Tapasya = Phālguna added.
date.tithi: Hara's tithi is probably caturdaśī (Śiva rules both the 8th and the 14th); marked as uncertain.
date.year: gave a digit analysis of the chronogram, which cannot be resolved as a straightforward number; ce_approx left empty.

title: Harivaṃśa
subject: Mahābhārata
colophon: ❖ sa śrīmān acaladbhavārṇṇavanavālaṃkāramukta (!) maṇiḥ śāntaḥ śaṅkarasiṃha ity avitathaṃ nāmāpi ramyaṃ vahan | yasyā − ⌣ lakūlamudrajayaśaḥ kṣīrād apūre raviḥ sadyājātasudhāṃśuvibhramamasaṃ bibhrad bhṛśaṃ śobhate || etasmād udagād agādh〇nidhibhūr ambhodhidhīr ā|| ❁ ||śayaḥ | śrīrāmārjunasiṃha ity atitarāṃ khyātāṃ sa〇mākhyāṃ (tāṃ dave tra |) yasyāgre gurutāṃ surāsuragurur manye na saṃprāptataḥ śaśvān nirmalacittadarpaṇatalonmīlan na [[..]] śrībhṛtaḥ || tasyāpatyam anantakāntimadhuro ma[[rttāsa]]varggo yamaḥ śrīmān la〇kṣmaṇasiṃha ity asunṛtāṃ yaṃ nāma karṇṇām pritaṃ | udgāḍha[[ā]]taruṇin nimohagahane prātyantaśantaśri〇yaḥ | śāstraṃ śrīharivaṃse (!) saṃjñakam idaṃ sa śraddhapālālikhat | yan nāṃno duritaprabhāṃ | hitakṛtām ekavyam avyeti (sa) tasyāvaśyam anaśvarā api bhṛśaṃ naśyanti pa.ā.a yāḥ | vaṃśa (!) ta〇sya harer udīrṇṇamanasaḥ | karṇṇāvataṃsaḥ satāṃm (!) uttaṃsaḥ kavikarmaṇāṃ | bhavatu vaḥ saṃkalpakalpa〈〈ka〉〉〇〈〈lpa〉〉drumaḥ | nayanagrahakaravarṣe | dvādaśyāṃ māghamāsi śuklāyāṃ bhūbhṛti caruṭadeve pravarddhamā⁅ne⁆ samāptam idaṃ || ❁ || (fol. 416r1-5)
notes: The date is expressed by the chronogram nayana-graha-kara = 292 (NS 292 = c. 1172 CE). The phrase 'sa śraddhapālālikhat' is metrically (Śārdūlavikrīḍita: – – ◡ – – ◡ –) and contextually a scribal error or misreading for 'sa śraddhayālīlikhat' ('he caused [the book] to be written with devotion/faith'); therefore Lakṣmaṇasiṃha is the commissioner and there is no scribe named Śraddhapāla. The royal name Caruṭadeva is unusual and unattested elsewhere; it may be a misreading or variant for Rudradeva (II), who was reigning in Nepal around NS 287–296.

title: Horāṣṭaka
subject: Jyotiṣa
colophon: iti yogacakrahorāṣṭakaṃ cchāyasāstra (!) 〇 samāpata (!) || ○ || samvat 538 vaiśākhaśuklapūrnnamāsyā (!) titho (!) | svātinakṣatre | vyatipātajoge (!) | budhavāsare | tadā dinalitasiddhaṃ (!) | sūdhaṃ vā masuvā (!) kṣemasi (!) śubhaṃ bhavatu sadām (!) astu śubha (!) || (fol. 8v1-4)
notes: The colophon names no persons: no scribe, commissioner or king. The era is not stated but is taken to be Nepāla Saṃvat, since the script is Newari and the catalogue gives NS 538. 538 + 880 gives c. 1418 CE (Vaiśākha pūrṇimā, so about April/May 1418). I have not verified the weekday, nakṣatra or yoga. 'yogacakrahorāṣṭakaṃ cchāyasāstra' should be read as Yogacakra-Horāṣṭaka, a chāyāśāstra. 'tadā dinalitasiddhaṃ' is probably a corruption of 'tadā dine likhitaṃ siddham' ('copying completed on that day'). 'sūdhaṃ vā masuvā kṣemasi' is a corrupt form of the usual 'śuddhaṃ vā aśuddhaṃ vā kṣantavyam' formula. It is not a personal name.
review: Normalized date fields: tithi 'pūrṇimā' (as written pūrnnamāsyā), weekday 'budha', nakshatra_yoga 'Svāti nakṣatra; Vyatīpāta yoga'.
Confirmed: no persons named; era NS 538 = c. 1418 CE (NS+880).
Notes expanded (text title chāyāśāstra, corrupt formulae).

title: Mudrārākṣasa
subject: Nāṭaka
colophon: audāryaṃ va〇casām apūrvvam aparā prauḍhiḥ prā/// racanā caitañ camatkāriṇīḥ || ❁ || anyā keyam ambu(mb)itārtha(!)ghaṭanā re⁅khā⁆madhuspa⁅kṣi⁆/// (77v1)bhoḥ || sauharddaṃ suhṛdā ripau kuṭilatā bhṛtyasya bhaktir dṛḍhā sācivya (!) sacive ⁅vidhe⁆r anuguṇan na /// triśaktiṣv api | kauṭilya(!)matau na ca prakaṭitaṃ kiṃ vāst〈〈a〉〉[[i]] 〇 nādya cchalāt || vaco ʼrthānāṃ citr⁅am vipulanayamārgge kha⁆/// lapitam ida (!) sādhyam avidi | ato rathyāvādaiḥ pra〇kaṭayata mā nāṭakam iti guṇeṣv eva prāyo vyabhicarati doṣaiḥ khalajana/// ❖ śreyo ʼstuḥ (!) || samvat 491 bhādrapadaśuklatṛtī〇yāyāṃ tithau hastanakṣatre śubhayoge bṛhaspativāsare || śrīmatpaśupa⁅ti⁆/// -ṇakamalaparāgapavītrīkṛtamaṇimukuṭaḥ sakala〇narendracakracūḍāmaṇicaraṇacumbitaripukulasūdanaravikuladīpaka/// kandarppapadm〈〈a〉〉[[i]]nīnāyakavirājamānaḥ rā(gh)abāndhayaparamopakārakaraṇa-samarthasakalaguṇādhivāsaṭoḍalamallavividhaviradāvalī/// (78r1)kṛtaḥ vīranārāyaṇetyādi || samastaprakriyāvirājamāṇa | rājādhirājaparameśva⁅ra⁆/// -nāṃ vijayarājye śrīnepālamaṇḍale || ○ || 〇 ādarśadoṣā mativi[[bhra]]mā/// -bhiḥ yatnena saṃsodhya pramādanīyaṃ || ○ || 〇 bālamūrkhavideśasthabā/// -sti kāriṇī || bhagn〈〈i〉〉[[a]]pṛṣṭikaṭīgrīvastabdhadṛṣṭir a〇dhomukham | (du)ḥkhe ++/// -re śrīmāṇīgalottaramahāvihāre śrīyokhācchevi〇hārādhivāsi/// -rthahetunā svahastena likhitam || sa eva mahāvihāre ⁅śrī⁆ (fol. 77r5-78r6)
purpose: Lost in a lacuna; only '…-rthahetunā' survives (perhaps svārtha- or dharmārtha-)
notes: The names of both the king and the scribe fall inside lacunae in the quoted colophon. Both are taken from the catalogue fields (probably from a fuller reading, e.g. Petech's), so their confidence is low. The royal praśasti (paśupaticaraṇakamala…, raghukuladīpaka, ṭoḍalamalla virudāvalī, vīranārāyaṇa) gives epithets, not separate persons. In 1371 the de facto ruler was Jayasthitimalla, and some of these virudas are associated with him. So it is possible that the lost name is not Jayārjunadeva, or that it is a joint reference ('-nāṃ' is an honorific or plural genitive). 'Māṇīgalottara mahāvihāra' points to Patan (Māṇīgala = the palace area of Patan). The catalogue's 'Galottara' is a truncation of this. The scribe's Yokhācche vihāra appears to be a branch vihāra under it. NS 491 + 880 = 1371 CE.
review: Added reigning king Jayārjunadeva (low confidence): his name is in the lacuna before '-nāṃ vijayarājye' and is taken from the catalogue field. It fits NS 491 = 1371 CE, which falls within his reign (c. 1361–1382).

Added scribe Gomendracandra (low confidence): the colophon has 'svahastena likhitam', but the name is in the lacuna after 'śrīyokhācchevihārādhivāsi'. The name is taken from the catalogue field. Residence recorded as Yokhācche vihāra.
Purpose: the bare fragment '-rthahetunā' replaced with a description saying the purpose is in a lacuna.
Notes expanded about the viruda string and the place name.

title: Tattvacintāmaṇyāloka; anumānakhaṇḍa
subject: Nyāya
colophon: iti mahāmahopādhyāyasanmiśraśrījayadevakṛtāv anumānālokaḥ saṃpūrṇaḥ || ○ || 〇 oṁ namo lambodarāya || ekadantāya namaḥ || dhūmrāya namaḥ || śubham astu || śrīr astu || ○ || śavāsane (!) sāyakasāvadhāne madhau dhunāne (!) sati pañcabāṇe | dalāni vāsāṃsi parityajantī latā na〇tāṅgī tarusaṅgatābhūt || ahaha likhāpanavṛtyā (!) bhṛtyāṇām bharaṇam asmākaṃ | samprati likhanāvṛttiṣ kāpi na śaktiḥ (kṣu)dhā mahatī || la saṁ 487 mārgaśuklapañcamyāṃ śukre vaiñāmagrāme mahosadupādhyāyaśrī(mādhī)..(śarmma)…. mudrām ekam (!) ādāya karaṇaśrīdevanāthena likhitvā dattam iti || ⁅lamboda⁆rāya namaḥ || śubham astu || (fol. 192r2-5)
purpose: paid copy: the scribe took one mudrā and handed the copy over to the upādhyāya (p3)
notes: The commissioner's name is damaged: the cataloguer reads (mādhī)..(śarmma) with further lacunae, and the case ending is lost. The reading 'mahosadupādhyāya' is probably 'mahāsadupādhyāya'. The commissioner role is inferred from the payment of one mudrā plus 'likhitvā dattam'. ce_approx uses the LS+1119 convention; other conversions (+1107/1108) would give about 1594/95, and the weekday was not checked. The first verse (śavāsane… latā… tarusaṅgatābhūt) is a stock spring verse. The second verse ('ahaha likhāpanavṛtyā…') is the scribe complaining that he supports his dependants by copying, has no other living, and is very hungry. Karaṇa marks the scribe as a Maithil kāyastha. The author is Jayadeva (Pakṣadhara) Miśra, who wrote the Āloka.
review: p3: removed the brahmin suffix śarman from the name (now 'Mādhī[..]') and moved it to titles. Normalized the title 'mahosadupādhyāya' to 'mahāsadupādhyāya' (written mahosadupādhyāya) instead of listing both sadupādhyāya and upādhyāya. Lowered confidence to low because the name is mostly lost.
p3 role: kept as commissioner, but noted that the colophon only implies it: the scribe 'took one mudrā' and handed over the copy, and the case ending of p3's name is lost.
Purpose rephrased as a paid copy made for p3.
Notes: added the era conversion caveat and described the two verses more accurately.

colophon: iti śrīgovindabhagavatpādapūjyaśiṣyasya paramahaṃsaparivrājakācāryaśrīśaṅkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau bhagavadgītābhāṣye ṣṭādaśādhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || || ṣaṭśatāni saviṃśāni ślokānām āha keśavaḥ | arjjunaḥ saptapañcāśat saptaṣaṣṭiṃ ca saṃjayaḥ || dhṛtarāṣtaḥ ślokam ekaṃ gītāyā mānam ucyate || || śubham astu || lasaṃ 422 bhādraśudi 7 śanau edine nepāladeśāntagatakāṣṭhamaṇḍapanagare (āsanamaṇḍala)grāme nirupadhiparopakārarasikajyotiṣavaidyakasmṛtipurāṇakāvyaalaṅkārabahuvidhavidyānidhānamahārājādhirājaśrīamaramalladevasya pradhānamantriśrījñāna.. ..syājñayā rājñā pārśve mahābhārataṃ paṭhatā likhitaṃ śrīmukundapāṭhakaśarmmabhir iti || gītā sugītā karttavyā kim anyaiḥ śāstravistaraiḥ | yā svayaṃ padmanābhasya mukhapadmād viniḥsṛtā || purāṇe bhārataṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bhīṣmaparvva tato pi ca | tatrāpi bhagavadgītā tarāpi ca śanaiḥ śanaiḥ || gītāviduravākyāni dharmmāḥ śantanaveritāḥ | yair nna śrutaṃ mahārāja teṣāṃ janma nirarthakaṃ oṃ namo bhagavate paramakāruṇikāya || oṃ naranārāyaṇābhyāṃ namaḥ || (fol. 132r5–9)
purpose: rājñā pārśve mahābhārataṃ paṭhatā (written while reading the Mahābhārata near the king by order of the prime minister)
notes: The name of the prime minister is partially broken (Jñāna.. ..). The catalogue incorrectly notes 'bhādrabadi 7' whereas the text clearly reads 'bhādraśudi 7'.

title: Bhagavadgītāśāṅkarabhāṣya
subject: Vedānta
colophon: iti śrīgovindabhagavatpādapūjyaśiṣyasya paramahaṃsaparivrājakācāryaśrīśaṅkarabhagavataḥ kṛ〇tau bhaga(vadgītā)bhāṣye ṣṭādaśo dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || || ṣaṭśatāni saviṃśāni ślokānām āha keśavaḥ | arjjunaḥ saptapañcāśat saptaṣaṣṭiṃ ca saṃjayaḥ || dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ ślokam ekaṃ gītāyā māna〇m ucyate || || śubham astu || la saṃ 422 bhādraśudi 7 śanau e dine nepāladeśānta(re) kāṣṭhamaṇḍape nagare a….(maṇḍaṇa)grāmanirupadhiparopakārarasikajy〈〈e〉〉[[o]]tiṣavaidyakasmṛti-purāṇakāvya-alaṅkārabahuvidhavidyānidhānamahārājādhirājaśra(!)śrī-amaramandadevasya pradhānaśrī..mijana(mobha)syājñayā rājñā pārśve mahābhāratapaṭhatā likhitaṃ śrīmukundapāṭhakaśarmmabhir iti gītāsu gītā karttavyā kim anyaiḥ śāstravistaraiḥ | yā ceyaṃ padmanābhasya mukhapadmād viniḥsṛtā || purāṇe bhārataṃ śastaṃ bhīṣmaparvva ..te ..(ta) | tatrāpi bhagavadgītā tatrāpi ca śanaiḥ śanaiḥ || gītāviduravākyāni dharmmāḥ śāntanaveribhāḥ (!) | yair nna śrutaṃ mahārāja teṣāṃ janma nirarthakaṃ || oṁ namo bhagavate paramakāruṇikāya || oṁ naranārāyaṇāya namaḥ || (fol. 133r5-9)
purpose: copied by order (ājñayā) of the pradhāna ..mijana(mobha)
notes: The king's name 'amaramandadeva' is most likely a corruption of Amaramalladeva, the Malla king of Kathmandu (c. 1529–1560 CE). This fits LS 422 = c. 1541 CE and copying at Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa. The long compound 'a….(maṇḍaṇa)grāma…vidyānidhāna' is a string of epithets for the king. The pradhāna's name is badly damaged ('..mijana(mobha)'). The reading is uncertain and is not normalised. Mukunda Pāṭhaka is described as 'reciting the Mahābhārata at the king's side' (rājñā pārśve mahābhāratapaṭhatā), i.e. a court reciter. That is his office, not a reader role for this copy. The colophon gives only the Lakṣmaṇasena era, LS 422 (+1119 = 1541 CE), so there is no second era to conflict with it. Govinda is listed only to identify the commentator Śaṅkara. Script: Maithili / Newari.
review: p1 Govinda(bhagavatpāda): role 'teacher' changed to 'other'. He is the teacher of the author Śaṅkara, not a teacher connected with this copy. Name normalised to 'Govinda', with 'bhagavatpāda' kept as an honorific title.

p3 king: the name is read as Amaramalladeva, taking 'amaramanda' as a corruption of 'amaramalla'. Confidence lowered to medium. The residence was removed because Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa is the place of copying, not a stated residence of the king. The added evidence quotes the king's epithets.
p4 pradhāna: added relation servant_of p3, since he is the king's pradhāna.
p5 Mukunda: no 'reader' role added. Mahābhārata recitation at the king's side is his office, not a reading of this copy. This is recorded in notes.
The purpose field was reworded in English.
Notes expanded: the king's identification, the corrupt minister's name, and the date check.

title: Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā
subject: Bauddha darśana
date_raw: 17?, i.e. the year 17 of King Madanapāla's rule (somewhere in the modern Bengal, corresponding roughly to A.D. 1159?)
colophon: samāptā ceyam bhagavaty āryāṣṭasahasrikā (!) prajñāpāramitā sarvvatathāgatajananī sarvvabodhi〇satvapratyekaj〈〈a〉〉[[i]]naśrāvakāṇa[[ā]]〇ñ ca mātā dharmmamu|| ||drā | dharmmolkā dharmmanābhir ddharmabherī dharmmanetrī | dharmmaratnanidhānam akṣayo dharmmakośo dharmmāci〇ntyādbhutadarśananakṣatramā〇lā sarvvasukhahetur iti sadevamānuṣāsura-gandharvvalokavanditā prajñāpāramitā samyag udgṛhya paryavāpya ca dhārayitvā pravartyai〇nāṃ viharantu sadārthina i〇ti || ye dharmmā hetuprabhavā hetus teṣān tathāgato hy avadat | teṣāñ ca yo nirodha evamvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ || deyadharmmo yaṃ pravaramahāyānayāyinaḥ paramopāsakaśausādhuśrīyamāricandrasya yad atra puṇyan tad bhavatv ācāryopādhyāyamātāpitṛpū(fol. 282v1)rvvaṅgamaṃ (kṛ)tvā sakalasatvarāśer anuttarajñānaphalāvāptaya iti || parameśvaraparamabhaṭṭārakaparamasaugatamahārājādhirājaśrīmanmadana-pāladevapādīyapravarddhamānavijayarājye abhilikhyamāne (yatrāddhonā)…….. (sūryamatyā) jyeṣṭhadine 17 || śrīsantoṣanagaravāstavyaśaulekha〇kamahīpatidattena likhiteyaṃ āryāṣṭasahasrikā (!) bhagavatī pra〇jñāpāramitā || ❖ namo buddhāya namo dharmmāya | namaḥ saṃghāya || (fol. 282r2-282v2)
notes: Santoṣanagara was a known settlement in the Pāla territory (Bengal/Bihar). The date is given in the regnal years of King Madanapāla Deva of the Pāla dynasty.

notes: No individual person (scribe, donor, or king) is named in the colophon; only the date of copying and a general dedication to all sentient beings are recorded.

title: Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā
subject: Bauddha darśana
colophon: lokaṃ prāpayituṃ sukhena padavīṃ samyak tvayā vāhinī (!) kāruṇyāhitace〇tāsā (!) bhagavatā buddhena saṃdīpitāṃ | śrutvā te ʼkhila dharmatatvanilayaṃ sūtraṃ samādhā〇nato gatvā sthā|| ||nam aharniśan ni(jam ala)ṃ dhyāyaṃtu (ye ʼbhyāgatāḥ ||) (fol. 205r1) −− − ⌣⌣−⌣−⌣⌣⌣− −− ⌣ −− (gate) nānābhedam anekapustakagatan dṛṣṭādhunā śraddhayā | kupyadvādigajendra〇kumbhadalane bhadreṇa yā śodhitā lokā〇rthaṃ hariṇā mayā suvihitais seyaṃ budhai〇r gahyatām (!) || || samāptā ceya(ṃ) bhagavaty āryāṣṭa⁅sa⁆hasrikā prajñāpāramitā || || ⁅sarvvatathāgata⁆jananī sarvvabodhisatvapratyekajinaśrāvakāṇāṃ mātā sarvamudrā dharmolkā dharmanābhir ddharmabherī 〇 dharmanetrī dharma-(ratna)nidhānam akṣayo dharmakośo dharmo cintyādbhutadarśananakṣa〇tramālā sadevamānusagandharvalokavanditā sarvasatvahetur iti || || ye ⁅dharmā⁆ hetuprabhavā hetus te (!) tathāgato hy avadat teṣāñ ca yo nirodha evaṃvāṃdī (!) mahāśravamaṇaḥ (!) || || deyadharmo yaṃ pravaramahā⁅yā⁆〇nayāyinaḥ || śrīlalitkrame śrīnoglake dhivāsina (!) | somalacchibhārīnāmna (!) 〇 yad atra puṇyaṃ sadbhavatvācāryopādhyāyamātāpitṛpūrvaṅgamaṃ kṛtvā sakalasatvarāśer anuttarajñānaphalāvāptayed iti || || samvat ā cū 2 vaiśākyasuklapaurṇṇamasyāṃ ādityadine 〇 śrīparameśvaraparamabhaṭṭārakamahārājādhirājaparamaśaivaśrī- āna〇ndadevapravarddhamānavijayarājy(e) likṣitam (!) iti || || (fol. 204v6-205r)
purpose: Merit transfer: the merit goes to the donor's ācārya, upādhyāya and parents first, then to all beings, so that they may attain supreme knowledge (sakalasatvarāśer anuttarajñānaphalāvāptaye).
notes: Year in Newari letter numerals: ā = 200, cū = 70, 2 = 2, giving NS 272 (Vaiśākha 1152 CE). This falls within the reign of Ānandadeva (c. NS 263–287). The catalogue lists Somalacchibhārī as the scribe, but the colophon presents them only as the donor (deyadharma). The verb 'likṣitam' has no named agent, so the scribe is unknown. The catalogue's place of copying, Lalitakramā (Nogala), is taken from the donor's residence ('śrīlalitkrame śrīnoglake adhivāsin'). That means Patan, Noglaka quarter, which is likely but not explicitly the place of copying. 'Somalacchi' may stand for Somalakṣmī. The verse naming Haribhadra is his recension verse, transmitted with the text, and does not concern this copy.
review: p1 Somalacchi: removed role 'commissioner'. The colophon gives only the deyadharma (donor) formula and no likhāpitam or similar verb.
p1: 'pravaramahāyānayāyin' is a Mahāyāna epithet, not an institutional affiliation. Affiliation is now 'Mahāyāna'. The title 'bhārī' is normalised to 'bhāro (bhārī)'.
p1 residence normalised to Lalitakrama (Patan), Noglaka quarter.

p3 Haribhadra: dropped role 'author'. He did not write the Aṣṭasāhasrikā. The appended verse is his statement as the reviser and commentator of the text, so the role is 'commentator' only, at medium confidence.
place: the colophon gives Lalitakrama/Noglaka as the donor's residence ('adhivāsin'), not explicitly as the place of copying. The field is now empty and the point is explained in the notes.
date: month, tithi and weekday normalised (Vaiśākha, pūrṇimā, Sunday). Reading NS 272 = 1152 CE confirmed.
purpose rewritten as a merit-transfer formula.

title: Kularatnodyota
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: iti śrīmadādidevād vinirggate paṃcāśatkoṭivistīrṇṇāt śrīmatkubjimahāmatottame śrīmatkularatnodyote prayāgādicakrapūjāpratiśṭhānānākarmmakaraṇakarmmāraṃbhācāryābhiṣekayoginā mateṣṭi.................. paṭalaḥ || ❁ || śrīma(tkulāgamaṃ) hy etat paścimāmnāyasaṃbhavam | sūcakaṃ sarvvamārggāṇāṃ bhaviṣyavi(dhinā) sphuṭam || ❁ || pakṣe śite cāśvinamāsa....................(nvite hni |) śrīharṣadevasya .......................... prajānām || ❁ || nepāladeśaṃ samupāgatena kāṣṭhābhidhe maṃḍape saṃsthitena | svaśiṣyavarggasya viśodhanāya paropakārāya kṛtaprayatnaḥ | .... svayaṃ śrīkularatnapūj(ya)m uptatam etadbṛhadāgamedam | śrīma..................kenāpi saṃlekhi ca paṃḍitena || ❁ || samāptam i〇daṃ kularatnodyotam iti || || ○ || saṃkhyā sahasradvitayaṃ ca sārddhaṃ siddhyākaraṃ śrīkularatnadīpaṃ | śrīmatparākhyena vidhī (not clear) m iti || ○ || || ○ || naṃdantu kulayoginyo naṃdaṃtu kulaputrakāḥ | naṃdaṃtu śrīkulācāryā ye cānye kuladīkṣitāḥ || ❁ || || iti śubham astu || ○ || || (fol. 72r6–v4)
purpose: for correcting the copies of his own disciples (svaśiṣyavarggasya viśodhanāya) and for the benefit of others (paropakārāya)
notes: The year and tithi are lost in a lacuna. Only the bright fortnight of Āśvina and the reign of Harṣadeva survive, so the CE date can only be placed within his reign (c. 1085–1098). This fits the catalogue's 'early 12th century' only loosely; late 11th century is more likely. The scribe's name is broken: 'śrīma…ka'. 'Śrīma' may be the honorific śrīmat- rather than part of the name. The scribe is described as having come to Nepal and as living at Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa, so he was probably a foreign paṇḍita. 'svayaṃ … uptatam' is probably a corruption of 'udyatam'. The phrase 'śrīmatparākhyena vidhī (not clear)' in the verse giving the extent (2,500 ślokas) is unclear. It may name someone connected with the text, possibly its author, but it is too damaged to identify, so no one was extracted from it.
review: p2: added residence (Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa, having come to Nepāladeśa from elsewhere), since the instrumentals samupāgatena / saṃsthitena / …kenāpi / paṃḍitena all refer to the same person
p2: evidence shortened to the key clause; name kept as fragment '[...]ka', with a note that 'śrīma' may be the honorific śrīmat- rather than part of the name
date.ce_approx: changed from the single year 1090 to the reign range c. 1085–1098
purpose rephrased; place evidence trimmed
notes: added the unclear 'śrīmatparākhyena' phrase and the lacunae in the dating verse

title: Uttaraṣaṭkaṭīkā
subject: Tantra
colophon: iti śrīkubjikāmate dvādasasahasrikā tṛpurāyoga dvātriṃśatipaṭalaḥ samāptaḥ || ❁ || subha śrīmahālakṣmī māṃgalyaṃ || ❁ || samvat ā 7 śrāvanakṛṣṇadasaṃmyāṃ sukradine | śṛīpannugaviṣayādhipatiśrīmahāsāmantaraphasadīvavijayarājeḥ | yupaṭolakādhivāsino | śrīkulaputra〈〈sya〉〉phulananāyakasya pustaka ddarmārthena li[khi]taḥ naiṣṭikatejādītalikhita || uddakānalacorebhyo mūśikānyaṃ tathaiva ca rakhitavyaṃ pra +++ mahākaṣṭe〈〈|〉〉na likhitam iti || ❁ || śubha śrīmahālakṣmī māṃgalyaṃ || (fol. 22r1–5)
purpose: dharmārtha (for merit), for the owner Phulana(nāyaka)
notes: The year 'ā 7' uses letter-numerals. I follow the cataloguer's NS 207 (= 1087 CE). I have not verified this independently. Era 'samvat' is unspecified but the letter-numerals point to NS. The place of copying is not stated. Yupaṭolaka is where the owner lives, and Pannugaviṣaya is the district governed by the mahāsāmanta. Identifying Pannugaviṣaya with Panauti is possible but unproven. 'nāyaka' in Phulananāyaka may be part of the name and not a title. It is not stated that he commissioned the copy, but this is implied ('his book, written for merit'). The catalogue calls him donor, but the colophon has no donation formula. Raphasadīva/Raphasadeva is a mahāsāmanta, a feudatory ruler of a district, not a king: 'vijayarāje' marks his rule. The names Tejādīta and Raphasadīva are likely misspellings of -āditya and -deva. The colophon ending names Kubjikāmata (dvādaśasāhasrikā), chapter 32 'tripurāyoga', which does not match the catalogue title Uttaraṣaṭkaṭīkā.
review: p2: removed 'commissioner' — the colophon only says the book is his ('phulananāyakasya pustaka'), with no likhāpitam or similar. Roles are now owner only; the inferred commissioning is mentioned in notes.
p2: name split into 'Phulana' with 'nāyaka' moved to titles (headman title), confidence lowered to medium; residence corrected to Yupaṭola(ka) per 'yupaṭolakādhivāsino'.

p1: name normalized to Raphasadeva (dīva = deva, kept as part of the regnal name); residence emptied — he rules Pannugaviṣaya, but the colophon does not say where he lives; the viṣaya is kept in titles.
p3: name read as Tejāditya (dīta = ditya), confidence medium; naiṣṭika (= naiṣṭhika) kept as title.
place: normalized 'Panauti' removed as uncertain; the place of copying is not explicitly stated (Yupaṭola is the owner's residence).
purpose normalized to dharmārtha.
notes expanded: letter-numeral year, Kubjikāmata colophon vs catalogue title.

title: Kulālikāmnāyatantra
subject: Śaktitantra
colophon: iti kulālikāmnāye śrīkubjikāmate samasta[sa]dbhāvabodhakanirddeso nāma pañcaviṃsatipaṭalaḥ || || iti caturviṃsatisāhasre sārāt sāraṃtaraṃ(!) śrīkubjikāmnāye śrīuḍiyāpīṭhavinirgataṃ pañcaviṃśapaṭalaḥ | sārddha trīṇi sahasraḥ śrīmataparisamāptilikhitam || ○ || ye śrīmatamārgam apratipadi prayacchanti ye mama prati teṣāṃ mahābhairavīgaṇaṃ guṇā prayacchanti mahojasāntam || ○ || rājādhirājaparameśvaraparamabhaṭṭārikamahārājādhirājaḥ śrīśrīanantamalladevasya vijarājye|| yoyakāgrahādhivāsinā || devajña| jotasomadattasya likhitam iti || śriyo ’stu samvat 416 caitraśukladittīyāyāṃ titho || || ❁ || || (fol. 194v4–195v2)
notes: 'devajña' is a corrupt form of daivajña. 'jota' is unclear. It may be a vernacular title (jośī / jyotiṣa, which would fit daivajña) or part of the name (Jyotisomadatta?). The catalogue gives the name as Somadatta. The 'yoyakāgrahādhivāsinā' (instrumental) does not agree grammatically with 'somadattasya' (genitive), but both clearly refer to the scribe. Yoyakāgraha is given as his residence ('agraha' possibly = agrahāra). It is not stated as the place of copying; the catalogue's 'Yoyakāgṛha' is taken from this phrase. 'paramabhaṭṭārika' is read as paramabhaṭṭāraka. The colophon also states the text length as 3500 (ślokas) and the chapter as 25th paṭala. NS 416 = 1296 CE, which fits Anantamalla's reign.
review: p2 (Somadatta): confidence lowered to medium, because 'jota' could be a title (jośī / jyotiṣa) or part of the name (e.g. Jyotisomadatta).
p2 residence written as 'yoyakāgraha' (from yoyakāgrahādhivāsinā); added a note that 'agraha' may stand for agrahāra.
Place: added a note that the colophon gives Yoyakāgraha as the scribe's residence, not explicitly as the place of copying.
Date checked: NS 416 + 880 = 1296 CE. Caitra falls in spring 1296, within Anantamalla's reign (c. 1274–1310). No change.

title: Niśvāsamahātantrāntargata-Pratiśṭhātantra
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: iti niśvāsā〇khye mahātantre prati[ṣṭhā]tantraṃ parisamāptaṃ || || aśītiyukte saśate sa[mva]tsare site subhe māghatṛtīyavāsare | nṛpānvaye śrībalade[va]rājake tri+++duḥkhavināśahetoḥ nirbhya (!) mayā likhitam eva sumaṅgalārtham (fol. 121r4–5)
purpose: tri+++duḥkhavināśahetoḥ ... sumaṅgalārtham (to destroy the [three kinds of] suffering; for auspiciousness)
notes: The colophon gives the year in words, 'aśītiyukte saśate' (100 + 80 = 180), but names no era. NS is inferred because Baladeva of Nepal reigned in the mid-11th century, which fits NS 180 (= 1059/60 CE) and agrees with the catalogue. The scribe is unnamed and appears only as 'mayā'. The word before it, 'nirbhya (!)', is corrupt (perhaps 'nirbhayaṃ' or similar) and is unlikely to be a personal name. The lacuna 'tri+++' probably held tri[vidha] or similar ('three kinds of suffering'). 'subhe' stands for śubhe, and 'site' means the bright fortnight (śukla).
review: Baladeva: affiliation 'nṛpānvaye' removed — the word means 'in the royal line' and is not a vihāra, guṭhi or lineage affiliation.

Date: the colophon itself names no era. NS is inferred from the reign of Baladeva, and the notes now say so. Year 180 (aśīti + śata) and ce_approx 1060 (Māgha NS 180 falls in early 1060 CE) are confirmed.
Notes: 'vāsare' here means 'on the day' (the tithi), not a weekday. The weekday is left empty.

title: Puraścaraṇacandrikā
subject: Tāntrikakarmakāṇḍa
date_raw: nepālahāyanagate viyadagnivāhe, māse ’site nabhasi sattithivahnidaive | gīrvāṇapūjitadine vasubhe
colophon: iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryaśrīvibudhendrāśramapūjya〈〈ṃ〉〉pādaśiṣyaśrīdevendrāśramakṛtā puraścaraṇacandrikā sampūrṇṇā || || nepālahāyanagate viyadagnivāhe, māse ’site nabhasi sattithivahnidaive | gīrvāṇapūjitadine vasubhe ca saṃgaṃ, jātaṃ puraścaraṇacandramarīcisāraṃ || (śrīmacchrī) .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. (sāgaraḥ | ) sajjīkṛtaḥ svapāṭhārthaṃ, puraścaraṇacandrikāṃ || daivajñanārāyaṇasiṃhena likhitam idaṃ || (fol. 69v3–5)
purpose: svapāṭhārtham: prepared for the study of [...]sāgara
notes: I read the chronogram viyat (0), agni (3), vāha (7, the horses of the sun) right to left, giving NS 730, about 1610 CE. If vāha is taken as 4, the year would be NS 430 (1310 CE), which is unlikely for this text. Vahnidaiva tithi is read as pratipad, whose presiding deity is Agni. Gīrvāṇapūjita is read as Bṛhaspati, giving Thursday. Vasubha is read as Dhaniṣṭhā, the nakṣatra of the Vasus. These identifications have not been checked against an ephemeris. The name of the person who had the copy prepared for his own study is lost in a lacuna; only '...sāgaraḥ' survives, probably preceded by 'śrīmacchrī'. The reading 'saṃgaṃ' may be corrupt (perhaps 'saṃjñe'). Vibudhendrāśrama is the guru of the author Devendrāśrama and is not connected with this copy.
review: Chronogram resolved: viyat=0, agni=3, vāha (horses of the sun)=7, read right to left = NS 730; ce_approx 1610 added; year field given as 730

Tithi interpreted: vahnidaiva (tithi presided over by Agni) = pratipad; weekday gīrvāṇapūjita(-dina) = Thursday (Bṛhaspati, revered by the gods); nakṣatra vasubha = Dhaniṣṭhā; month nabhas = Śrāvaṇa; pakṣa asita = kṛṣṇa
Vibudhendrāśrama: role changed from 'teacher' to 'other'. He is the author's guru and is not connected with this copy
Notes updated

colophon: i〇ti vidyāpīthibrahmajāmale, yoginīvijayaṃ, māhākālaproktā mahāśāntikādhyāyaṃ samāpta || śubham astu | sarvvadākālaṃ || tena punyena sāntiāyulakṣmīsantativradhanaṃ bhavati || śreyo stu samvat 675 aśvīnimāse || kṛṣṇapakṣe || sptamīpra,aṣṭamyāyān tithau || puṇavasupra,pukhenakṣatreḥ siddhiprasādhyayoge || jathākuhnumūhurtte 〇 somavāsare || tularāśigate savitari, kraktarāśigate candramasi || rājādhirājaparamesvaraparamabhaṭṭārakaḥ śrīśrījayanarendramalladevasya vijayarājye || jvajamāna śrīyebubrumāyāṃ, śrīgāṅgulaṃge śrīkisiroglatolake vaṃthanihmagṛhāddhivāśīna madhanasiṃha bhāro bhrātṛ amṛtasiṃha bhāro bhrātṛ paṃḍu bhāro tṛbhayasana pitā divaṃgata sajubhārosana lihālatā thāsa śrīmat śrīśrīājñamasa upadāṣitaṃ || jathādṛṣtaṃ tathā likhitaṃ lekhiko nāsti dokhanaṃ | jadi suddhaṃm aśuddhaṃ vā 〇 mama dokho na diyate | likhita vaṃkato thaṃthu duthaṃnihmaṃ devajña jagatarājavadhanasya śubham astuḥ || ❖ amṛtasi bhāro prāthvā || (fols. 24v2–25r3)
purpose: tena punyena sāntiāyulakṣmīsantativradhanaṃ bhavati; in memory of their late father Saju Bhāro (pitā divaṃgata sajubhārosana lihālatā thāsa)
notes: Yebubrumā refers to Yambu (northern Kathmandu). Scribe's name Jagatarājavadhana likely represents Jagadrājavardhana.

colophon: /// 653 bhādrapada(śu)kla(daśa)myāyān titho, somavāsare, yoginīsañcārapustaka | śrīśrīrājādhirāja/// rāje ka .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. .. pālitena riṣarṇṇati (!) | likhitam iti || ❁ || śubham astu sarvvasatvānāṃ || ○ /// (last folio v4–5)
notes: The catalogue field gives the year as NS 635, but the quoted colophon reads 653. 653 is taken here; NS 653 = 1533 CE, and NS 635 would be 1515 CE. The weekday (Monday for Bhādrapada śukla 10) has not been checked with a calendar calculation. The colophon names a reigning king ('śrīśrīrājādhirāja/// rāje ka ..'), probably 'rājye' followed by a name beginning ka-, but the name is lost in the lacuna, so no king entry is given. review: purpose cleared: 'śubham astu sarvasattvānām' is a closing benediction, not a statement of purpose
notes expanded: the corrupt 'riṣarṇṇati', the possible 'rājye ka...' reading, and an unverified weekday

title: Guṇanighaṇṭu
subject: Āyurveda
colophon: iti dravyaguṇadhyāyanāmneti bhikhakasya sāstra (!) samāptaḥ || ❁ || śreyo stu || samvat 547 kārttika (fol. 20v5)
notes: 'bhikhakasya' is read as bhiṣakasya ('of the physician'), with kh written for ṣ as is usual in Newari orthography. The phrase means 'the physician's śāstra' and does not name an author. The phrase 'dravyaguṇadhyāyanāmneti' is garbled; it probably stands for dravyaguṇādhyāya-nāmnā, the section or alternative title. The colophon names no scribe, patron or place. The era is not stated, but 'samvat 547' in Newari script fits NS, which agrees with the catalogue.
review: Removed p1 'Bhikhaka': 'bhikhakasya' is almost certainly bhiṣakasya ('of the physician'). Newari scribes often write kh for ṣ, so this is a common noun describing the śāstra, not a personal name. No persons remain.
Date confirmed: NS 547 + 880 = 1427 CE, Kārttika (Oct–Nov 1427).
Notes rewritten.

title: Yogāvalī
subject: Āyurveda
colophon: śreyo stu samvat 575 vaiśāṣaśuklapratipadāyāṃ tithau aśvinīnakṣatre viṣkambhayoge śukravāsare iti || likhita śrīyaṃbūbrumāyāṃ śrīgāṃkulake śrībhāskaradevasaṃskārita,satriśrīkeśavacandrakṛtamahāvihārasaṃghabhikṣuśrī⁅vajrācā⁆[rya]+++++candreṇeti | na cāhaṃ śāstrakarttā ca na ca śabdārthacintakaḥ | yādṛ⁅śaṃ sthita⁆m ādṛśe (!), tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā || bhīmasyāpi bhaved bhaṅgo muner api matibhrama (!) | yadi śuddham aśuddhaṃ vā soddhanīyaṃm (!) ata (!) budhaiḥ || ○ || likhāpitam idaṃ tatraiva brumāyāṃ śrīāśvamandapasthāne, asanavihārakuṭumbaja, vaṭurājikajyotirāmasiṃhasya pārārthena, svārthaparārthahetunām (!) iti || ❁ || (fol. 21r4–v3)
notes: Bhāskaradeva and Keśavacandra are mentioned only as part of the formal name of the vihāra (Itum Bāhā: Bhāskaradeva-saṃskārita Keśavacandra-kṛta Mahāvihāra) and are therefore omitted.

title: Mādhavanidāna
subject: Āyurveda
colophon: devaḥ śrīkamalāsarojanayanaḥ śrīyakṣamallo nṛpaḥ putreṇaiva sahānujena sahitaḥ śrīrāyamallena vai| khyātaḥ śrīraghuvaṅśapaṅkajaraviḥ sannītiratnākaraḥ so ʼyaṃ śrīhimaśailasānubhuvane saṃrājate ʼharnniśaṃ || tadvijayarājye || bhaktāpure nivasitaḥ śubharājadhīro natvā guror ggayapateś caraṇāravindaṃ | vadyottamo jotirājaguṇābhilāṣī tasmai lilekha śubhadañ ca nidānaśāstraṃ || samvad yuge vasau bāṇe pañcamyāṃ ca madhau śite | idaṃ pustaka (!) sampūrṇṇaṃ likhitaṅ śodhyatām budhaiḥ || ❁ || śubham astu || ❁ || (fol. 104r2–5)
notes: The era is not stated in the colophon. NS is assumed because Yakṣamalla is named as the reigning king, and the catalogue also gives NS 584. The 'nivasitaḥ' clause gives Bhaktapur as the scribe's residence; it is assumed to be the place of copying. 'vadyottamo' (= vaidyottamaḥ) is a separate nominative word, in agreement with 'śubharājadhīro', and 'jotirājaguṇābhilāṣī' is also in the nominative, describing the scribe. So the 'excellent physician' is grammatically Śubharāja. The catalogue instead reads the donor as 'Jotirāma Vaidya'. That would require the word to be compounded with the name (vaidyottama-jotirāja-), which the transmitted text does not show. The name is 'jotirāja' in the colophon, not 'Jotirāma'. Nothing in the colophon says there was a donation or a commission; Jotirāja is only the person the copy was written for. Rāyamalla is named as Yakṣamalla's son, together with an unnamed younger brother (sahānujena).
review: Chronogram checked: yuge(4) vasau(8) bāṇe(5) read right to left = 584; NS 584 + 880 = 1464 CE; madhu = Caitra, śite = śukla. Date confirmed.
p5 Jotirāja: removed 'commissioner'. The colophon only says 'tasmai lilekha' (he wrote it for him) and has no likhāpita/lekhayāmāsa wording, so he is kept as beneficiary only.

Epithet 'vadyottamo' moved from Jotirāja to Śubharāja. It is a separate nominative word, in agreement with śubharājadhīro and the finite verb lilekha, while Jotirāja appears only inside the compound and as 'tasmai'. Confidence is lowered because the catalogue reads it as 'Jotirāma Vaidya'.
p4 Gayapati: removed 'guru' from titles. It is the relationship (teacher), not a title.
Notes expanded.

title: Pañcarakṣā
colophon: śrīkāṣṭhamaṇḍa || ❁ || pamahānagarī śrī­kīrtti­puṇyamahāvihārā­vasthitayolācche­śrīpadmarājacandrasābhāryā­sahena | yad atra puṇyaṃ tad bhavatv ācāryo­padhyāya­mātā­pitṛ­pūrvvaṅgama­sakalasava(!)rāśer anuttarajñānaphala prāpnuvantu || rājādhirāja­parameśvara­⁅pa⁆rama­bhaṭṭāraka­śrīśrījaya­ratnamalla­devaśrīśrījaya­arimalla­deva uvaye ṭhākureṇa vijayarājye || likhite 'yam maṇisaṃgha­vihāra­vāsita­vajrācārya­śrīrūparājena || śreyo 'stu || samvat 609 bhādrapadamāse śuklapakṣe pañcamyān tithau svāti nakṣatre saubhāgnya(!) yoge ādītya(!)vatsare 〈〈asya〉〉dine saṃpūrnnam astu śubham || mānse(!) bhādrapade grahāmvararase śukle tithau pañcamī saṃpūrṇṇaiva tu leṣakaṃ bhagavatī devī saha pañcakaiḥ | rakṣāpañcam imām supuṣṭikan sadā pāṭhāt savarṣam prati bhikṣuśrīvarapadmarājasagaṇān devī ciraṃ rakṣatuḥ || yathā dṛṣṭaṃ tathā likhitaṃ lekhiko nāṣṭi doṣa || yadi śuddham aśuddham vā śodhanīya mahadbudhaiḥ || śubham astu || ❁ || (88v5-89r3) (exp. 092)
purpose: merit transfer: the merit goes to the teachers, parents and all beings, so that they attain supreme knowledge (anuttarajñāna)
notes: The catalogue gives NS 509, which is wrong. The colophon has 'samvat 609' in digits, and the chronogram 'grahāmvararase' confirms it: read right to left, rasa 6, ambara 0, graha 9 = 609. NS 609 is about 1489 CE, which fits the joint rule of Ratnamalla and Arimalla in Kathmandu. 'uvaye ṭhākureṇa' = ubhaya-ṭhākureṇa ('the two lords'). 'kāṣṭhamaṇḍa || ❁ || pa' is Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa, split by the ornament. 'sava(!)rāśer' = sattvarāśer. The kīrtipuṇyamahāvihāra is where the patrons live; the colophon does not explicitly call it the place of copying. Padmarāja and Candrasā are taken as patrons only from 'sābhāryāsahena' plus the merit dedication: no likhāpitam or deyadharma appears. The wife's name 'Candrasā' may be incomplete or abbreviated. Padmarāja is called bhikṣu in the closing verse.
review: Weekday normalized to 'Sunday (ādityavāsare)'; as written 'ādītyavatsare' is a scribal slip for vāsare, not a year.
Purpose shortened to a plain description of the merit-transfer formula.

Padmarāja and Candrasā lowered to medium confidence as commissioners: there is no likhāpitam; the role rests on the instrumental 'sābhāryāsahena' plus the dedication of merit. Padmarāja also given role beneficiary, since the closing verse asks the goddess to protect him and his people.

title: Cāndravṛtti
subject: Vyākaraṇa
colophon: ❖ samvat 517 kārtikṛṣṇadasamyāyā titho vṛrsapavāre śrīrathahemavyākranaseṅājuroḥ kalāpavyākrnasūtraḥ (!) || (fol. 25r)
purpose: study of grammar by Rathahema (vyākaraṇa seṅā juro)
notes: The era is not named, but 'samvat 517' with a Newari phrase points to NS: 517+880 = 1396/97 CE. Kārtika kṛṣṇa falls at the start of the NS year, so Oct/Nov 1396. 'vṛrsapavāre' is a corrupt spelling of bṛhaspativāre (Thursday). The Newari 'vyākrana seṅā juro' seems to mean '[he] completed learning grammar'. So Rathahema is the student who studied this text. He may also have been the scribe or owner, but the colophon does not say so. 'Rathahema' may be corrupt for Ratnahema. The colophon calls the text 'kalāpavyākrnasūtra' (Kalāpa/Kātantra grammar). That conflicts with the catalogue title Cāndravṛtti: either the colophon belongs to a different text or the catalogue identification is wrong.

title: Gurusantati
subject: Śāktatantra
colophon: iti śrīkādibhede śrīsvāminīmate caturviṃśatisahasrasaṃhi〇tāyāṃ ambākramabhāśite tvaritāvidhānasūtraṃ dvitīyakhaṇḍasya || ○ || saṃ 308 dvirāśāḍhakṛṣṇanavaṃmyāṃ budhavāre rohiṇī〇nakṣatre śrīśītāṭyāṃ śrībālambūśaṇḍhakārṣṭāśvapoṃbrumāyām adhivāśīpaṃṇḍitācāryaśrīkāmadevarudrātmajapaṃḍitācārya〇śrīśrīvaccharudreṇa svaparārthaheto kādibhedād udhṛtā śrītvaritāsūtraṃ likhitaṃ || ○ || maṅgalamahāśrī || ○ || udakānalacaurebhyo mūśikebhyaś ca duṣṭata[[ḥ]] | rakṣitavyaṃ prayatne[na] kaṣṭeṇa likhitaṃ mayā || ○ || (fol. 13v2-6)
notes: The era is not named ('saṃ 308'), but NS is the only plausible reading for a Nepalese Nagari MS (NS 308 + 880 = c. 1188 CE). 'dvirāśāḍha' means a second (intercalary) Āṣāḍha. The catalogue reads the place as 'Bālambūkhaṇḍha...', but the colophon has 'bālambūśaṇḍha...'. The long toponym is obscure and probably corrupt. Bālambū is very likely modern Balambu in the Kathmandu Valley, but this is not certain, and Śītāṭī may be a locality within it. Grammatically, 'adhivāśī' ('resident') is part of the father's name compound, so the residence is directly stated for Kāmadevarudra and only inferred for the scribe. 'svaparārthaheto' could also mean the scribe kept the copy, but 'owner' was not added because the colophon does not say so explicitly.
