title: Gaṇeśagītā
subject: Vedānta
colophon: śrīmatpadvākyapramāṇamaryādādhuraṃdharacāturdhara vaṃśāvataṃsa goviṃdasūrisūnor nīlakaṇṭhasya kṛtau gaṇēśagītāṭīkāyāṃ gaṇapatibhāvadīpikāyāṃ ekādaśodhyāyaḥ 11 oṃ tatsaditi śrīgaṇeśagītāsūpanisadarthagarbhāsuyogāmṛtārthaśāstre gaṇēśapurāṇe uttarakhaṃḍe śrīgajānanavareṇyasaṃvāde trividhavastuvivekanirupaṇaṃ nāmaikonapaṃcāśatatamodhyāyaḥ 149 gagana śaragirindai vikramārkasya śāke puraharapuri kāśyāṃ bhādraśukle caturthyāṃ || suragurudivasebhūt pūrna eṣaḥ prabadho gaṇapatipadapadme cārpitotīva bhaktyā 1 (fol. 73r2–5)
notes: Chronogram: gagana (sky) = 0, śara (arrow) = 5, giri (mountain) = 7, indu (moon) = 1. Read right to left this gives 1750. 'vikramārkasya śāke' means the Vikrama era, so the year is VS 1750 = c. 1693 CE. The catalogue's 'ŚS 1750 ?' is therefore probably wrong: 'śāka' is used here loosely for 'era'. The weekday (Thursday, suragurudivasa) was not checked against an ephemeris. The day, Bhādrapada śukla 4, is Gaṇeśacaturthī. The verse 'pūrṇa eṣaḥ prabandho gaṇapatipadapadme cārpito' records when and where Nīlakaṇṭha Caturdhara finished his commentary (prabandha), at Kāśī, which fits his known activity in Vārāṇasī in the late 17th century. It does not record when or where this manuscript was copied. The copy may be a later apograph. No scribe, owner or commissioner of this copy is named.
review: p1 Nīlakaṇṭha: removed role 'author' — he is only the commentator (ṭīkā Gaṇapatibhāvadīpikā); the Gaṇeśagītā itself is part of the Gaṇeśapurāṇa
p1/p2 affiliation normalized to 'Caturdhara vaṃśa' (as written cāturdhara)
purpose emptied: 'gaṇapatipadapadme cārpito ... bhaktyā' is the commentator's dedication of his work, not the purpose of this copy
notes expanded: chronogram verification, ŚS/VS conflict with catalogue, date/place refer to the composition of the commentary

colophon: iti carṇavyūhaḥ saṃmāptaḥ || || iti dhṛti śivāśyāmā catvāro vedapaṃktitaḥ || dātavyā yajñakāleṣu īśānādi vyavasthitāḥ || lakṣaṃ tu caturo vedā lakṣabhārata eva ca || lakṣaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ proktaṃ caturlakṣaṃ tu jyotiṣaṃ || || idaṃ pustakaṃ nīlakaṃṭha bhaṭṭasya || || tataḥ padmanābhakeśariśarmaṇaḥ (fol. 4v4–7)
notes: The colophon records successive ownership: 'idaṃ pustakaṃ nīlakaṃṭha bhaṭṭasya || || tataḥ padmanābhakeśariśarmaṇaḥ' ('This book belongs to Nīlakaṇṭha Bhaṭṭa; after that, to Padmanābhakeśariśarman'). The relation p2→p1 ('other') means p2 owned the book after p1. The catalogue lists Padmanābhakeśari Śarmā as scribe and both men as donors ('Nīlakaṇṭhabhaṭṭa–padmanābhakesarī'), but the colophon names no scribe and does not mention a gift. The verses before the ownership note ('iti dhṛti śivāśyāmā...', 'lakṣaṃ tu caturo vedā...') are stock verses, not a record of how this copy was made. Spelling variants: 'carṇavyūhaḥ' for caraṇavyūhaḥ and 'saṃmāptaḥ' for samāptaḥ. The name stem is given as Padmanābhakeśarin; the catalogue spells it Padmanābhakeśari/kesarī.

colophon: iti daśamaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ samāptaḥ ❁ || iti chaṃdogyabrāhmaṇaṃ samāpta (!) || || || || likhitaṃ riṣijī brāhmaṇa gujarāti modacāturvedī rāmakṛṣṇajī (fol. 30r10–11)
notes: The scribal statement 'likhitaṃ riṣijī brāhmaṇa gujarāti modacāturvedī rāmakṛṣṇajī' has no case endings or kinship words. Rāmakṛṣṇa is taken as the scribe because the personal name usually closes the run of caste descriptors (Gujarati Moḍha (Modh) Cāturvedī brahmin; 'moda' is read as moḍha). 'riṣijī' (= ṛṣijī) could be an honorific for that same scribe or a separate person, for example the father. If it is the same person, merge p2 into p1. The catalogue's Scribe field leaves out rāmakṛṣṇajī, so it may have truncated the name. The manuscript is undated. The colophon calls the text chaṃdogyabrāhmaṇa, ending with the 10th prapāṭhaka. A Gujarati scribe suggests the copy was made outside Nepal.
review: Rāmakṛṣṇa (rāmakṛṣṇajī) made the probable scribe, at medium confidence. In this kind of colophon (likhitaṃ + caste descriptors + name), the personal name normally comes last, after the descriptors brāhmaṇa gujarāti modacāturvedī.
riṣijī lowered from scribe/high to 'other'/low. It may be an honorific (ṛṣijī) for the same scribe, or a separate person such as the father. The colophon does not say which.

title: Pañcadaśī
subject: Vedanta
date_raw: aṅkendudakadairmete (!) śakara ite patyaudyutīnāṃ ghane lakṣmījānidine dale tu dhava lekhīḥ
colophon: [Mūla] iti śrīvidyāraṇyamunikṛtāyāṃ vedāntapañcadaśyāṃ pañcabhūtaviveko nāma dvitīyaṃ prakaraṇaṃ sampūrṇam || (fol. 23r5) [Ṭīkā] iti śrīmat paramahaṃṣaparivrājakācārya śrībhāratītīrthavidyāraṇyamunivaryaśiṣyeṇa śrīrāmakṛṣṇākhyaviduṣā viracitā pañcabhūtavivekatātparyadīpikā samāptām aglovīvīt (!) || śrīgaṇapataye namaḥ || || aṅkendudakadairmete (!) śakara ite patyaudyutīnāṃ ghane lakṣmījānidine dale tu dhava lekhīḥ || śrīrāmakṛṣṇa śrīrāmakṛṣṇagopāla || (!) (fol. 23r12, 6–7)
notes: The date verse is badly corrupt. 'aṅkendudakadairmete' is a bhūtasaṃkhyā chronogram, perhaps aṅka(9)-indu(1)-…-mite. The middle number-words can't be recovered, so no year is given. 'śakara ite' probably stands for 'śake' (+ something), so the era is tentatively ŚS. 'patyau dyutīnāṃ ghane' probably names the sun (dyutipati) in some rāśi, but the month can't be identified with certainty. 'lakṣmījānidine' = 'on Viṣṇu's day', which could mean ekādaśī or a weekday. 'lekhīḥ' = 'wrote', but the scribe is not named. 'aglovīvīt (!)' is unintelligible. 'śrīrāmakṛṣṇa śrīrāmakṛṣṇagopāla' at the end looks like a devotional invocation. It could also be the scribe's signature, but no scribe is recorded here. Bhāratītīrtha and Vidyāraṇya are named only as the commentator's gurus. The catalogue fields are empty.

This gives NS 747, which agrees with the cataloguer's NS 747? and with c. 1627 CE. If 'barhis' is instead taken as a separate number word (fire = 3), the expression would give too many digits, so the reading is uncertain. 'anuvāsite' and 'yogod yogataraṃ taraṃgavibhavaṃ' are corrupt (the cataloguer marks this with (!)). The scribe's name could also be divided differently (for example Suparṇarāma), so it is uncertain. title: Sanatsujātīya
subject: Vedānta
colophon: iti śrīmahābhā(1)rate udyogaparvvaṇi sanatsujātīya samāpte trayodaśaḥ || 13 || śrīśāke 1659 caitraśukla 10 śanivāsare svasti śrīgirirājacakracūḍāmaṇinaranārāyaṇetyādi vividhavirudāvalī virājamānamānonnata śrīmanmahārājādhirājakumāra yuvarājaśrīśrīśrīmannṛpapṛṭhvīnārāyaṇaśāhadevājñayā likhitam idaṃ pustakaṃ śrīmokṣeśvaraśarmmaṇā dharmmādhikaraṇena || śrīkṛṣṇo jayati || || (fol. 60v7 and 61r1–5)
purpose: copied by order (ājñayā) of crown prince Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa Śāha
notes: The colophon writes 'pṛṭhvī' with a retroflex ṭh, a scribal or typing slip for 'pṛthvī'. The text calls Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa yuvarāja / mahārājādhirājakumāra, so in ŚS 1659 (= VS 1794 = 1737 CE) he was crown prince, not king. He took the Gorkha throne in 1743. His father, Narabhūpāla Śāha, was reigning but is not named. 'Dharmādhikaraṇa' (literally 'court of justice') here describes the scribe, so it probably means he held the office of judge (dharmādhikārin) at the Gorkha court. The catalogue's VS 1794 matches ŚS 1659. The weekday has not been checked. No place of copying is stated, although Gorkha is likely.
review: p1: removed role 'king'. In ŚS 1659 (1737 CE) Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa was only crown prince (yuvarāja, mahārājādhirājakumāra). The reigning king of Gorkha was his father, Narabhūpāla Śāha, who is not named in the colophon. Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa keeps the role 'commissioner' because the copy was made by his order (ājñayā likhitam).

title: Śvetāśvataropaniṣada
subject: Vedānta
colophon: iti śrīma(4)tparamahaṃsaparivrājakācārya śrīmat jñānottamapūjyapādaśiṣya śrīmadvijñānātmamuni(5)bhagavataḥ kṛtau śvetāśvataropaniṣadvivaraṇe ṣaṣṭhodhyāyaḥ || || śivārpaṇam astu || || || (6)śvetāśvataradīpikā || rāma || rāma || rāma || (fol. 77r3–6) putakamadaḥ śrīkṛṣnajośī rāmanagaravāle | heramba | elvīrādevyai namaḥ || ❁ || viprogastyakulodbhavo dvijavaraḥ śrībhaūnāmā svayaṃ śāke vikramabhūpater atidhṛti devair mite vatsare māse pauṣamite vidhoḥ kṣayadale namgārike vai tithau śrīhemādrisutāpateścaraṇayossevāṃ karoddhārmikaḥ || 1 || śrīkṛṣnajośīracitoyaṃ ślokaḥ saṃ 941 phālguna śukla 5 bhaume divā tṛtīyaprahare racitoyaṃ ||1
notes:
The commentary is Vijñānātman's Śvetāśvataropaniṣadvivaraṇa, also called Śvetāśvataradīpikā. No scribe and no date of copying are stated. 'putakamadaḥ' (= pustakam adaḥ) śrīkṛṣṇajośī rāmanagaravāle marks Kṛṣṇa Jośī of Rāmanagara as the owner. He may also have been the scribe, but the colophon does not say so.

The verse that follows records that the brahmin Bhaū, of the Agastya kula, devoted himself to the feet of Śiva (hemādrisutāpati). This may commemorate his death or renunciation. Its date is 'śāke vikramabhūpater atidhṛti devair mite', i.e. the era of King Vikrama, 'atidhṛti' = 19 and 'devāḥ' = 33. Read in the natural order this gives VS 1933, which is about Dec 1876–Jan 1877 CE. A strict right-to-left reading would give the impossible 3319. The rest of that date is Pauṣa, waning fortnight (kṣayadala), Tuesday ('namgārike' = aṅgārike). The tithi is unclear ('vai tithau').

Kṛṣṇa Jośī says he composed the verse on 'saṃ 941' Phālguna śukla 5, a Tuesday. I take this as VS 1941 with the thousand dropped, which is about Feb–Mar 1885 CE. The catalogue gives VS 1949 (c. 1893), so either the colophon reads 941 for 1949 or the catalogue's date is an error; this needs checking against the manuscript. Both dates describe events written after the copying and give only a terminus ante quem for it.
review: p2 Jñānottama: role 'teacher' → 'other'. He was the commentator's guru, not a teacher connected with this copy.
p3: name 'Kṛṣṇa Jośī' → 'Kṛṣṇa'. 'Jośī' is a surname/caste title and stays only in titles.
p3: role 'author' → 'other'. He composed only the appended verse, not the text; he stays 'owner'.
p4 Bhaū: the titles 'vipra' and 'dvijavara' are kept as descriptions.
Date: ce_approx 1884 → 1885. Phālguna of VS 1941 falls in Feb–Mar 1885. The year '941' is an emendation to 1941, and the conflict with the catalogue's VS 1949 is noted.
The dates in the colophon are for the owner's verse and for Bhaū's act, not for the copying. This is noted.
Added the chronogram in the verse (vikramabhūpater … atidhṛti devair mite = VS 1933, Pauṣa kṛṣṇa, Tuesday) to the notes.
Place: Rāmanagara is the owner's residence, not a stated place of copying, so the place field is now empty. The town is not identified, because many places are called Ramnagar.

title: Ṣoḍaśamahāvākya
subject: Vedānta
colophon: iti śrīmatparamaguru śrīsudarīśakarācāyārya (!) namostu || dvādaśamahāvākyavivar(!) ṇaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ || ślokasaṃkhyā 650 || śrīkṛṣṇārpaṇam astu || he pustaka nārāyaṇatirthasvāmīyāceṃ ase hastākṣara khuda likhita śaṃke 1737 ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || ❁ || (fol. 27r13–15)
notes:
The note at the end is in Marathi: 'he pustaka nārāyaṇatīrthasvāmīyāceṃ ase, hastākṣara khuda likhita' ('this book belongs to Nārāyaṇatīrtha Svāmī; written in [his] own hand'). So he is both owner and scribe. 'Tīrtha' is kept as part of the name because it is a Daśanāmī order name.

The homage name 'śrīsudarīśakarācāyārya' is corrupt. The most likely reading is śrīśaṅkarācāryāya (namo 'stu), meaning Śaṅkara as the paramaguru of the tradition, possibly also the author the text is ascribed to. The colophon does not support treating him as the scribe's personal teacher. A reading Sudarśanācārya is less likely.

The colophon names the work as 'dvādaśamahāvākyavivaraṇa', but the catalogue title is Ṣoḍaśamahāvākya. The number of mahāvākyas differs (12 vs 16).

The catalogue spelling 'Nārāyaṇathirtha' is a misspelling of Nārāyaṇatīrtha.

ŚS 1737 converts to about 1815–16 CE.

p1: role changed from 'teacher' to 'other'. The line is a closing homage to the paramaguru, the founder of the tradition, who may also be the author the text is ascribed to. It does not name a personal teacher of the scribe.
The p2 pupil_of p1 relation is removed: the colophon does not support it.
Purpose rephrased as a dedication formula, not a scribal purpose.
Notes: the work-name conflict (colophon 'dvādaśa-' vs catalogue title 'Ṣoḍaśa-') is now flagged, and the Marathi note is explained.

title: Śārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣyam
subject: Vedānta
colophon: iti śrīmat śārīraka mīmāṃsā bhāṣye śrīmat śaṃkara bhagavatpāda kṛtau caturthādhyāyasya caturthaḥ pādaḥ samāpteyam uttaramīmāṃsā, śāke taponiṣṭha śarāṃgacandre jyeṣṭhāsite paṃcātithau surejye(!) śārīrakaṃ bhāṣyam alekhiyaste ayodhyāṃ samīpe matimadvijena(!) ❖ paṃca saṃvat 1809 āṣāḍha kṛṣṇapakṣe 11 || || || || || || || (fol. 20r2-4)
notes: The scribe is not named. 'matimadvijena(!)' = matimad-dvijena, 'by a wise brahmin', copied 'ayodhyāṃ samīpe' (near Ayodhyā). The colophon gives two dates that do not agree. (1) A verse with a Śaka chronogram, 'śāke taponiṣṭha-śarāṅga-candre jyeṣṭhāsite pañcatithau surejye'. Read right to left, candra=1, aṅga=6, śara=5 and taponiṣṭha is an uncertain unit digit, so the year is Śaka 165x (c. 1728–1737 CE). The day is Jyeṣṭha kṛṣṇa 5, Thursday (surejya = Bṛhaspati). (2) A numeral date, 'saṃvat 1809 āṣāḍha kṛṣṇapakṣe 11', i.e. VS 1809 = c. 1752 CE (= Śaka 1674). The two cannot both be right. One possibility is that the verse was carried over from the exemplar and the numeral saṃvat date belongs to this copy. The meaning of the word 'paṃca' before 'saṃvat' is unclear. The catalogue gives VS 1806, which differs from the 1809 in the quoted colophon.
review: Date: the first reading put ŚS together with ce_approx 1752, which is inconsistent. The Śaka chronogram 'taponiṣṭha śarāṃgacandre', read right to left, gives candra=1, aṅga=6, śara=5 and an uncertain unit (taponiṣṭha), so Śaka 165x (c. 1728–1737 CE). It does not give Śaka 1674 (=1752 CE). The main date is now the explicit numeral date 'saṃvat 1809 āṣāḍha kṛṣṇapakṣe 11', taken as VS 1809 = c. 1752 CE. The Śaka date is moved to notes.
Date fields (month, pakṣa, tithi, weekday) now follow the VS date: Āṣāḍha, kṛṣṇa, 11, weekday not stated. The Jyeṣṭha kṛṣṇa 5, Thursday (surejya) date from the verse is recorded in notes.
Notes: added that the two dates conflict, that the verse may have been carried over from the exemplar, and that the catalogue's VS 1806 differs from the 1809 in the colophon.

colophon: āryāṣṭasahasrikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ parīndanāpari〈pari〉vartto nāma dvātriṃśattamaḥ || 39 || ❖ || samāptā ceyaṃ bhagavatyāryāṣṭasahasrikāprajñāpāramitāsarvatathāgatajananīsarvabodhisatvapretyeka | jena śrāvakānāñ ca mātā dharmamudrā dharmolkā || ❖ || dharmanābhiḥ dharmabherī dharmaratnanidhānaakṣayā dharmmakoṣaḥ || dharmācintyādbhutadarśananakṣatramālādharmatāparamasukhahetur iti || sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvalokavanditāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ samyagunṛjyaparyavāpya ca vācayitvā pravarttyenāṃ viharantu sadārthinaḥ iti || ❖ || ye dharmāhetu prabhavā hetus teṣān tathāgataḥ || jyevadat teṣāṃ yo nirodha evamvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ || ❖ || śubham astu || ❖ || ❖ || saṃvat 963 mti mārgaśiraśudiyā trayodasi budvavārathvaṣuhnū saṃpūrṇṇasiddhayakā juro || || ❖ || dānapatiḥ vakaṃ vāhārayāḥ kāsyapagvatraḥ nalavirasiṃḥ kasya putraḥ mānavirasiṃḥ dvitṛyaputraḥ kṛṣṇamānasiṃḥ bhāryyāḥ tejalakṣmī || thūti parivālayāḥ dharmmacitte utpattijuyā vanalavirasiṃhenaḥ pitāḥ devagatajuyāvaḥ mātṛṃḥ devaṃgatajuyājoḥ dhanavirasiṃ gaṃgālakṣmi niṣnasayā nāmanaḥ || thva śrīprajñāpāramitāḥ pustakadayakā juro || thvayā pūnaijana dhana guṇa saṃtāna saṃpati paripūrṇṇa jayamāla || || mānadevasaskālitaḥ cakravāhārayāḥ śrīvajrācāryyaḥ śrīvidyādattena coyā juro || śubhaṃ || (fol. 311v7–312v1)
purpose: for deceased parents Dhanavirasiṃha and Gaṃgālakṣmī (pitāḥ devagatajuyāvaḥ mātṛṃḥ devaṃgatajuyājoḥ dhanavirasiṃ gaṃgālakṣmi niṣnasayā nāmanaḥ)
notes: Mānadevasaṃskārita Cakra-vihāra (Cukā-bāhā) is in Patan (Lalitpur). The donor's vihāra is Vakaṃ Vāhāra.

title: Abhidharmakośavyākhyā (Sphuṭārthā)
subject: Bauddha Darśana
colophon: ācāryayaśomitrakṛtāyosphuṭāyām abhidharmmakośavyākhyāyām aṣṭamaṃ kośaṣṭhānaṃ samāptam iti || || nairātmyadṛkpravarayānanayasṭhitasya deyākhyadharmaurūdhīdhanabuddhakīrṇaḥ | puṇyaṃ yad atra mama tena janās tu sarvā mātādibhir gurujanaiḥ saha buddhakīrttiḥ || kośasya ṭīkāṃ vimalāṃ sphuṭārthāṃ lekhāpanāt puṇyam upārjitaṃ yataḥ | tenās tu loko ʼkhilakośapūrṇo buddho yathādhīdhanakośapūrṇaḥ || 7 || ye dharmāhetuprabhavā hetus teṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat || teṣāñ ca yo nirodha evamvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ || deyadharmmoyaṃ pravaramahāyānayāyinaḥ śākyabhikṣumahāpaṇḍitaśrīsiddhamuner lekhakasya yad atra puṇyaṃ tatbhavatvācāryopādhyāyamātāpitṛpūrvaṅgamaṃ kṛtvā sakalasattvarāśer anutarajñānaphalāvāptaya iti || śaśimunirasevde likhitam iti gurūstake(!) likhitam || śubham || || (fol. 352v4–10)
purpose: Gift of the Dharma (deyadharma). The merit is transferred to teachers, upādhyāyas, mother and father first, then to all beings, for attaining supreme knowledge (anuttarajñānaphalāvāptaye). Copied from the guru's book (gurupustake).
notes: The chronogram śaśi (1), muni (7), rasa (6), read right to left, gives 671. The colophon names no era. NS is assumed from the Nepalese Buddhist context (śākyabhikṣu) and the catalogue's 'SAM 671', which gives ≈1551 CE. If the era is not NS, this date does not hold. The two verses (numbered 7) are badly corrupt. 'deyākhyadharmaurūdhīdhanabuddhakīrṇaḥ' probably stands for something like 'deyākhyadharmo 'yam adhīdhana-buddhakīrteḥ', which would name a donor Buddhakīrti. However, 'buddhakīrttiḥ' in pāda d could also be a wish ('may all beings gain a Buddha's fame') rather than a name, so p3 is doubtful. The verses use the stock 'lekhāpanāt' (having had it written), and they may have been copied from the exemplar along with the text. 'gurūstake(!) likhitam' is best read as 'gurupustake likhitam': copied from the teacher's manuscript. The script is given as Devanagari, which is unusual for a Nepalese copy of 1551 CE and worth checking against the reel.
review: Siddhamuni: removed 'commissioner' – he is called lekhaka and the deyadharma formula makes him donor; nothing says he had someone else write it (roles now scribe + donor).
Yaśomitra: role reduced to 'commentator' (he wrote the vyākhyā, not the root text).

Added Buddhakīrti (low confidence), read from the corrupt verse 'deyākhya-dharma … buddhakīrtiḥ'. He may be the donor/commissioner named in the stock verses (lekhāpanāt), probably carried over from the exemplar's colophon. Role set to 'other'.
Date: no era is named ('abde' only), so era changed to 'unspecified'. NS is assumed because of the Nepalese śākyabhikṣu context (≈1551 CE).
Purpose: spelling normalised; recorded that the copy was made from the guru's book ('gurūstake' = gurupustake).
Notes expanded.

title: Kāraṇḍavyūhamahāyānasūtra
subject: Bauddha Darśana
colophon: āryakāraṇḍavyūhammahāyānasūtraṃ ratnarājaṃ samāptaṃ(!) || || ye dharmā hetu prabhāvā hetu[s] teṣān tathāgata(!) hṛvat(!) teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃ vādi(!) mahāśramaṇaṃ(!) || || || śubha || śrī(!)yoʼstu saṃvat 788 śrāvaṇa śuklapratipadā(!) budhavāra (!) śubhaṃ || || ❖ śrī śreyostu saṃvat 788...śrīkacchapāgirī parvatāgre , śrīcovāhārasa śrī3 ānandā(vitā)keśvarasthe manaharṣana duntā juro, śrōvacchavāhārayā śrīsākyābhikṣu muktā juna, paralokārthana duntā juro likhitaśrīman (++++)rayā na juro || (fol. 86v1–5)
purpose: offered (duntā) at the Lokeśvara shrine of Chobhar for the welfare in the next world (paralokārtha) of a deceased śākyabhikṣu
notes: The era is not stated. NS is taken from the catalogue and the Newari context: NS 788 ≈ 1668 CE. The second colophon repeats 'saṃvat 788'. The weekday was not checked. 'ānandā(vitā)keśvara' is probably Ānandādi-Lokeśvara, i.e. the Ādinātha Lokeśvara of Chobhar (Kacchapagiri, Covāhāra). This is the place of dedication and not necessarily the place of copying. 'manaharṣana' is taken as 'with a joyful mind'; reading it as the donor name Manaharṣa + ergative is less likely. 'mukta juna' = 'having died / when he died'. The alternative reading, a śākyabhikṣu named Muktā(-ju), cannot be ruled out. The vihāra 'śrōvacchavāhāra' is corrupt and cannot be identified. The scribe's name is lost in a lacuna ('(++++)rayā na'), probably a name ending in -ra followed by the ergative -na. Whether the scribe also made the offering is unclear.
review: Removed p1 'Manaharṣa': 'manaharṣana duntā juro' is best read as 'offered with joy of mind' (mana-harṣa-na), not a personal name; the donor is not named.

Beneficiary: 'muktā juna' is read as Newari 'mukta juna' ('when he died'), so the personal name of the śākyabhikṣu is probably not given. Name set to unnamed and confidence lowered to low; 'Mukta' as a name is kept only as an alternative in notes. The vihāra name is given as written because the reading is uncertain.
Scribe kept with a fragmentary name. Notes now say that '(++++)rayā na' may be a name ending in -ra followed by the ergative -na.
Place: notes say this is where the book was offered (the Lokeśvara/Ādinātha shrine on Kacchapagiri, Chobhar). It is not necessarily where the copy was made.
Purpose made more precise: offered for the welfare in the next world of a deceased śākyabhikṣu.

title: Laṅkāvatārasūtra
subject: Bauddhasūtra
colophon: āryyasaddharmmalaṃkāvatāla(!) nāma mahāyānasūtrasagāthakaṃ samāptam iti || ❁ || || ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetus teṣāṃ tathāgataḥ hy avadat teṣāñ ca yo nirodha evam vādī mahāśramaṇa[ḥ] || śubham astu jagat || ❁ || śubham || śreyo stu samvat 966 miti caitrakṛṣṇayā, trayodasi, bṛhaspativāra, thva kuhnu thva puṣṭaka sidhayakā dina julo || śubhaṃ || dānapati śrīlalitāpūramahānagarayā, ekakṣe, vakaṃbāhālayā, kāyaṣṭha, jyeṣṭhanaravīrasiṃha, bhāryyātejalakṣmī, jyeṣṭhaputra, mānavīrasiṃ, dvitīyaputra; kṛṣṇamānasiṃ, tṛtīyaputra, kulamānasiṃ, caturthaputra, gajamānasiṃ, jyeṣṭhaputrī, devithakuṃ, dvitīyaputrī, bhavānidevi, tṛtīyaputrī, durgādevī, thuti sakalaparivārayāṃ, dharmacittautpatti juyā o, svapitā, dhanavīrasiṃha, svamātṛ, gaṃgālakṣmī, svargārohana juyā o, thva śrī3nokhaṇḍapuṣṭaka cocakaṃ dayakā julo || śubhaṃ || thvaguyā puṇyaṃ, dānapatiyā, dhana, jana, guṇa, jñāna, saptavṛhiṃ paripūrṇṇajuyamāla, sāstrasadjñānātako sophalpa juya māla || śubhaṃ || lekhaka elacukravāhālayā, śrīvajrācāryya, śrītejadattana coyā jula śubham || || thva pustaka sunānaṃ lobhayā yama dujula śubhaṃ || nidānayā yamāla || śubhaṃ (fol. 218r4–218v6)
purpose: Merit transfer for the donor's deceased parents, Dhanavīrasiṃha and Gaṅgālakṣmī (svargārohana juyā o). Also made because the donor's family resolved on a religious act (dharmacittautpatti), with wishes for the donor's prosperity and knowledge.
notes: The catalogue field gives Maṇidatta as scribe, but the colophon names the scribe as Vajrācārya Tejadatta of Elacukravāhāla ('śrītejadattana coyā jula'); the -na ending is the Newari ergative. No place of copying is stated. The donor lived in Lalitapura (Patan) at Vakaṃbāhāla. 'ekakṣe' is unclear (perhaps a locality or a corruption). In 'jyeṣṭhanaravīrasiṃha', 'jyeṣṭha' is taken as an epithet ('eldest' or head of household), not part of the name. 'śrī3nokhaṇḍapuṣṭaka' is unclear; it may be a corruption of 'navakhaṇḍa' or a name of the text. The date NS 966 Caitra kṛṣṇa 13, a Thursday, falls in about March/April 1846 CE. The weekday has not been checked.
review: p1 name: 'jyeṣṭha' treated as an epithet ('eldest' or head of household), not part of the name, so the name is Naravīrasiṃha. 'jyeṣṭha' moved to titles and kāyastha normalised.
p1: Lalitapura and Vakaṃbāhāla moved to residence. Vakaṃbāhāla is the donor's locality and is not clearly a monastic affiliation.
Place of copying: the colophon does not state where the copy was made. The Lalitapura address belongs to the donor, so the place field is now empty and this is explained in the notes.
p10/p11: 'relative_only' removed. They are the beneficiaries of the merit transfer.
Added son_of/daughter_of relations from the children to the mother, Tejalakṣmī (p2).
Purpose rephrased as a merit transfer to the deceased parents rather than 'parārtha'.
Notes expanded: the catalogue gives Maṇidatta as scribe but the colophon names Tejadatta; the form 'śrī3nokhaṇḍa' is unclear; 'ekakṣe' is unclear.

title: Laṅkāvatārasūtra
subject: Bauddhasūtra
colophon: āryyaśrīlaṃkāvatāraṃ nāma mahāyānasūtraṃ saṃ(!)gāthakaṃ dasamādhyāya[ḥ] samāpta〈m〉[ḥ] iti || ❁ || || svasti sa〈ṃ〉mvat 819 ākhāḍhakṛṣṇa 13 thva kuhnu ālaṃbhayāña coyā dānapatimakhanabāhālayā, vajrācārya parmmadhrabhābhṛ,vajrācāṛya dharmmadhrakāṃ ke … likhitayaṃ, ratnakṛtivihālayā, 〈〈dha〉〉 dharmadhātu〈〈tu〉〉sevita, sāṃtikra〈〈sa〉〉vaṃ samāgavajrācāṛya dharmadhralena, tha(va)ta, vyākhyānayā yayā taco yā julo || … || || || śubha (fol. 205r3–206r3)
purpose: for the scribe's own use in exposition (thavata vyākhyānayā yayā); sponsored by a dānapati
notes: NS 819 = c. 1699 CE. 'ālaṃbhayāña coyā' means 'began and wrote', so the date may be the day copying started. 'parmmadhra' is the Newari scribal shorthand for -dhara: Padmadhara is the more likely reading, but Paramadhara is possible. 'bhābhṛ' is corrupt. It may stand for 'bhrātṛ' (brother), which would make the two Vajrācāryas brothers, but this is uncertain. Makhan Bāhāl in Kathmandu is generally identified with Ratnakīrti Mahāvihāra, so both men probably belonged to the same vihāra. 'sāṃtikra〈〈sa〉〉vaṃ samāga' is unclear: it may refer to a Śāntikara lineage or title. 'vyākhyāna' (exposition) suggests Dharmadhara meant to use the text in teaching; 'reader' is not added because the colophon does not say so explicitly. Whether the dānapati also commissioned the copy is implied, not stated.
review: p2 Dharmadhara: dropped 'donor' — the colophon calls only the Makhan Bāhāl man dānapati; Dharmadhara keeps scribe ('dharmmadhrakāṃ … likhitayaṃ', '…dharmadhralena … coyā') and owner ('thavata … yayā').
p2 residence and affiliation set to Ratnakīrti Vihāra, which the colophon states ('ratnakṛtivihālayā'), instead of Makhan Bāhāl, which is only given for p1.
p1 name confidence lowered to medium: 'parmmadhra' could be Padmadhara or Paramadhara.
The 'brother_of' relation is kept but marked doubtful: it rests on the corrupt word 'bhābhṛ'.
Place of copying emptied: 'makhanabāhālayā' is the donor's residence; the colophon does not say where the copy was made.
Month normalized to Āṣāḍha; the purpose wording is clarified.

title: Lokeśvaraśataka
subject: Bauddhastotra
colophon: iti śrīvajradattajinabhikṣukaviviracitaṃ śrīlokeśvaraśatakaṃ samāptam || || śubham astu || || || || khanayananidhiyuṃkte[[varṣe]] mārgamāse valakṣe ditisutaguruvāre sūryajābhrātṛtithyāṃ || nṛpatigurunimittaṃ śrṭmadāryavaloke śvaraśatakam aleṣīt(!) kopi bauddho ʼmṛtādyaḥ(!) || 1 || || || śubham astu jagatāṃ || || || || (fol.19r4-6 )
purpose: nṛpatigurunimittaṃ — for (the sake of) the king's guru, or for the king and the guru
notes: Chronogram read right to left: kha = 0, nayana = 2, nidhi = 9, giving 920. The era is not named, but in a Nepalese Buddhist context it is most likely NS: NS 920 Mārgaśīrṣa ≈ Nov/Dec 1799 CE. The catalogue's '[VS] 420?' looks like a misreading of nidhi (9) and is implausible. 'valakṣe' = bright fortnight (śukla). 'ditisutaguru' = Śukra, so the weekday is Friday. 'sūryajābhrātṛtithi': Sūryajā = Yamunā; her brother is Yama. Yama is lord of the 10th tithi (daśamī). Yamadvitīyā belongs to Kārttika and does not fit Mārga. The catalogue's 'pratipadā' has no support in the text. The weekday has not been checked against an ephemeris. 'aleṣīt(!)' = alekhīt. Scribe: 'kopi bauddho ʼmṛtādyaḥ(!)' means 'some Buddhist, Amṛta...'. Possibly read ʼmṛtāhvaḥ 'named Amṛta', which fits the mālinī cadence. Given the date (c. 1799) and the phrase 'nṛpatigurunimittaṃ', an identification with the Buddhist paṇḍita Amṛtānanda of Kathmandu is tempting but unproven. The verse is mālinī.
review: Tithi: 'sūryajābhrātṛtithi' = tithi of Yama (brother of Yamunā, daughter of the Sun). Under the standard tithi-lord scheme Yama governs the 10th tithi, so it is daśamī, not dvitīyā. Yamadvitīyā is a Kārttika festival and does not fit Mārga. Confidence medium.
Scribe name normalized to 'Amṛta' (ʼmṛtādyaḥ(!) probably corrupt for ʼmṛtāhvaḥ 'named Amṛta'); possible identification with the Buddhist paṇḍita Amṛtānanda (fl. c. 1800) noted.
'bauddha' moved from titles to affiliation.
Era: chronogram 920 most plausibly NS; era left as unspecified because the colophon does not state it. ce_approx 1799 kept on the NS assumption.
Purpose clarified: written for the king's guru (or for the king and guru).
Notes expanded: catalogue's 'VS 420?' and 'pratipadā' do not agree with the colophon.

title: Bhūtaḍāmaratantra
subject: Bauddha Tantra
colophon: bhūtaḍāmaramahātantrarājaḥ samāptaḥ || ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetu[s] teṣāṃ tathāgataḥ | hyavadat teṣāñ ca yo nirodhaḥ evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ || || maṇiyugāṅke siddhye, abhāmāse site dine pañcamyāṃ ca tathā caiva, saumyānandā(!) likhet khalu || || || śubham astu (fol. 50v3–5)
notes: The era is not stated; NS is assumed from the Newari script and the three-digit chronogram. The chronogram maṇi-yuga-aṅka, read right to left, gives 9(aṅka)-4(yuga)-x(maṇi). Taking maṇi = 9 gives NS 949 (≈1829 CE). The catalogue's 'NS 94(1)' implies maṇi = 1, which is less usual; if that is right, the date is NS 941 (≈1821 CE). 'siddhye' may simply mean 'for success' (or be a corruption of siddhe), not part of the number; if siddhi = 8 were meant, the number would not make sense. The month 'abhāmāse' is corrupt; it might stand for bhādramāse or adhimāse, but this is uncertain. 'site dine' = śukla pakṣa. The name ending saumyānandā(!) is marked by the cataloguer; the stem is Saumyānanda. The ye dharmā stanza follows the end of the text.
review: Chronogram re-read: maṇi normally = 9 (nine gems), yuga = 4, aṅka = 9; reading right to left gives NS 949 (≈1829 CE), not 941. The catalogue's 94(1) is noted as an alternative reading.
Month left as written ('abhāmāsa', corrupt); possible emendations given in notes.
Notes expanded.

title: Uddhārakośa
subject: Śaivatantra
date_raw: svāṃgarbhūrvī sammite śākalāe jyeṣṭhaye ṣaṣṭhyāṃ śuklapakṣe’kavāre
colophon: iti śrī dakṣIṇāmūrtti viracite uddhārakośe sakalāṃgamasāre ṣoḍaśadevī saptakumāra navagraha saptadevī catuṣṭadevī maṃtradhyānakośa nirṇayo nāma saptamakalpaḥ svāṃgarbhūrvī sammite śākalāe jyeṣṭhaye ṣaṣṭhyāṃ śuklapakṣe’kavāre || pṛthvīpālasyālayādo(!) lilekha gaṃgā viṣṇustaṃtram uddhārakośam ❁ ❁ || trivikrama varmaṇo rājñādeḥ pustakaṃ śubhadm astu ❁ (fol.23v2-5)
purpose: book of King Trivikramavarman (copied at the king's palace)
notes: 'śākalāe' is probably a corruption of śākakāle, so the era is Śaka. The chronogram 'svāṃgarbhūrvī' is corrupt. One possible reading is kha (0), aṅga (6), bhū (1), urvī (1). Read right to left, that gives ŚS 1160, about 1238 CE. However, 'sva' is not a standard number-word: it could also be svara (7), giving ŚS 1167. I have left ce_approx blank for that reason. A 13th-century date also seems early for a Devanagari paper manuscript, so this needs checking against the weekday. 'pṛthvīpālasyālayādo(!)' is most likely pṛthvīpālasyālaye, 'in the king's palace'. The 'pṛthvīpāla' there is probably the common noun 'king', meaning Trivikramavarman, not a personal name. 'rājñādeḥ' could be rājñaḥ, or rājñā + ādeḥ/ādeśāt ('by the king's order'). If it is ādeśāt, Trivikramavarman would also be the commissioner. Read 'gaṃgā viṣṇustaṃtram' as Gaṅgāviṣṇus tantram. 'śubhadm' should be śubham.
review: Removed 'Pṛthvīpāla' (p3) as a person: pṛthvīpālasyālaya most likely means 'the residence/palace of the king' (pṛthvīpāla = king, a common noun), probably meaning Trivikramavarman's palace; this is now recorded only under place.

Trivikramavarman: removed 'commissioner' because the colophon only says the book is his (pustakam), with no likhāpita/lekhayāmāsa. Kept 'owner' and added 'king' with medium confidence, since he is called rājan and the copy was made at a king's palace.
Weekday changed to its normal form 'arkavāra' (Sunday); the colophon has ’kavāre.
Place: added a tentative reading of 'king's palace'.
Purpose filled in: the copy was made for the king's own book.
Notes: added a tentative decoding of the chronogram.

title: Kālīkulakramārcana
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: iti vāśiṣṭhīye, uttarāmnāya,kālīkramasaṃkṣepahomavidhiḥ || || ❁ || samvat 819 kārtikaśuklaṣaṣṭhami utrabhadranakṣetra bṛhaspativāra thva kunhu śrīśrīśrī vimalaprabodhamata śrīśrīśrīguhyakālyāna krama saṃpūrṇṇa yāṅā likhita karmmācāryya cakrasiṃhana || śubham astu sarvvadā kālam || (fol. 61r2-4)
notes: The era is not named, but 'samvat' with Newari text is Nepal Saṃvat (NS), which matches the catalogue. The NS year starts at Kārtika śukla 1, so Kārtika śukla 6 of NS 819 is Oct/Nov 1698 CE. The usual NS+880 rule gives 1699, which is too late for a Kārtika date. The tithi 'ṣaṣṭhami' is corrupt: it could be ṣaṣṭhī or aṣṭamī. On either day the moon is unlikely to be in Uttarabhādrapadā; on Kārtika śukla 6–8 it is usually around Uttarāṣāḍhā to Dhaniṣṭhā. So the date details are internally inconsistent, and the weekday has not been checked. The copy contains the krama of Guhyakālī 'according to Vimalaprabodha's doctrine' (vimalaprabodhamata). I take Vimalaprabodha as the traditional author of the Kālīkulakramārcana, not as someone involved in making this copy. The colophon names the text as 'kālīkramasaṃkṣepahomavidhiḥ' from the Vāśiṣṭhīya, Uttarāmnāya.
review: Added Vimalaprabodha (p2) as author: 'vimalaprabodhamata' is the doctrine of Vimalaprabodha, to whom the Kālīkulakramārcana is attributed. The first reading treated it only as a school name.
ce_approx changed from 1699 to 1698. The Nepal Saṃvat (NS) year begins at Kārtika śukla 1, so Kārtika śukla 6 of NS 819 falls in Oct/Nov 1698.
Normalized the nakṣatra and recorded it as inconsistent with the tithi; marked the corrupt tithi 'ṣaṣṭhami' as doubtful in notes.
Normalized the scribe's title to 'karmācārya'.

title: Tārākalpalatā
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: iti tārākalpalatāyāṃ praṃcamastavake paṃcamaṃ kusumaṃ || || sādhakāya pradattāsi, tārākalpalate mate | (!) sarvvabhāvamayībhāva,m anubhāveya sādhakaṃ || x || iti śrīmahāmahopādhyāyaśrīnandanācāryyānte,vāsiniravedyāgamavidyāvidyetitaśrīsanātanaguṇārṇṇavācāryyātmajaśrītatkālaṃkārabhaṭṭācāryyaviracitāyāṃ (!) tārākalpalatāyāṃ pañcamastavakaḥ samāptaṃḥ (!) || x x || bhīmaseno ranyabhaṅga, (!) munīnāñ ca matibhrama (!) jathā diṣṭaṃ tathā likhitaṃ mama dvaṣya na dīyate || (!) x || śubham astu || || || || (fol. 83v7-84r5)
notes: The colophon only identifies the author. It gives no scribe, no commissioner and no copy date. The closing verse 'bhīmaseno ranyabhaṅga (= raṇe 'pi bhaṅgaḥ) ... yathā dṛṣṭaṃ tathā likhitaṃ mama doṣo na dīyate' is a stock scribal apology; Bhīmasena in it is mythological, not a person. The author's name 'Tatkālaṃkāra' is probably corrupt, perhaps for Tattvālaṃkāra or a similar -alaṃkāra name. The epithet 'niravedyāgamavidyāvidyetita' is probably meant as 'niravadyāgamavidyāvidyotita'. Nandana(ācārya) is the author's teacher (antevāsin) and Sanātanaguṇārṇava(ācārya) is the author's father. Neither is connected with this copy.
review: p1: name normalized to 'Nandana' (ācārya already in titles); role changed from 'teacher' to 'other' because he is the author's teacher, not connected with this copy (the pupil_of relation is kept)
p2: name normalized to 'Sanātanaguṇārṇava' (ācārya already in titles)
p3: name 'Tatkālaṃkāra' kept as written, with low confidence; notes now discuss the probable corruption
notes expanded: the verse is a stock scribal apology, Bhīmasena in it is mythological and not a person, and the epithet is corrupt

review: No substantive changes. The note now explains that the era is inferred: 'saṃvat' alone does not name one, and VS is chosen because the catalogue's king fits.

notes: The colophon gives only 'samvat 963' and does not name the era. I inferred Nepāla Saṃvat (= c. 1843 CE) from the Devanagari script and the 'roja' weekday formula. VS 963 (c. 906 CE) is not plausible for this kind of manuscript. The tithi is written 'śudi (10) 8'. The first akṣara of the scribe's name is uncertain ('(jñ)ogarasiṃha'). It may stand for Jogarasiṃha or a similar name. The cataloguer also queries it ('Jñogarasiṃha ?').

title: Mantrakoṣa
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: || iti śrīmad āditya tripāṭhīsaṃgṛhīte maṃtrakoṣe mudrādikathanaṃ nāma viṃśatimaḥ (!) paricchedaḥ samāpto yaṃ maṃtrakoṣaḥ ||…………………… || ………………………………………………………………………………………….. śrīśāke 1565 pauṣavadi 13 vidhānurādhāyāṃ likhitaṃ manoharasutaśrīmad anaṃtaśarmaṇo || || śubham astu || (fol. 183v10–11, 184r1–5)
notes: The catalogue gives 'Āśāditya Tripāṭhī' as the scribe. In the colophon he is the compiler of the Mantrakoṣa (saṃgṛhīte), so the role is author. The quoted text reads 'śrīmad āditya'. The catalogue's 'Āśāditya' may come from a misreading of 'śrīmadāditya', or the manuscript may actually read 'śrīmadāśāditya'. The copy was written by Ananta(śarman), son of Manohara. 'vidhānurādhāyāṃ' is taken as vidhau (Monday) + anurādhāyāṃ (nakṣatra). Adding 78 to ŚS 1565 gives 1643/44. Pauṣa kṛṣṇa 13 falls around late December 1643 (pūrṇimānta) or January 1644 (amānta). The weekday has not been checked.

notes: The only person named is the author. The colophon calls him Kāśīnātha 'bhaṭṭopanāmaka', meaning his surname (upanāma) is Bhaṭṭa, and gives him the epithet 'dakṣiṇāmūrti-śivārādhaka' (worshipper of Śiva as Dakṣiṇāmūrti; 'śīva' is a slip for 'śiva'). He is probably Kāśīnātha Bhaṭṭa (Śivānandanātha), the late Tantric compiler, but the colophon does not say so. Bhaṭṭa is recorded as a surname-title. The colophon closes the uttarārdha with the stock 'ādarśadoṣā...' and '...kṣamasva' formulas but names no scribe, patron, date or place. 'likhidisva' is corrupt, probably for likhitvā or likhitam.

title: Mantramahodadhi
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: iti śrīma(5)nmahīdharaviracite maṃtramahodadhau ṣaṭkarmādinirūpaṇaṃ paṃcaviṃśas taraṃgaḥ || || śrīnṛsiṃhāya namaḥ | saṃvat 1824 mīti (!) (6) agahanabadī 1 vārasanīścarake līkhāḥ (!) dasakhataguravakaśakāethaḥ kāsī madheyī arīparaḥ cīraṃjīvīnāmaḥ (7) śrīkṛṣṇāya namo namaḥ || || śrīrāmāya namo namaḥ || || śrīnaraśīṃghāya (!) namo namḥ (!) ❁ (fol. 136r4-7)
notes: The colophon is in Hindi. 'mīti' is miti and 'līkhāḥ' is likhā. 'dasakhata' is dastkhat, 'handwriting/signature', so the phrase reads 'written in the hand of Guravakaśa (probably Gurbakhś) Kāyastha (kāetha), in Kāśī (kāsī madhye)'. The era is not named: 'saṃvat' with a Hindi date formula (agahana badī) points to Vikrama. Under the North Indian pūrṇimānta reckoning, Agahana badī 1 falls about late October or November 1767 CE. I did not verify the weekday. 'arīparaḥ cīraṃjīvīnāmaḥ' is unclear. It may name a locality in Kāśī (Haripura?) and a person Cirañjīvī, perhaps the owner or beneficiary. It may also be a corrupt blessing formula (cirañjīvī). Cirañjīvī is therefore recorded with role 'other' and low confidence.
review: p2: 'dasakhata' read as Hindi dastkhat 'handwriting/signature' (not part of the name); name kept as Guravakaśa, probably the Hindi name Gurbakhś (Gurubakhśa); confidence lowered to medium because the reading is not certain

date: month normalized to Mārgaśīrṣa (agahana); paksa normalized to kṛṣṇa (badī); weekday to Saturday (śanaiścara)
place: normalized spelled Vārāṇasī
notes: expanded on dastkhat, the pūrṇimānta month reckoning, and the unclear 'arīparaḥ cīraṃjīvīnāmaḥ'

title: Bhūtaḍāmaratantra
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: iti bhūtaḍāmare mahātaṃtre yakṣasiddhisādhanavidhiḥ paṃcadaśaḥ paṭalaḥ samāptaḥ || || śivaproktabhūtaḍāmarataṃtro yaṃ lalitāprarīyaśrīsūryānaṃdenālikhat || (!) śrī 1915 || pauṣe site śukladale viśāṣe (!) tithicaṃdrage || etatprāpte śubhadine sampūrṇam agamat śubham || (fol. 35r4-6)
notes: The colophon gives no era name ('śrī 1915'). It is taken as VS because NS 1915 is impossible and ŚS 1915 lies in the future. Pauṣa of VS 1915 falls in Dec 1858 to Jan 1859. 'tithicaṃdrage' is read as tithi = candra (1), i.e. śukla pratipad. 'viśāṣe (!)' most likely stands for Viśākhā. But the moon is not normally in Viśākhā on Pauṣa śukla 1, so the word may instead be a corruption of 'viśeṣe'. Lalitāprarīya stands for lalitāpurīya, 'of Lalitapur (Patan)'. It describes where the scribe is from, and the place of copying (catalogue: Latitapura, sic) is inferred from it. 'ayaṃ … ālikhat' is ungrammatical, as the cataloguer marked with (!).
review: p1 as_written trimmed to the name itself (sūryānaṃdena); residence given as lalitāprarīya (= lalitāpurīya, Patan)
tithi: 'tithicaṃdrage' read as candra = 1, i.e. pratipad (śukla 1), not just 'caṃdra'
nakshatra: viśāṣe (!) read as Viśākhā, with a note that this is astronomically doubtful
era: the colophon has no era name; VS is inferred, and this is now stated in notes; ce_approx changed to 1858/1859
place: noted that it is inferred from the scribe's residence, not stated as the place of copying

title: Merutantra
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: || iti śrīrudrayāmale gāya〈ta〉trītattv[as]āre stavaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ || śubham astu || saṃvat || 1869 || aśvini(!)māse śuklapakṣe tithau || 15 || bhaumavāsare || pratiliṣi(!)taṃ ma///veratharīyā || yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ kṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā || yad aśuddham(!) aśuddhaṃ vā mama doṣo na dīyate || 1 || śrīmate rāmacaṃdrāya. (fol. 26r9–11)
notes: The scribe's name is damaged ('ma///veratharīyā'). The opening 'ma' could even be the start of 'mayā', so the personal name may be lost entirely. 'Tharīyā' looks like a family, clan or caste designation (cf. Nep. Tharī), but this is uncertain. The era is not stated explicitly; VS is assumed from the year 1869 and the catalogue. The weekday was not checked against the tithi. The quoted colophon closes a 'Gāyatrītattvasāra stava' attributed to the Rudrayāmala, not the Merutantra of the catalogue title; it may be an appended text, or the title may be wrong. The catalogue's 'King: Upendravikama' is not in the colophon. Girvāṇayuddha Vikrama Śāha ruled Nepal in VS 1869, so the catalogue field is doubtful and no reigning king is recorded. 'śrīmate rāmacaṃdrāya' is an invocation of the deity Rāma. 'yad aśuddham(!) aśuddhaṃ vā' is a corruption of the stock verse 'yad (a)śuddham śuddhaṃ vā'.
review: Scribe name: removed the invented capitalised stem 'Ma...veratharīyā'. The name is given as a lacuna-marked fragment '[ma]...vera Tharīyā', and 'tharīyā' may be a family or caste name. Confidence stays low.

notes: 'saṃ. 1615' in a Devanagari manuscript is taken as Vikrama Saṃvat. If the year is Caitrādi, Kārttika kṛṣṇa 8 of VS 1615 falls in Oct/Nov 1558 CE; if it is Kārttikādi, it falls in Oct/Nov 1557 CE. 'kā. Va.' is read as kārttika vadi (dark fortnight), and 'bhaumayuktāyā' gives Tuesday. Uduṃvara (= Audumbara) is probably the scribe's community, lineage or family name (possibly the Audumbara brahmin group) rather than a personal name. The catalogue gives the scribe as 'Uduṃvara Śrīgiviṃda', but the colophon reads 'goviṃdena', so Govinda is the right reading. A lacuna (dots) after 'ālekhi' may have held more names or details.

title: Śivārcanacandrikā
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: iti śṛīsundarācāryyacaraṇāraviṃdadvadvāṃte vā śrīnivāsabhaṭṭeba viracitāyāṃ śrīśivārcanacaṃdrikāyāṣaṭcatvāriṃśaḥ parakāśaḥ || samātā śivārcanacandrikāḥ || yādṛśa (!) pustakaṃ………………………. ……………………………doṣo na dīyate || śrīśāke samvatsare 965 || śrīvikramasamvatsare 578 ? śrīkarisamvatsare 4833 nepālasamvatsare 852 | āṣāḍhaśuklacaturddaśī, mūlanakṣatra (!) aindrayoge caṃdravāsare saṃpūrṇam iti, bhaktapattanasthāna (!) lekhyate | (fol. 292v7–9)
notes: The colophon gives the date in four eras. Nepāla Saṃvat 852 (Āṣāḍha falls in 1732 CE) and Kali 4833 (4833−3101 = 1732) agree. Śaka 965 and Vikrama 578 do not: the expected figures are about ŚS 1654 and VS 1789. These two numbers are corrupt, either in the manuscript or in the cataloguer's transcription (the '?' after 578 may be the cataloguer's). The weekday (Monday) and the nakṣatra have not been checked against an ephemeris. Mūla on śukla 14 of Āṣāḍha is astronomically plausible. The scribe and the commissioner are not named; the passage after 'yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ' is only the stock scribal verse. Sundarācārya and Śrīnivāsa Bhaṭṭa are connected with the composition of the Śivārcanacandrikā, not with this copy. The author's name, 'śrīnivāsabhaṭṭeba', should read śrīnivāsabhaṭṭena, and 'dvadvāṃte vā' should read dvandvāntevāsinā.

title: Śivārcanacandrikā
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: ❖ śrīśrīsumatijayatitāmitramalladeasanadhapustakadayakā bhagirāmapramaānayāvelasa saṃvat 810 kārttika śudi 9 (fol. 65v11)
notes: The colophon is in Newari. It reads roughly '[Sumatijaya]jitāmitramalladeva-sana (agentive) dhā(?) pustaka dayakā (had made) Bhagirāma pramāṇa-yā velasa (at the time of)'. 'jayatitāmitra' is a corrupt spelling of jayajitāmitra, and 'malladea' of malladeva. The king is Jitāmitra Malla of Bhaktapur (r. c. 1673–1696), whose full style is Sumatijayajitāmitramalla. 'dhā' is unclear: it may be a corruption of thva ('this') or part of a word for the type of text. 'pramaāna' is taken as the office title pramāṇa/pramāna; Bhagirāma's exact office is uncertain. NS 810 is consistent with Jitāmitra's reign. The place is not stated, but Bhaktapur is likely given the king.

date_raw: śaradi apani paṃcāṅkendge īṣa śūbhre ahi tithi gurū pāre
colophon: iti śrīmadakṣobhyamahogratārāsamvāde tārāsūkte vrahamajātivarṇane daśamaḥ paṭalaḥ śaradi apani paṃcāṅkendge īṣa śūbhre ahi tithi gurū pāre śakti saṃgākhyataṃtraṃ vilikhatya śūbhamaṃ vedvāś dhanāyaṃ suviñair anativipulavudhir ṭōḍarānandasaṃjñaḥ śubham astu śāṃtir astu lekhakapāṭhakayo (!) bhavyaṃ bhūyāstām samāptaḥ (fol. 177r2–4)
notes: The colophon is a corrupt verse. 'apani paṃcāṅkendge' = avani(1) pañca(5) aṅka(9) indu(1); read right to left this gives 1951. The colophon names no era. VS 1951 (= 1894 CE) is the likely reading for a Devanagari manuscript; Śaka 1951 would be impossible. 'ahi' = 8 (serpent), so the date is Āśvina (Iṣa) śukla aṣṭamī, a Thursday, which fits śarad. The name Ṭoḍarānanda (or Ṭoḍara-, depending on how '-ānandasaṃjñaḥ' is parsed) is taken as the scribe, who describes himself modestly as 'anativipulabuddhi'. The name is unusual and the passage around it ('vedvāś dhanāyaṃ suviñair') is garbled. Be careful not to confuse it with the well-known compendium Ṭoḍarānanda. The phrase 'lekhakapāṭhakayoḥ' is a standard blessing formula and does not name anyone.

Tasadīna leṣaka. Śahara mṃktāpurai pācheyā śrīharakumārajāra dvijātmaja śrīāśvinīkumārarāja vipraṇa 21 saṃphudayekā || śubham sarvadā śubham || || || (fol. 41r8–11)
notes: The colophon is in Nepali. VS 1949 and NS 1012 agree (both 1892 CE), and Āṣāḍha śukla 4 falls on about Tuesday 28 June 1892, which matches maṃgalavāra. 'mṃktāpurai' is most likely Muktāpura. It could be a misreading of Bhaktāpura (Bhaktapur), since म and भ are easily confused, but this is not certain. 'pācheyā' may name a locality or tole. The father's name 'harakumārajāra' is corrupt: it could be Harakumārarāja (with metathesis, matching the son's '-kumārarāja') or contain 'Jhā'. 'Tasadīna leṣaka' = 'tas dina lekhaka' ('the scribe on that day'), which confirms p2 as the scribe.

colophon: || ādyakhaṃṇḍasaṃpūrṇṇaḥ || || śubham astu sarvvadā || || saṃvat 752 thvadaṃ śrī 3 bhavānīśaṃkarapritina śrīkālidāsena saṃcaya yāṅā | umeśāprītaye tantraṃ kālidāsena saṃcitaṃ | anena puṇyayogena tayor anter ayo ʼstute || || (fol. 169v9–11)
purpose: for the pleasure of Bhavānīśaṅkara (Umeśa); merit (puṇyayoga)
notes: The era is not named. NS is assumed because the script is Newari and the colophon is in Newari (NS 752 ≈ 1632 CE). The text says Kālidāsa compiled (saṃcaya yāṅā / saṃcita) the tantra in NS 752 ('thvadaṃ' = 'this year'). This may record when the compilation was made, so the manuscript could be his own or an autograph copy. However, the colophon does not explicitly call him the scribe or commissioner. The catalogue gives Pūrṇānaṃdanātha as scribe, but that name does not appear in this colophon; perhaps it comes from elsewhere in the manuscript. The final pāda 'tayor anter ayo ʼstute' is corrupt; perhaps 'tayor antar ... astu te'. Bhavānīśaṅkara and Umeśa are deities and are not counted as persons.
review: Kālidāsa: roles changed from commissioner+owner to author (compiler). 'saṃcaya yāṅā' and 'tantraṃ kālidāsena saṃcitaṃ' mean he compiled the work. They are not commissioning or ownership formulas. Confidence lowered to medium.
Evidence extended to include 'tantraṃ kālidāsena saṃcitaṃ'.
Purpose rephrased in English.
Notes expanded: the compilation date may coincide with this copy, the final line is corrupt, and the era is assumed.

title: Cikitsāmṛta
subject: Āyurveda
colophon: śrīsarvavidyānidhāna kavīndrācārya sa………. ci[[ki]]tsāmṛtapustakam || rāmāya namaḥ || || (cikīrśīte) (!) karmaṇicakrapāṇe ‥‥‥ tāneva sāhāya sampat || pāṃcālajāyā paṭalaṃvittāne (!) madhye samaṃ yaṃ na tu nīnavedmā (!) || || | (fol.134v3–5)
notes: The quoted passage is an ownership note in the standard form used by the library of the Benares scholar Kavīndrācārya Sarasvatī (fl. c. 1600–1675): 'sarvavidyānidhāna kavīndrācārya sa[rasvatīnām] … pustakam'. The name breaks off after 'sa…', so the restoration to Sarasvatī is a guess, though a very likely one. The ownership note means the copy existed before c. 1675, but no date is given. The verse that follows ('cikīrṣite karmaṇi cakrapāṇe…') is a corrupt stanza and contains no persons. The catalogue fields 'Scribe: milhaṇa' and 'Place of Copying: ḍhillikānagara' do not appear in the quoted text. They very probably come from the author's own colophon: Milhaṇa composed the Cikitsāmṛta at Ḍhillikā (Delhi) in the 13th century (traditionally VS 1281 ≈ 1224 CE). If so, Milhaṇa is the author, not the scribe of this copy, and Delhi is where the text was composed, not where this copy was made. Neither has been added here as a person or place connected with the copy; this should be checked against the full catalogue entry.

title: Nāḍīparīkṣā
subject: Āyurveda
date_raw: Saṃvat 1773 jeṣṭhamāse dinagatā 29 vāra 1 thithau 2 nakṣatra 20 sudī saptamyāṃ sanaiścare likhitaṃ
colophon: iti samrāḍagnicit sūryadāsātmaja rāmacaṃdra somayāji kṛtaṃ sāḍyādi (!) parīkṣyāprakaraṇaṃ samāptaṃ || samvat 1773 varṣe jeṣṭamāse (!) dinagatā 29 vāre 1 tithau 2 nakṣatre 2 sudī saptamyāṃ sanaiścarai (!) liṣitaṃ sāḍyādi (!) parīkṣāprakaraṇaṃ samāptaṃ || yādṛsī pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tādrisi pustakaṃ mayā yadi suddham asuddhaṃ vā mama doṣo nadīyateḥ (!) || || śrīsarasvatyai namaḥ || || śubha || || || || || || || || || ( fol.23r2-4)
notes: The scribe (Gṛhapati Jaisī), the king (prithipati sāha) and the place ('dharmmānadī taṭagrāme gorṣeśvarasthāne') are in the catalogue fields but not in the colophon quoted from fol. 23r2–4. They probably come from a part of the manuscript the cataloguer did not quote, so p3 and p4 are kept at low confidence. The catalogue's identification of the king as Pṛthvīvīravikrama Śāha (r. 1881–1911) is wrong. VS 1773 = 1716 CE, which falls in the reign of Pṛthvīpati Śāha of Gorkha (r. c. 1669–1716). 'Saṃvat' is read as VS because the copy comes from the Gorkha/Śāha milieu. The numbers 'dinagatā 29', 'vāre 1', 'tithau 2' and 'nakṣatre 2' don't fit the named day 'sudī saptamyāṃ śanaiścare' (śukla saptamī, Saturday). They may be counts of elapsed days or ghaṭīs; their meaning is unclear. The catalogue gives the nakṣatra as 20, the colophon as 2. In 'samrāḍagnicit-sūryadāsātmaja' the titles samrāṭ/agnicit grammatically belong to Sūryadāsa, but they may be meant for the author Rāmacandra. 'sāḍyādi' is a corruption of 'nāḍyādi'.

title: Jvaranirṇayavivaraṇa[ṭīkā]
subject: Āyurveda
date_raw: vasvagniṣaṭ caṃdramite ca ca śāke kujesite śrāvaṇike daśamyāṃ | [ŚS] saṃ1638 śrāvaṇa kṛṣṇa 10 maṃgalavāra
colophon: iti śrīmad vaidyakulatilakāyamāna śrīkṛṣṇapaṃḍitātmaja bhiṣaṅnārāyaṇa paṃḍita praṇītaṃ jvaranirṇaya vivaraṇaṃ samāptim agamat || || ❁ || || śrīr astu śubhaṃ bhūyat(!) || graṃthasaṃkhyā || 770 || śrāvaṇasya sitepakṣe daśamyāṃ kujavāsare alekhi mādhavenedaṃ jvaranirṇaya ṭippaṇaṃ || 1 || vasvagniṣaṭ caṃdramite ca caṇake kuje ʼsite śrāvaṇike daśamyāṃ | vyalīlikhan mādhava saṃjñako bhiṣak svapūrvaṭīkāṃ jvaranirṇayasya || 1 || śaṃbhuṃ suśruta carakau guruṃ ca nāgeśayā namya || nāyāyaṇo vivṛṇute vātaghnatvādi nirṇayaṃ svakṛtaṃ || 1 || bhiṣajāṃ paritoṣāya vātaghnatvādi nirṇayaḥ || nārāyaṇena racito nāgeśasya prasādataḥ iti ||1744
notes: The chronogram vasu (8), agni (3), ṣaṭ (6), candra (1), read right to left, gives Śaka 1638 (≈1716 CE). 'caṇake' is a corruption of 'śāke'. The pakṣa conflicts: the first verse has 'śrāvaṇasya sitepakṣe' (bright fortnight). The second verse as printed has 'kuje ʼsite', which would mean the dark fortnight, but it could equally be read 'kuje site' (bright). The catalogue gives kṛṣṇa. I have chosen śukla because the first verse states it explicitly. The trailing '1744' at the end of the extract is unexplained. It does not match the Śaka date: read as VS it would give 1687 CE, and it may be a later note or a count. 'nāyāyaṇo' should be read 'nārāyaṇo'. 'guruṃ ca nāgeśayā namya' should probably be read 'guruṃ ca nāgeśam ānamya'. Nāgeśa was the author's guru and is not connected with this copy. In 'svapūrvaṭīkāṃ', 'sv-apūrva-ṭīkāṃ' ('excellent, unprecedented commentary') is probably meant, so I have not inferred ownership by Mādhava. The 770 in 'graṃthasaṃkhyā' is the length of the text.

title: Kokamañjarī
subject: Āyurveda
colophon: iti śrī paṃḍitavaidyaka sodāsaputra nainasuṣaviracite vaidyamanotsaveṣudarapuṣyavāsabamdhyāgarbhapātapradarakuṣṭhīṣthī istrīvidhā kucavidhā liʼgavidyānirdhātaprajogapratīkāranāma saptamaḥ śamudesa (!) || (fol. 51v5-6) iti ānaṃdaviracite kokamaṃjarī saṃpūrṇṇaṃ | samāpta (!) śubhaṃ bhavamtu (!) || iti samvat 902 āśviṇa vadi 13 sukravāraṣu thāsā phocoya sidhuko juro, dhaṃju vaidyana coyā juro, śubha || || (fol.93r4-6)
notes: The colophon on fol. 51v ends the 7th samuddeśa of the Vaidyamanotsava ascribed to Nainasukha, son of Sodāsa. The colophon on fol. 93r ends the Kokamañjarī, ascribed to Ānanda. Two points are uncertain. First, the father's name 'sodāsa' may be corrupt; it could be a short form of something like Keśodāsa. Second, 'paṃḍitavaidyaka' could describe either the father or the son. 'thāsā phocoya sidhuko juro' is Newari for 'the copying is finished' (roughly 'thva saphū coyā siddhayakā julo'). It is not a place name. The catalogue gives the scribe as 'Dhuṃju', but the quoted colophon reads 'dhaṃju'; the colophon reading is kept here. The date checks out: NS 902 + 880 = 1781/82, and Āśvina at the end of the Nepal Era year falls in about September–October 1782. The weekday was not verified.

title: Ajīrṇamañjarī
subject: Āyurveda
colophon: iti śrīkāśirājaviracite ajīrṇamaṃjarī samāpti magāt || śubham || śrīrāma śitā(!)jikā caraṇa o sukirtidattaś caraṇa sadāsarvadā śubham bhūyāt || āṣāḍhike śite pakṣe bhūrāmāṅkenduvatsare || alikhat sukradattena daśami bhaumavāsare || 1 ||
notes: The year is given only by the chronogram bhūrāmāṅkendu (1-3-9-1, read in reverse = 1931). No era is named. The catalogue's 'Saṃvat 1931' and the Devanagari script suggest Vikrama Saṃvat (VS), giving c. 1874 CE. The colophon gives no place. 'śite' stands for sita, the bright fortnight (śukla). The scribe's name is written 'sukradatta'; the catalogue normalises it to Śukradatta, but 'Sukradatta' cannot be ruled out. The blessing 'śrīrāma śitā(!)jikā caraṇa o sukirtidattaś caraṇa' is mixed Sanskrit and Hindi/Nepali: '(may) the feet of Śrī Rāma and Sītājī, and the feet of Sukīrtidatta (bring blessing) always'. Sukīrtidatta is therefore honoured as a human, probably the scribe's guru or father. The colophon does not state this, so his role is left as 'other'. His name 'sukirtidattaś' may be a corruption of 'sukīrtidatta-kā'.

notes: The chronogram 'dṛṅnetracārvāha' is corrupt. Dṛk = 2 and netra = 2. The rest ('cārvāha') cannot be resolved with confidence; read right to left, the year ends in ..22. The cataloguer's Śāke 1621 is marked with a query and does not fit a reading of dṛk = 2 as the units digit. ŚS 1622 (CE c. 1700) is equally possible, and ce_approx 1699 is only approximate. Maheśa's tithi is taken as caturdaśī (Śiva's tithi), as the cataloguer does. Kavi = Śukra, so the weekday is Friday. The scribe's name 'Nārānidhi' may be a corrupt form, for example of Nārāyaṇa or Nārāṇidhi. The Āyurvedic recipe (trikaṭuka...) after the colophon is a later addition and names no persons. The author Madanapāla is the king of Kāṣṭhā who composed the text, not a reigning king at the time of copying.

colophon: iti śrīmanmanohara sūnunā gosvāmīnā harināthakṛtāyāṃ vaidyajīvanaṭīkāyāṃ paṃcamo vilāsaḥ || śrīmadbhūpati vikramābda gaṇanā khaṃ vahni sapteṃdubhir māse jeṣṭha asi saptami tithai (!) vāre bhṛgu śoriyaṃ || ṭīkā || vaidyajivanasya (!) racī (!) śrīnātha gosvāmībhir caitastvaṃṭamāsthite (!) śarapure dhāryābhiṣaghi sadā likhitaṃ brāhmaṇa saṃbhūrāmeṇa (!) likhāyataṃ cīraṃjī (!)gosvāmi bālakṛṣṇajī miti bhādrapada śuklapakṣe tithau || 2 || ravivāsare || || saṃvat ||1849 || vṛṣe śākhe || || 1714 || || śubhaṃ bhūyāt || śrīmuthareśa(!) (fol.46r1-4)
notes: The colophon also quotes the composition chronogram of the ṭīkā (VS 1730 Jyeṣṭha kṛṣṇa 7, composed by 'Śrīnātha Gosvāmin', likely an alternate/abbreviated form for Harinātha Gosvāmin). The copy date gives both VS 1849 and ŚS 1714.

title: Rugviniścaya
subject: Āyurveda
colophon: iti śrīmādhavakaraviracitarugviniścayaḥ saṃgrahaḥ saṃpūrṇaḥ || ||… saṃvat 1848 mīṭī (!) māgha vadī 2 vāra budhavāra || || kāśyāṃ madhye || || śrīrāmacaṃdrāya namaḥ || śrīkṛṣṇāya namaḥ || śrīgopālo jayati || śrīhanumataye || śrīlakṣmī najīāya(!)namaḥ || ❁ ❁ ❁ śrī śrī rājārāmacaṃdrāya nama (!) || || (fol. 92v6-93r1)
notes: The catalogue gives the scribe as Kṛṣṇadāsa, but that name is not in the quoted colophon. It may be in the part left out at the ellipsis '…'. Because it can't be checked, Kṛṣṇadāsa is not added as a person. The era is not named. VS is assumed because the copy was made in Kāśī and because of the year range. The CE year is given as 1792, not 1791 (VS−57), because Māgha of VS 1848 (counting the year from Caitra) falls in early 1792. 'mīṭī' is Nepali miti, meaning 'date'. 'śrīlakṣmī najīāya(!)' is probably a corruption of Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa. That name, and Rāmacandra, Kṛṣṇa, Gopāla, Hanumat and 'rājārāmacaṃdra', are deities in the closing invocations, not people.
review: ce_approx changed from 1791 to 1792. VS 1848 began in Caitra 1791, so Māgha vadī 2 of that year falls in January or February 1792. The simple VS−57 formula gives 1791.
Notes expanded: the scribe name in the catalogue cannot be verified, 'mīṭī' is the Nepali word miti, and the invocations name deities, not people.

notes: Vijayarakṣaka is a scribal variant for Vijayarakṣita, the well-known commentator on the Mādhavanidāna (Madhukoṣavyākhyā). The four-digit year 1765 in Devanagari script is likely Vikrama Saṃvat (1708 CE).

title: Śāraṅgadharasaṃhitā
subject: Āyurveda
colophon: iti śrīśārṅgadharacikitsā samāpta(!)|| śrībhavānīśaṃkarābhyāṃ namaḥ || śubham astu || 6 || śrīkalyāṇam astu || mohanajibhahālajamiṭhālahena svārthaṃ paropakārārthaṃ śārṅadharākhyaṃ pustakaṃ yal likhitaṃ tat śrīmatkāśyāṃ kṣayasavatsare pauṣamāsi śuklapakṣe trītiyāyāṃ(!) samāptaṃ || || śubhaṃ bhavatu || śrīsadāśivārpaṇam astu (fol.155r6-11)
notes: The scribe's name is a single instrumental compound (-ena) and is probably corrupt or a vernacular (Hindi/Gujarati/Marwari) name. One possible segmentation is Mohanajī + bhahā(?) + lālaja (born of Lāla?) + Miṭhālā(la), with miṭhālahena perhaps an error for miṭhālālena. This would make the scribe one Mīṭhālāla, possibly identified through Mohanajī or Lāla(jī), but the segmentation is uncertain, so the full string is kept as the name. The year is given only as the Jovian saṃvatsara Kṣaya, without a numbered era. Under southern reckoning, Pauṣa of a Kṣaya year falls around Dec–Jan 1866/67, 1926/27, and so on (1986/87 is too late for this collection), so ce_approx is left empty. The book was copied at Kāśī, not in Nepal. Both svārthaṃ and paropakārārthaṃ are stated, so the scribe is treated as both scribe and owner.
review: Place normalized to 'Vārāṇasī' (schema form) instead of 'Varanasi'.

Scribe name confidence lowered to low; notes expanded with a possible segmentation (the final element looks like the common western-Indian name Mīṭhālāla, with miṭhālahena possibly a corruption of miṭhālālena).
Date year field clarified as Kṣaya, the 60th year of the 60-year Jovian cycle. Possible CE dates are listed in notes; ce_approx is left empty because no era is given.
Persons (author Śārṅgadhara; scribe+owner from svārthaṃ), relations (none), tithi/month/pakṣa confirmed.

title: Haramekhalā
subject: Āyurveda
colophon: || śrī śāke 1629 māse 7 tithau 30 vāsare 3 dinagatā 13 litaṃ (12\u2 2 1 dha 4ī) rmmaṇāḥ || tailādrakṣe jalādrakṣedrakṣe[t] śītalabandhanāt || mūrkhahaste nadātavyaṃ rvaṃ(!) vadati pustakāt(!) || bhagnapṛṣṭī(!) kaṭī grīvā vadhū(!) dṛṣṭiradhomukhaṃ || kaṣṭēna likhitaṃ graṃthaṃ yatnenaḥ paripālayet || śubhaṃ || || rāma rāmeti rāmeti rame rāme manorame || sahastra(!) nāmatā tulyaṃ rāmanāma varānaṇe (!) || || (fol.117v5-118r2)
notes: The scribe's name is garbled in the catalogue: 'litaṃ (12\u2 2 1 dha 4ī) rmmaṇāḥ'. 'litaṃ' is probably 'li[khi]taṃ' and 'rmmaṇāḥ' is the end of '-śarmaṇā', an instrumental with a stray visarga. So the scribe was a brahmin whose name contains something like 'dha' and 'ī'. The name itself cannot be recovered. 'dinagatā 13' may mean day 13 of a solar month, which would make month 7 = Tulā. It may instead mean 13 ghaṭikās elapsed. Month numbering is therefore ambiguous. ŚS 1629 = 1707 CE. This matches the catalogue field, but the date has not been checked against an ephemeris. The verses after the date ('tailād rakṣe…', 'bhagnapṛṣṭhakaṭīgrīvā…', 'rāma rāmeti…') are stock scribal verses. They name no persons.
review: p1 name: removed the caste/brahmin suffix śarman from the name field, which now records the name as illegible; śarman is kept only in titles.
Date: 'month 7' is only a number. It is Āśvina if months are counted from Caitra, or the solar month Tulā if counted from Meṣa. Both are recorded in the month field and notes.
Date: weekday 3 is now marked as uncertain (Tuesday only if counting starts with Sunday = 1).
Notes: explained the garbled name, 'dinagatā 13' and the stock verses that follow.

title: Jvaratimirabhāskara
subject: Āyurveda
colophon: iti kāyasthacuṃḍakṛte, jvaratimirabhāskare jvaropadravacikitsā(3)paripūrṇṇatā nāma ṣoḍaśo dhyāyaḥ || || samāpto yaṃ jvaratimirabhāskaro nā(4)ma graṃthaḥ || || rasāṣṭavasbhir llakṣye, yāte nepālahāyane || māghe māsy aśite pakṣe, dvādaśyāṅ guruvāsa(5)re || jvarastimirahaṃsākhyaṃ, (!) raṃmyāsyākhyena (!) dhīmatāḥ (!) || vyalekhīdaṃ hitārthāya, sutārthaṃ jagatā (!) mudā || || (158r1) atha nepālabhākhā || samvat 886 māghakṛṣṇayā dvādasi,(!) bṛhaspatīvāra thva kuhnu vaidya bhinakhvāra(2)na, thva jvarastimirabhāskara (!) nāma grantha coya sidhakādina, thvaverasa, gorakhārina, kiṃdosa, segu(3)sa, hnuti sathā nātayāo edeśa sagheraya, yāṅāḍo dukhaviyāo tao juro || || śubha || || (fol. 157v2-158r3)
purpose: hitārthāya, sutārthaṃ jagatāṃ mudā: for the benefit (of the world) and for his son's sake (reading uncertain)
notes:
The chronogram rasa (6), aṣṭa (8), vasu (8), read right to left, gives NS 886. This matches 'samvat 886' in the Newari part. Māgha kṛṣṇa of NS 886 falls in early 1766 CE. The weekday was not checked by calculation.

The Sanskrit verse names the scribe 'ramyāsya' (corrupt 'raṃmyāsyākhyena dhīmatāḥ'). This is a Sanskrit rendering of the Newari name Bhinakhvāra: bhina = good/beautiful, khvāra = face. The '-na' in 'bhinakhvārana' is the Newari ergative ending.

The Newari note says the copy was finished at a time of hardship: the Gorkhalis set up posts at Kindol (kiṃdosa) and Segu (segusa, probably the Svayambhū area) and surrounded the country. This fits the Gorkha siege of the Kathmandu Valley in 1766.

The catalogue gives Yoginīpattana as the place and Rājamalla as the king. Neither appears in the quoted colophon, so both are left empty here. Also, in NS 886 Kathmandu was ruled by Jayaprakāśa Malla, so the catalogue's king field is doubtful.

'sutārthaṃ' could mean 'for his son'. No son is named, and no owner is stated.

title: Nakulacikitsā
subject: Aśvāyurveda
colophon: iti nakula cikitsite aśvaśālā kathanaṃ nāma ṣoḍaśodhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || || śāke 1553 tathā saṃvat 1688 pravarttamāne śrāvaṇakṛṣṇaikādaśyāṃ 11 jīvavāsare śālihotrasya pustakaṃ samāptaṃ || || ādarśa doṣānmati vibhramādvā tvarā viśeṣāllikhanasya vegāt | tanmārjjayitvā pariśodhayaṃtī kṣamaṃ tu saṃtaḥ khalu lekhakasya ||| śubhaṃ || || oṃ || rāmāya namaḥ || || || śrī śrī sumati jayajitāmitramalladevasana thva pustaka dayakā, bhāgirāma paramānayāvelasa, saṃvat 810 kārtika śudi 9 (fol.27r1-7)
notes: The colophon has two dates. (1) An inherited date, probably from the exemplar: śāke 1553 tathā saṃvat 1688, Śrāvaṇa kṛṣṇa 11, jīvavāsara (Thursday). Śaka 1553 + 78 = 1631 and VS 1688 − 57 = 1631, so the two eras agree (July/Aug 1631 CE). (2) The date of this copy: NS 810 Kārtika śukla 9, about Oct/Nov 1689 CE. That falls within Jitāmitra Malla's reign at Bhaktapur (1673–1696). 'śālihotrasya pustakaṃ' names the text tradition (Śālihotra, the hippiatric author), not a person connected with this copy. The catalogue lists Bhāgīrāma as scribe, but 'bhāgirāma paramānayāvelasa' only dates the copy to 'the time when Bhāgīrāma was pramāṇa/pradhāna (minister)'. Bhāgīrāma is known as a pradhāna of Bhaktapur under Jitāmitra Malla. The scribe is not named. The place of copying is not stated, though Bhaktapur is likely from the king.
review: p1: name changed to the standard regnal stem 'Jitāmitramalladeva'. 'sumati jaya' is part of the royal style, so it moves to titles. Roles king + commissioner kept: 'thva pustaka dayakā' means 'had this book made'.

p2 Bhāgīrāma: the vague role 'other' is removed and only 'minister' is kept. 'paramāna' is read as pramāṇa/pradhāna, an office title. He is not the scribe, so the catalogue's 'Scribe' field is wrong. Confidence raised to high because the Newari is clear.
Date: ce_approx changed from 1690 to 1689. NS 810 began in Kārtika 1689, so Kārtika śukla 9 of NS 810 falls in Oct/Nov 1689.

Notes: confirmed that Śaka 1553 and VS 1688 agree (both 1631 CE) and that jīvavāsara means Thursday. 'Śālihotra' is noted as a text title, not a person. Added that the place is not stated but Bhaktapur is implied by the king.
Purpose filled in: commissioned by the king.

colophon: iti nānāgraṃthasamuccayam aśvaśāstraṃ samāptaṃ || śrī śrīsumati jayajitāmitramalladevasana thva pustaka dayakā || bhāgīrāma pradhāṃnāṃgayā velasa saṃvat 810 kārttika sudi 9 || || (fol.82r4-6)
notes: The catalogue lists Bhāgīrāma Pradhānāṅga as the scribe. But 'bhāgīrāma pradhāṃnāṃgayā velasa' means 'in the time of Bhāgīrāma the pradhānāṅga (chief minister)'. It dates the copy to his term in office and does not name him as scribe. The colophon names no scribe. King Jitāmitra Malla of Bhaktapur (r. c. 1673–1696) had the book made ('thva pustaka dayakā'). This makes Bhaktapur a likely place of copying, but the colophon does not say so. NS years begin with Kārttika, so NS 810 Kārttika śukla 9 corresponds to about Oct/Nov 1689 CE. The relation p2→p1 has been changed from under_reign_of to servant_of. That is a judgment call; he is a minister of the reigning king.

title: Aśvavaidyakaśāstra
subject: Aśvāyurveda
colophon: mahāsāmanta śrījayadatta kṛtam aśvavaidyakaśāstraḥ samāptaḥ || (!) yādṛśaṃ pustaṃ dṛstvā (!) tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mama | (!) yadi suddhamasuddhaṃ (!) vā mama doṣo nadīyateḥ (!) || || jayadattanāma pustakaṃ śrī śrīhemantamalla varmanā svakarena likhitam idaṃ saṃpūrṃ || || samvat 807 phālguṇa māse śuklapakṣe navamyāṃ thithau rohinī (!) nakṣatre viskambhayoge vṛhaspativāsare thva kuhnu saṃpūrṇa yāṅādi juroṃ || śrī śrī śrī revantasuprasaṃnostu || śubham astu || (fol.48v1–4)
notes: The era is not named in the colophon ('samvat 807'), but the Newari script and Newari text make Nepal Saṃvat certain. Phālguna of NS 807 falls in about February–March 1687 CE. In the colophon the scribe's name is 'śrī śrīhemantamalla varmanā', which the catalogue gives as 'Hemanatalāla varmmā'. I follow the colophon text and read the name as Hemantamalla, with varman as a surname or title. The name could also be split as Hemanta Malla Varmā, so confidence is medium. 'jayadattanāma pustakaṃ' means the book is called after its author Jayadatta; it does not name an owner. The Newari line 'thva kuhnu saṃpūrṇa yāṅādi juroṃ' says the copy was completed on that day. Revanta, named in the closing invocation, is a deity and is left out. Rohiṇī on śukla navamī of Phālguna is a little early for that tithi (Mṛgaśiras or Ārdrā would be more usual), so the nakṣatra may be slightly off. I have not checked it by calculation.
review: Weekday normalized from 'vṛhaspativāsara' to 'bṛhaspativāra (Thursday)'; as_written left unchanged
Nakṣatra spelling normalized to Rohiṇī, yoga to Viṣkambha
Notes expanded: explains the varman title, the CE reckoning for Phālguna, the Newari completion formula, and why the Revanta invocation is excluded

title: Nakulacikitsā
subject: Aśvāyurveda
colophon: iti nakulacikitsite aśvaśālākathanaṃ nāma śoḍaśo ʼdhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || || (fol.89v1–2) śrī śrīhemantamallanatha[[va]]tā nimirttina (!) dayakā || kayaṃgalana pitāṃ viya mate va || mahādullaṃbha vastu || samvat 799 māghamāsa śukla pakṣa śrīpañcamyāṃ tithau revatī nakṣetre gurudine || śubham astu sarvvadā || (fol.89v5–7)
purpose: for his own sake (thavatā nimittina); sons are told not to give it away
notes: The Newari reads: 'śrī śrī Hemantamalla-na thava-tā nimittina dayakā' = 'made by Hemantamalla for his own sake'. 'nimirttina (!)' stands for nimittina. The cataloguer's [[va]] is an inserted akṣara, giving thavatā. 'dayakā' (made, had made) usually marks the person who had a copy produced, so commissioner + owner is the more likely reading. The catalogue calls him the scribe, though, and dayakā alone does not rule that out. 'kayaṃgalana pitāṃ viya mate va || mahādullaṃbha vastu' = '[my] sons must not give it out(side); [it is] a very rare object'. The double śrī suggests a royal or noble person, but he is not called king, and no Malla ruler of that name reigned in NS 799 (Pārthivendra in Kathmandu, Śrīnivāsa in Patan, Jitāmitra in Bhaktapur). He may have been a prince or a member of the nobility. Date: NS 799 + 880 = 1678/79; Māgha śukla 5 (Vasanta/Śrīpañcamī) falls in Jan/Feb 1679 CE. Revatī as the nakṣatra is astronomically plausible for that tithi; the weekday has not been checked.

as_written changed to show the full ergative phrase segmented as hemantamallana thavatā
weekday normalised to Thursday (gurudine); tithi normalised to pañcamī (Śrīpañcamī)

title: Śālihotra
subject: Aśvāyurveda
colophon: || ❖ saṃvat 806 āṣāḍhaśukla saptamī śukravāra thva kuhnu, sohnemhavantā dvija śrīdevaśaṃkaraṇa (!), thva ṣaḍaṃśāstra (!) coya dhunakā dina joro śubham || revantāya namonamaḥ || || ○ || || saṃºº 902 phālguṇa śukla caturthī thva kuhnu śrīlakṣmīpati ju oṃ rāyā agnihotra mākasa śrīlakṣṃīśvarī agnihotrī sativana; thvana hṅāsati oṃ sivamadū(!) (fol. 9v4–8)
purpose: "Not stated. The closing 'dina joro' (perhaps 'given/offered'?) is unclear."
notes: The catalogue gives the scribe as Bhavāniśaṃkara, but the colophon reads 'dvija śrīdevaśaṃkaraṇa (!)', i.e. Devaśaṃkara in the Newari agentive. The cataloguer's (!) may mean that the name is doubtful. 'sohnemhavantā' before 'dvija' is unclear. It could be a place or epithet, or a misreading. 'ṣaḍaṃśāstra (!)' is probably a corruption, perhaps of ṣaḍaṅga-śāstra or a name for the Śālihotra text. A second, later note dated NS 902 (≈ CE 1782), Phālguna śukla 4, records an event involving Lakṣmīpati, apparently his death. It also records that Lakṣmīśvarī, the agnihotrī who kept the agnihotra, became sati; 'thvana hṅāsati ... sivamadū' perhaps means 'five days after this ... died'. This note says nothing about the copying, and these persons may be later owners or their family. The NS 806 weekday has not been verified.

Added p2 Lakṣmīpati and p3 Lakṣmīśvarī from the later note dated NS 902. Both are recorded in the manuscript, possibly as owners' family, so they get role 'other' with low confidence.
Added a wife_of relation for Lakṣmīśvarī and Lakṣmīpati, inferred from the sati context (low certainty).

title: Karaṭikautuka
subject: Gajāyurveda
colophon: || iti śrīkāyastha balabhadrātmajagopāladāsaviracite karaṭikautuke nakhataḥ sādhyā ʼsādhyanakhottamalakṣaṇa dvijamukhajātilakṣaṇāraṇyadantisādhukaraṇa hastivāhana hastisaṃkīrṇajātidaṃtidoṣakharaśītalīkaraṇa jalodgārajāṭharanāḍīsvaraviśeṣalakṣaṇa viṣacikitsā hasticakragajapraśaṃsā gajalūtākavacādikas tṛtīya ullāsaḥ | | samāpto ʼyaṃ karaṭikautukanāmā graṃthaḥ || || abde nāmgayugāṃgaśītakiraṇe 1648 taiṣetithau pakṣatau 1 kṛṣṇāyā minavāsare mṛgaśiraḥ sādhyollasat kaulave saṃpūrṇaṃ kṛtavān ayaṃ gajahitāyājñām avāpyāvanī pālādeḥ karikautukaṃ balisuto gopālanāmā ʼvanau || 1 || na sthāyi caṃcalaṃ varṣma tanujānām iha kṣitau cirasthāyyakṣaraṃ jñātvā ʼkarot karaṭikautukam || 2 || nindantu durjanāḥ sarve stutiṃ kurvaṃtu sajjanāḥ samam evāṃjaliṃ tebhyo badhvā ʼkāri dvipākṣaram || 3 || śubham || likhitaṃ jagannāthena śrīmad raṇabahādūrasenārthaṃ | śubhaṃ | (fol.54r1–9)
notes: The only date in the colophon is in the author's verse (saṃpūrṇaṃ kṛtavān ... gopālanāmā). The chronogram nāga 8, yuga 4, aṅga 6, śītakiraṇa 1, read right to left, gives 1648, which matches the numerals. So 1648 is when Gopāladāsa finished composing the text, not when this copy was made. The catalogue's 'Date of Copying: SAM 1648' is therefore probably wrong, and this copy is undated and must be later than 1648. No era is named: VS 1648 would be about 1591 CE and ŚS 1648 about 1726 CE, so ce_approx is left empty. 'kṛṣṇāyā minavāsare' is read as 'kṛṣṇāyām inavāsare' (Sunday). 'balisuto' in the verse is taken as a short form of Balabhadra's son. The king whose permission the author obtained (ājñām avāpyāvanīpālāt) is not named. Raṇabahādūrasena, for whom Jagannātha copied the manuscript, is presumably a Sena ruler; the catalogue gives 'King: Raṇabahādura'. The colophon gives him no royal title, so he is recorded as beneficiary only. He may also have commissioned the copy, but the colophon does not say so.

p2 Balabhadra: title 'kāyastha' removed. The colophon applies it only to Gopāladāsa.
p1: evidence extended with the verse's 'balisuto gopālanāmā', which supports the father relation.

title: Vājalakṣaṇa
subject: Śyenāyurveda
colophon: navadalananagacaṃdrais 1729 saṃmite śrīśakābde dinakara kriyasaṃsthe kṛṣṇapakṣe navamyāṃ || suragurudivasesmin vājahotraṃ sugopyaṃ likhati śivanṛsiṃhaś caikadantaprasādāt śubhaṃ || (fol. 11v3–4)
notes: The era is given explicitly as Śaka (śrīśakābde 1729), so the date is ŚS 1729 = 1807 CE (April–May, with the sun in Aries). The catalogue's 'SAM 1729' is misleading: read as Vikrama it would give 1672 CE. Chronogram: 'navadalananagacaṃdrais' = nava (9), dala(na) (2; probably a corruption of nayana = 2), naga (7), candra (1); read right to left this gives 1729, which matches the numeral. 'kriya' is the zodiac name for Aries (Meṣa). The text calls itself 'vājahotra', but the catalogue title is Vājalakṣaṇa. The name could also be read as two words, Śiva Nṛsiṃha.
review: No substantive changes. Notes now explain the chronogram (nava 9, dala/nayana 2, naga 7, candra 1; read right to left as 1729) and that 'dinakara kriyasaṃsthe' gives a solar month (sun in Aries), not a lunar month name.

This is most likely a corrupt or misread Newari phrase, perhaps for '(sa) coyakā juro' ('was caused to be written' / 'had it copied'), and not a personal name, so no scribe can be identified. The era is not stated: 'saṃvat 766' with a Newari phrase and Newari script means Nepāla Saṃvat. 'aiji 3' is probably a weekday notation (3 = Tuesday), but the meaning of 'aiji' is unclear. subject: Purāṇa
date_raw: samvat 786 caitrakṛ trayodaśī pra caturdaśyān tithau revatī pra aśvinī nakṣatra ādityavāra
colophon: iti kālikāpurāṇaṃ samāptaṃ || || samvat 786 caitrakṛ trayodaśī pra caturdaśyān tithau revatī pra aśvinī nakṣatra ādityavāra (tho kuhnū dhunakājuro) || || [[śrīharivaṃśanāthavatacocaka || ]]
notes: The Newari '(tho kuhnū dhunakājuro)' means 'finished on this day' (tho kunhu dhunakā juro), so the date is the completion date. The name and role are inside the cataloguer's [[ ]] brackets: '[[śrīharivaṃśanāthavatacocaka || ]]'. This passage may be in a later hand or a doubtful reading, so it is uncertain whether it belongs to the original colophon. The segmentation of the name is unclear. 'vata' might be a corrupt case ending or particle (Newari ergative -na/-naṃ?), or it might be part of the name. 'cocaka' is probably a corrupt Newari verb from coy- ('to write'). If it stands for coyā ('wrote'), Harivaṃśanātha is the scribe. If it stands for coyakā ('had written'), he is the commissioner. The scribe role is tentative. Date: no era is given, but 'samvat 786' in Newari script is taken as NS, so 786 + 880 gives about 1666 CE (Caitra kṛṣṇa, around March/April 1666). The weekday and nakṣatra have not been checked against an ephemeris.

With the sun in Makara this is about January 1641 CE. This conflicts with the stated reign of Jagatprakāśamalla of Bhaktapur, who acceded c. NS 764 / 1644 CE. Either śiśu stands for a different number, the year is misread, or the king is named anachronistically. The weekday was not checked. The locatives dīnādhināthe kamanīyavarṇe deśapradhāne sukṛtaikarāśau grammatically continue the king's epithets. Still, 'deśapradhāna' might be meant for Dhanasiṃha, who could be a pradhāna (minister); if so, his role may be 'minister' as well. The scribe's name is marked (!) by the cataloguer: 'Kutu' is doubtful, possibly Kuṭu or Khuṭu. The text copied is the Kāśīkhaṇḍa of the Skandapurāṇa.
