title: Viṣṇupurāṇa and Vaiṣṇavākūṭacandrikāṭīkā
subject: Purāṇa
colophon: [Mūla] iti śrīviṣṇupurāṇe pārāśarasaṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭheṃ ʼśe ʼṣṭamodhyāyaḥ || || 8 || samāptaṃ cedaṃ śrīviṣṇupurāṇaṃ śubham || (fol.409r7) [Ṭīkā] iti śrīratnagarbhabhaṭṭācāryaracitāyāṃ śrīmadvaiṣṇavākūṭacandrikāyāṃ ṣaṣṭheṃśe ʼṣṭamodhyāyaḥ || || varṣe śailasaripatībharajanīkāṃtair mite tīkṣṇagau kanyārāśim upāgate ʼmaladale some vivasvattithau || svasti śrīyuvabhūpater likhitavān viṣṇoḥ purāṇaṃbahā- dūrasyā ʼvanidevajaḥ śivanidhir nāmājñayā prabhoḥ || 1 || yuvarājavareṇa ropiteyaṃ janatāyāṃ karuṇakaṭākṣasekaiḥ || karuṇāvaruṇālayena tūrṇaṃ tarūṇām apy adhunā vidhīyatām || 2 || || ❁ || || || || ❁ || || || || ❁ || || || || || || || || || || (fol.409r8-11)
purpose: copied by order of the yuvabhūpati Bahādur
notes: The chronogram reads śaila 7, saritpati 4, ibha 8, rajanīkānta 1; read right to left, this gives 1847. The colophon does not name an era. VS is inferred because the date (1790 CE) fits the Gorkhā court of Bahādur. Śaka 1847 (1925 CE) would not fit. Tīkṣṇagu (the Sun) in Kanyā, the bright fortnight (amaladala) and Monday (soma) point to amānta Āśvina śukla. 'Vivasvattithi' is ambiguous. As a number-word, vivasvat = 12 (dvādaśī). As the tithi ruled by Sūrya, it would be 7 (saptamī). A rough mean-lunation calculation puts the new moon at about 8 Sept 1790 and the Kanyā saṅkrānti at about 13 Sept. On that basis Monday 20 Sept 1790 falls on or near śukla 12, while saptamī (14–15 Sept) falls on a Tuesday or Wednesday. So 12 is preferred, but this is not verified with exact tables. Who 'yuvabhūpati Bahādur' is remains uncertain. It is most likely the regent Bahādur Śāha (Pṛthvīnārāyaṇ's son, regent 1785–94). However, 'yuvabhūpati' could also mean the young king Raṇa Bahādur Śāha, who was about 15 in 1790. The catalogue is wrong to call Avanideva the scribe and Śivanidhi the donor. The text says Śivanidhi, son of Avanideva (avanidevajaḥ), copied the book by order of the prince. Verse 2 is a benedictory verse to the yuvarāja. The compound 'purāṇaṃbahādūrasyā' is a word-division artefact: purāṇaṃ + bahādūrasya.

notes: The text reads 'dvivedinā kānhajīkena vā someśvareṇa'. 'someśvareṇa' is in the instrumental case like the scribe's name. That allows three readings: (a) a second name for the scribe ('Kānhajī alias Someśvara'); (b) a corrupt place reference such as 'vā(stavyena) someśvare', meaning 'resident of Someśvara', which is what the catalogue's place field suggests; (c) a second scribe, which is least likely. I recorded one scribe and gave Someśvara as a possible residence or place. The word 'bhavatyāṃ(!)' is corrupt and unclear. 'Kavi' is a standard name for Śukra, so the weekday is Friday. I did not check that weekday against VS 1775 Bhādrapada pūrṇimā (about August/September 1718 CE). The date is in Vikrama saṃvat, which fits a Devanagari manuscript from outside Nepal; the name 'Kānhajī' and the Gujarati/Rajasthani title 'dvivedī' point the same way.

Place: entered 'someśvareṇa' as the possible place of copying (the catalogue gives Someśvara). Left the modern identification empty.
Weekday: kavi- is a name of Śukra (Venus), so kavivāsara means Friday. The (!) is probably unnecessary.

notes: The closing verse is an ownership statement: '[let] the world know [this] book [belongs to] the learned, wise Viśvanātha, son of the grandson of Ananta whose upanāma is Rāma(vvupta)'. The compound 'rāma(vvupto)panāmaka' marks Rāma(vvupta) as Ananta's upanāma (family name or surname). The cataloguer's reading is uncertain: it could be Rāmagupta, or a misreading of something like 'Rāmabhaṭṭa'. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Rāmagupta?' seems to come from this word. The colophon names no scribe; Viśvanātha is named only as owner, and that does not prove he copied it. There is no date and no place.
review: Added Ananta's upanāma (family name) 'Rāma(vvupta)', a corrupt reading, to his titles. The catalogue's 'Rāmagupta?' scribe comes from this word, which names a family, not a scribe.
Relation p1→p2 kept as 'other' but made precise: Viśvanātha is Ananta's great-grandson ('pautraputra' = son of a grandson).
Corrected Ananta's as_written to the compound substring 'upanāmakānaṃta' and widened the evidence.
Expanded the notes on the corrupt upanāma and on the missing scribe and date.

title: Nepālavaṃśāvalī
subject: Itihāsa
colophon: yo vasāvari naka vahila atha nanivasnyā (!) ranavirasiṃha vānā inakā putra. harṣa bahādūraḥ ina ikā manasuvāle yo vaṃsāvari vanāyāḥ yo vaṃsāvari leṣanyāḥ pīvahālako pātravaṃsubābu manirājale yo vaṃsāvari lekhidiyā yo vaṃsāvari kasaile lobhanagarnū nepāli saṃvat 1030 miti+++++++siddha bhayo - - suubha (!) - (fol. 71v8–11)
purpose: made at the wish of Harṣabahādura
notes: The colophon is in Nepali. The month and day after 'miti' are lost. NS 1030 corresponds to 1909/10 CE, which agrees with the catalogue's 'SAM 1030'. 'vānā' is probably Bānā/Bare, the Newar Buddhist caste name. 'ina ikā manasuvāle' (read inikā, honorific 'by their wish') most likely refers to Harṣabahādura, though father and son together may be meant. 'pātravaṃsubābu' is obscure; it could be a surname or epithet, or a reference to Manirāja's father. Naka Bahila (Nakabahil) and Pīvahāla (Pim Bahal) are both localities in Patan. No place of copying is stated explicitly, but the scribe lived at Pīvahāla. The colophon ends with an imprecation against coveting the book ('kasaile lobha nagarnū').

title: Amarakośa
subject: Kośa
colophon: śrīśāke saṃmvat (!) 1743 || saṃmvat (!) 1878 || nipālasaṃmvat (!) 941 mti hāgruna || sivarātri (7) khunu saṃpūnūna julā suja || likhitaṃ bhājumana vaide || (unu) torako || robhagalyā maṃcce māhāryāpa ||| (8)subhaṃ || ❁ | ❁ || ❁ || jadi sudhorasudho vā. mama dokha na diaite (!) || ❁ || (fol. 72v6-8)
notes: The colophon gives three eras, and all three agree: ŚS 1743 (+78), VS 1878 (−57) and NS 941 (+880) each give 1821 CE. Phālguna Śivarātri falls around February–March 1821. 'saṃpūnūna julā' is Newari for 'was completed'. The phrase '(unu) torako || robhagalyā maṃcce māhāryāpa' is obscure. It may contain a locality (a ṭola?) or a further statement about the scribe or the copy, but no person or place can be read from it with confidence. The closing line 'jadi sudhorasudho vā. mama dokha na diaite' is a Nepali scribal formula meaning 'whether correct or incorrect, do not blame me'. 'vaide' is read as the caste name Vaidya. The catalogue fields (scribe Bhājumana Vaidya, ŚS 1743) agree with this reading.
review: Date: added implied pakṣa 'kṛṣṇa' and glossed the tithi as caturdaśī (Śivarātri); the colophon itself names only the festival
Notes: confirmed that the three eras agree on 1821 CE; glossed 'saṃpūnūna julā' and the scribe's closing formula; kept the obscure phrase unresolved

title: Amarakośa vyākhyā dīpikākhyā
subject: Kośa
colophon: iti śrī dāṇIṇātya śiromaṇībhūta citta pāvana śrī mukuṃda bhaṭṭātmajaḥ śrī viśvanāthabhaṭṭāṃ ghrilaghavidhyena śrī manmahārādhirājapārvata viṣayādhipa śrī trivikramasena pramvāśritena pāṃḍe ityupanāmaka viracitāyāmamaradīpikāyāṃ mamarasiṃhakṛta nāmaliṃgānuśāsana paṃjikāyāṃ tṛtīyaḥ kāṇḍaḥ saṃpūrṇaḥ śubham śrī śāke 1727 māse 6 likhitamidaṃ pustakaṃ rupanārāyaṇātmaja revatīramaṇa śarmaṇā śubham gokhuragrāme (fol. 97v10-98r4 )
notes: Corrupt readings: 'dāṇIṇātya' = dākṣiṇātya; 'viśvanāthabhaṭṭāṃ ghrilaghavidhyena' = viśvanāthabhaṭṭāṅghrilabdhavidyena ('who gained learning at the feet of Viśvanātha Bhaṭṭa'); 'manmahārādhirāja' = śrīmanmahārājādhirāja; 'pramvāśritena' probably = prabhvāśritena ('dependent on [his] lord'). The commentator of the Amaradīpikā is named only by his surname Pāṇḍe. He is described as a Cittapāvana (Chitpavan) brahmin of the South, son of Mukunda Bhaṭṭa and pupil of Viśvanātha Bhaṭṭa. Strictly, the Cittapāvana epithet qualifies the father inside the compound, and the commentator is assumed to share it. Trivikramasena, overlord of Parvata, was the commentator's patron. His role is recorded as 'other', not reigning king of this copy, although the catalogue field lists him as King. The colophon does not show whether he was still ruling in ŚS 1727 (c. 1805 CE). The scribe Revatīramaṇa, son of Rūpanārāyaṇa, copied the manuscript at Gokhuragrāma, which is not identified.
review: p4 Trivikramasena: role changed from 'king' to 'other'. He is the patron of the commentator ('prabhvāśritena', read as prabhu-āśritena), not a ruler shown to be reigning when this copy was made in ŚS 1727. The catalogue field 'King' likely carries over the composition-time patron.
Relation p1→p4 changed from under_reign_of to servant_of (the commentator was a dependant of the king).
p6 Revatīramaṇa: removed residence 'Gokhuragrāma'. The colophon gives it only as the place of copying.
p1 confidence lowered to low: 'Pāṇḍe' is only the surname (upanāmaka), and the personal name is not given.
Notes rewritten: corrupt readings explained and typo corrected.

title: Amarakośa ( 1-3 kāṇḍa )
subject: Kośa
colophon: liṃgādi saṃgraha varggaḥ || || ityamarasiṃhakṛtau nāmaliṃgānuśāsane | sāmānyakāṇḍa stṛtīyaḥ sāṃgaeva samarthitaḥ || || samvat 784 vaiśākhaśuklaḥ paurṇṇamāsī vudhahasta likhiti saṃpūrṇṇadina || śrī 3 bhavānī śaṃkara prītirastu || śubhaṃbhavatu sarvvadā || namaḥ || (fol. 73v4-6 )
notes: The catalogue gives the scribe as 'Vudhahasta ?'. The most likely reading of 'vudhahasta likhiti saṃpūrṇṇadina' is budha(vāra), hasta-likhita, saṃpūrṇa-dina: 'Wednesday, the day the handwritten copy was completed'. Hasta as nakṣatra is ruled out because a Vaiśākha pūrṇimā cannot fall in Hasta. A less likely reading is 'written by the hand of Vudha/Budha', which would make Budha the scribe; because of that doubt no scribe is recorded. The era is not named but is assumed to be NS (the script is Newari): 784 + 880 = c. 1664 CE (April/May). The weekday has not been checked against the calendar. Bhavānī-Śaṅkara is a deity and is not recorded as a person.
review: Removed 'hasta' as nakṣatra: at a Vaiśākha full moon the moon stands near Viśākhā/Anurādhā, so Hasta (two asterisms before Citrā) is astronomically impossible here. 'vudha' is taken as Budhavāra, and 'hasta likhiti' is read as hastalikhita ('written by hand').
Date as_written now includes 'likhiti saṃpūrṇṇadina'.
Purpose reworded as a devotional dedication.
Notes expanded with the Vudha-as-scribe alternative.

notes: The scribe is not named. He calls himself the son of someone whose name ends in -svāmin: 'muninamivaryyāḥ svāmināmtaḥ' probably stands for something like 'munivarya-svāmi-nāmnaḥ'. The father's name, read here as Munivaryasvāmin, is corrupt and uncertain. The verse gives a date of Nabhas (Śrāvaṇa), dark fortnight, Saturday, with a corrupt tithi word 'sarajvana'. This is probably a corrupt tithi name, or possibly a chronogram, and cannot be resolved. The prose date is saṃvat 1863 Vaiśākha kṛṣṇa 13, so the two dates give different months. They may mark different stages of the work, or one of them may be copied over from the exemplar. The era is taken as Vikrama, since this is a Devanagari manuscript and the place is Vārāṇasī (VS 1863 ≈ 1806 CE); the era itself is not stated. 'śrīviśvanāthopakaṇṭhe' means near the Viśvanātha temple, i.e. Vārāṇasī. 'śrīraviḥ prīyatām' is an invocation of the god, not a person.
review: Scribe: 'Svāmin' is not the scribe's name. The text says the copy was written 'svāmināmtaḥ (= °svāmināmnaḥ?) sutena', i.e. by the son of a man called …svāmin. The scribe is now recorded without a name (p2), and the father is added as p3 (relative_only), with his name read tentatively as Munivaryasvāmin.
Added relation p2 son_of p3.

title: Nepālamāhātmya
subject: Mahātmya
colophon: iti skandapurā(4)ṇe himavatkhaṇḍe nepāla[[māhā]]tmye triṃśodhyāyaḥ || || śākābde siṃdhubājīdharaṇi ca dharayute, (!) kārttike kṛṣṇapakṣe, paṃcamyāṃ sādhyajoge, (!) ruru(5)śira ca ravau saṃcitaṃ dharmaheto (!) | vyākhyārthaṃ devidāsa dvijakulasumaṇeḥ pūjyapujāṃ prayatnā,l lekho 'yaṃ parśurāmo hariharakathāṃ pustakaṃ santayo(6)gyaṃ || || yatrāste śaṃkaro devo, vāgmatī yatra nimnagā | naipālasaṃbhavaṃvāṇīṃ sthāpitaṃ girijālaye || || || bhavānyai (!) prītir astu (fol. 92r3–6)
purpose: dharmahetoḥ; for Devīdāsa's exposition (vyākhyārtham); deposited (sthāpitam) in the Girijālaya by the Vāgmatī
notes: The chronogram is corrupt (dharaṇi ca dharayute). The most likely reading is sindhu(4)-vājī(7)-dharaṇidhara(8)-dharā(1), which reads right to left as ŚS 1874 = 1952 CE and matches the catalogue. If dharaṇi and dharā are each taken as 1, the year would be ŚS 1174 (1252 CE), which is implausible. The catalogue's bracketed alternative, NS 874 (1754 CE), conflicts with the explicit 'śākābde', so ŚS is kept. A 1952 copy in Newari script is late but possible. The date details (Kārttika kṛṣṇa 5 with the moon in Mṛgaśiras) fit an amānta month. Devīdāsa is described with the epithet 'dvijakulasumaṇi' (jewel of the brahmin family). He is not explicitly the commissioner. The final verse records that the book was installed in the Girijālaya (a Pārvatī shrine where Śaṅkara resides and the Vāgmatī flows, probably in the Paśupati area). This is where the book was deposited, not necessarily where it was copied, and the shrine is unidentified. bhavānyai (!) prītir astu is the closing benediction.
review: p2 name normalized to Devīdāsa (devidāsa is a short-vowel spelling); roles changed from commissioner+beneficiary to beneficiary+reader: the colophon says the copy is for his exposition (vyākhyārtham), but nothing says he had it made

chronogram resolved: sindhu=4, vājī=7, dharaṇi(dhara)=8, dharā=1, read right to left = 1874; year set to 1874 and ce_approx to 1952
place of copying emptied: girijālaye is where the book was deposited (sthāpitaṃ), not where it was copied; moved to purpose and notes
weekday written as Sunday (ravau); nakshatra/yoga field tidied

title: Nepālamāhātmya
subject: Mahātmya
colophon: || iti śrīskandapurāṇe himvatkhaṇḍe nepālamāhātmye triṃśodhyāyaḥ || || nepāle smi(4)n rudravasubhi (!) vaiśāṣakṛṣṇapakṣe aṣṭamyāyāṃ (!) tithau śatavṛṣanakṣetre (!) vaidhatiyoge (!) āditavāsare (!) vṛṣarāsiko savitari kumbharāsiko candramasi, śrī 2 bhūpālendramallasya sāmrājye, śrīke(5)śavacandrakṛta pārāvatamahāvihārāvasthita, (ṅataḍholake,) mārgapūrvabhāge, gṛhavāsinā, śrīsūryyacandrabhiunā (!) likhitaiṣā pustīti || || yādṛśaṃ...(6) guṇirjjanai || || ❁ || || || śubham astu || || || ❖ || śrīśrīśrīpaśupatiprītir astu śubha || || ❁ || ❖ || (fol. 89r3–6)
notes: The year is given as a chronogram in Nepāla (= NS) era: 'rudravasubhiḥ'. Read right to left it gives vasu = 8, then rudra = 11, so NS 811 (≈ 1691 CE). This agrees with the catalogue and falls within Bhūpālendra Malla's reign in Kathmandu (c. 1687–1700). The Moon in Kumbha fits Śatabhiṣā nakṣatra. The scribe's 'bhiunā' is a corrupt or vernacular form of bhikṣuṇā. 'gṛhavāsinā' marks him as a married (householder) monk living at Keśavacandrakṛta Pārāvata Mahāvihāra, i.e. Itum Bāhā in Kathmandu. 'ṅataḍhola' is a local Newari place name of uncertain identification. The closing benediction 'śrīśrīśrīpaśupatiprītir astu' is a blessing, not a purpose of copying. The 'yādṛśaṃ...' verse is the usual formula asking forgiveness for scribal errors.

title: Nepālamāhātmya
subject: Mahātmya
colophon: iti skandapurāṇe himvatkhaṇḍe nepālamāhātmye triśodhyāyaḥ || || nepālasmin rudravasubhiḥ vaiśāṣakṛṣṇapakṣeaṣṭamyāṃtithau śatavṛṣa nakṣetre vaidhatiyoge ādityavāsare vṛṣarāsike savitari kumbharāsiko candramasi, śrī 2 bhūpālendramallasya sāmrājye, śrī keśavacandra kṛtayārāvatamahāvihārāvasthita, ṅataḍholake, mārga pūrvabhāge, gṛhavāsinā, śrī sūryyacandrabhiunā likhitaiyāpustīti || || yādṛśaṃ ---- guṇirjjanai || || ❁ || || || śubhamastu || || || ❖ || śrī śrī śrī paśupatirastu śubha || || ❁ || ❖ || (fol. 89r3-6 )
notes: The year is given as a chronogram: rudra (11) and vasu (8), read right to left, give NS 811 (≈1691 CE). This matches the catalogue and Bhūpālendra Malla's reign. The astronomical details agree with each other: with the sun in Vṛṣa, the moon on kṛṣṇa 8 would be in Kumbha, which is where Śatabhiṣā lies. Some words are corrupt. 'kṛtayārāvata' should be (Keśavacandra)kṛta Pārāvata Mahāvihāra, which is Itum Bahal in Kathmandu. 'bhiunā' is most likely a corruption of bhikṣuṇā. 'likhitaiyāpustīti' probably stands for 'likhitam idaṃ pustakam iti'. The locality 'ṅataḍhola' is uncertain. Keśavacandra is part of the vihāra's name and is not a person connected with this copy.

title: Nepālamāhātmya
subject: Mahātmya
colophon: || iti skandapurāṇe himvatkhaṇḍe nepālamāhātmye triśodhyāyaḥ || 30 || śubhaṃ || ❖ munirandhai samudraiśca, yute nepālavatsare | bhādra ca sitapakṣetu, dvitīyāyāṃ ravaudine || daivajña cakrasiṃhena nepāla mahimā likhet || (fol. 128r4-6 )
notes: The chronogram is muni (7), randhra (9), samudra (4). Under the standard rule aṅkānāṃ vāmato gatiḥ it reads 497, i.e. NS 497 = 1377 CE (Bhādrapada falls in Aug–Sep 1377). The catalogue reads the digits in direct order as 794(!), i.e. 1674 CE. Scribes sometimes did write chronograms in direct order. A 1377 copy of the Skandapurāṇa Nepālamāhātmya would be unusually early, which makes the 794 reading worth taking seriously. Checking whether Bhādrapada śukla 2 fell on a Sunday in NS 497 or in NS 794 should decide it. The text is 'nepāla mahimā', i.e. the Nepālamāhātmya. 'likhet' is an optative used with past meaning.
review: No substantive changes; persons, roles, date and era confirmed.

Notes expanded: the direct-order reading 794 (1674 CE) is flagged as a real possibility, given the catalogue's reading and the generally late dating of the Nepālamāhātmya; the weekday could settle it.

title: Prayāgamāhātmya

colophon: iti śrībra(11)hmapurāṇe nāradayudhiṣṭhirasaṃvāde prayāgamāhātmye dvādaśo dhyāyaḥ || saṃpūrṇaḥ || saṃvat 1869 māghamāse (12) śuddhapakṣe 10 ghṛguvāsare likhitaṃ vireśvarajottirvidena (!) || svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca || 4 śubham bhūyāt || ❁ || (13) prayāgamāhātmyasyedaṃ pustakaṃ samāptam (fol. 24v10-13)
notes: 'ghṛguvāsare' is a scribal corruption of bhṛguvāsare (Friday). 'jottirvidena' is a corruption of jyotirvidena; 'vireśvara' is read as Vīreśvara. The era is taken to be VS because the colophon says only 'saṃvat'. VS 1869 −57 gives 1812, but Māgha śukla 10 of that year falls in January/February 1813 CE. The '4' after 'svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca' is unclear and may be a punctuation or filler mark. 'svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca' is a stock formula, so the scribe is not also recorded as owner.

purpose: offered with devotion (bhaktyārpitam?) to King Rājendravikrama
notes: The colophon has no date. If the king is Rājendra Vikrama Śāha of Nepal, the manuscript would date from about 1816–1847 CE. 'rājendrādimavikramāya' is garbled; it probably stands for Rājendra(-ādima?)vikrama, and the catalogue reads Rājendravikrama Śāha. 'bhavatyārpitaṃ' is probably an error for 'bhaktyārpitaṃ' (offered with devotion). 'gairīya bhāṣā' presumably means the hill language, i.e. Nepali (Gorkhālī/Parbatiyā). 'prasastam' should read 'praśastam'. Nīlakavi made the Nepali bhāṣāṭīkā on the Rudrākṣamāhātmya, which comes from the Tantracintāmaṇi, and presented it to the king. The catalogue lists him as the scribe, but the colophon only shows him as the commentator who offered the book; this copy may be his own autograph presentation copy. 'kavi' may be a title (the poet Nīla) rather than part of the name.

'vārddhy-āṣāḍha' most likely stands for vṛddhi-Āṣāḍha, the intercalary (adhika) month. Whether Śaka 1776 actually had an adhika Āṣāḍha has not been checked against an ephemeris. 'asita' means the dark fortnight (kṛṣṇa pakṣa). 'vinikhati(!)' is a corruption of 'vilikhati'. 'jinajo' qualifies Bhuvanānanda and is unclear: it may mean 'son of Jina' (a patronymic, though the father's name would then be uncertain) or be a corruption, for example of 'dvijajo'. No separate person has been created for it. 'śrībadaryyākhya(!)' refers to the Badarī-māhātmya. This agrees with the catalogue fields (scribe Bhuvanānanda, Śāke 1776).

Notes: the first reading stated that an intercalary Āṣāḍha 'indeed occurred in 1854'. This has not been checked, so it is now marked as unverified.
Notes: 'jinajo' is explained as possibly 'son of Jina', which would be a patronymic, or a corruption. No separate person is created for it.

notes: The colophon says only 'saṃvat 1938'. VS is inferred: it fits the north Indian context, and VS 1938 Bhādrapada kṛṣṇa 8 (pūrṇimānta), i.e. Janmāṣṭamī, falls around 18 Aug 1881, which was a Thursday, matching guruvāsara. The catalogue's 'ŚS 1838' (=1916 CE) does not match the colophon and is probably a cataloguing slip. Read as ŚS, 1938 would be 2016 CE, which is impossible. The verse chronogram rasa(6)-vahni(3)-aṅka(9)-candra(1), read right to left, gives 1936 (probably VS, c. 1879). This is the year Puruṣottama found and made known the 'hidden' māhātmya, two years before the copy. 'aṇveṣyāviś' stands for anviṣyāviś; 'apyuta' is unclear. The colophon gives Vilāsapura only as the scribe's residence, not explicitly as the place of copying. It may be Bilaspur (Himachal Pradesh, which would suit a Himādikhaṇḍa text) or Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh), so it is left unnormalised.

subject: Kathā
colophon: iti śrī[[bhaviṣyottarapurāṇe śrīkṛṣṇa arjuna samvāde]] anaṃtavratakathā samāptaḥ (!) śubham astu samvat 1762 samaināma āśvinavadi aṣṭamī idaṃ stotraṃ jaikṛṣṇa brāhmaṇa chitupuragrāmavāsinaṃ (!) rāma rāma (fol. 9r4–6)
notes: The phrase 'idaṃ stotraṃ jaikṛṣṇa brāhmaṇa chitupuragrāmavāsinaṃ (!)' has no verb such as likhitam. It reads most naturally as a statement of ownership ('this stotra [belongs to] Jaikṛṣṇa, a brahmin living in Chitupuragrāma'). The scribe role rests only on the catalogue. 'Jaikṛṣṇa' is probably a vernacular form of Jayakṛṣṇa. 'samaināma' is most likely a vernacular form of 'samaye/samaya nāma'. 'samvat 1762' is taken as Vikrama (NS 1762 is impossible). Āśvina vadi 8 in VS 1762 falls in roughly September–October 1705 CE. Chitupuragrāma is given as his place of residence and is not explicitly the place of copying, although the catalogue lists it as the place of copying. The catalogue spells the names 'Jaikṛṇa Brāhāmaṇa' and 'Chitupurgrāma'; these are typos for the colophon's jaikṛṣṇa brāhmaṇa and chitupuragrāma.

notes: The catalogue lists Rāghava Śarmā as the scribe, which is wrong. The colophon names Govinda Jyotirvid as the scribe of this copy. Rāghava Śarman is cited for a deśāntara value of 205 yojanas in the Gauḍa work Siddhāntarahasya ('śrīrāghavaśarmaṇā likhitam asti tenātrāsmābhir likhitaṃ'). He is probably Rāghavānanda Śarman, the Bengali author of the Siddhāntarahasya, so he is the source of a cited figure, not someone involved in making this copy. 'svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca' could imply Govinda also owned the copy, but because it is for others as well, owner was not added. 'śrīgaṃgāsāgarārppaṇam astu' ('may it be offered to Gaṅgāsāgara') is ambiguous: it could refer to the pilgrimage site or deity, or to a person named Gaṅgāsāgara. No person was recorded for it. CE: Pauṣa śukla 7 of ŚS 1643 falls around late Dec 1721 or early Jan 1722, and the weekday has not been checked. The numbers after the colophon (deśāntara 2135, prabhā 5/10 or 5/8) are the scribe's astronomical notes.

title: Gopīcandranāṭaka

colophon: samvat 810 bhādrapada śukla trayodaśyāṃtithau vudhavāsare || li[[khi]]ta saṃpūrṇṇa miti || dvijavala śrīvi[[śva]]nā(52v4]thena ṛṣitaṃ śubhamastu sarvvadā || || || ❖ halaḍa, kaśurī, kaḍavasī kīva, vaṃśaliocana, puskarāmura, karkkaṭasiṃ, samabhāga (5) kastiḥ bulāva nake sāthaṃthapaṅa mośoka loya rāvakhaṃ ||(6) ≪ Added with different hand ≫ śrīśrī sumati jaya jitāmitramalladevasana thva pustaka dayakā || bhāgīrāma paramānayā verasa || śubhaṃ || (7)
notes: 'ṛṣitaṃ' is a corruption of likhitaṃ, and 'dvijavala' stands for dvijavara. The line 'halaḍa, kaśurī, kaḍavasī ... rāvakhaṃ' is a medical recipe (haritakī, kastūrī, vaṃśalocana, puṣkaramūla, etc.) and names no persons. The note about Jitāmitra Malla is added in a different hand: 'Jitāmitra Malla had this book made, at the time of Minister (pramāna) Bhāgīrāma.' notes: The dates were added in a later hand and appear to record the production of the play rather than the copying of the manuscript. In chronological order: NS 809 Caitra śukla 13 (c. Mar/Apr 1689), the ghaṃtijyā was begun (ārambha); NS 809 Śrāvaṇa śukla 1 (c. Jul/Aug 1689), the ghaṃtijyā was finished (dhuna); NS 810 Pauṣa śukla 3 (c. Dec 1689/Jan 1690), the day of the pyākhana (dance-drama performance). 'ghaṃtijyā' is unclear; it may mean rehearsal or preparatory work for the play. The phrase 'pyākhana ṛ tayā' looks corrupt. title: Ākhyātacandrikā
subject: Vyākaraṇa
colophon: ity ākhyātacandrikā samāptā || || vītyāśugābdābdaśake śucer dale ʼṣṭamyāṃ bhṛgau dvandvabhage bhage tv idam | nepāladeśe nijadarśanārtha〈〈ṃ〉〉m alīlikhac chrīdvijalālaśarmmā || 1 || (fol. 14v14-15)
notes:
Role: 'alīlikhat' is strictly the causative aorist of likh ('caused to be written'), so Dvijalāla might have commissioned the copy rather than written it. Nepalese colophons, however, often use alīlikhat simply for 'wrote'. Together with nijadarśanārtham and the catalogue's Scribe field, this makes scribe + owner the more likely reading. Commissioner remains possible.

Chronogram: 'vīty-āśuga-abda-abda-śake' is unresolved. vīti (horse) = 7 and āśuga (arrow) = 5, but 'abda' (cloud? or simply 'year') has no secure numerical value. If the second 'abda' just means 'year', only three digit-words remain, which is too few for a Śaka year. The era is taken as ŚS from 'śake', but 'śaka' can also mean 'era' in general. If the year were ŚS 1757 the date would be about CE 1835, but this is speculative, so ce_approx is left empty.

Pakṣa: 'dale' does not name the pakṣa. Śukla is inferred from the astronomy: Āṣāḍha aṣṭamī with the sun in Mithuna and the moon in Pūrvaphalgunī fits the bright fortnight. 'Śuci' may also denote Jyeṣṭha in some usage.

The 〈〈ṃ〉〉 in nijadarśanārtha〈〈ṃ〉〉m is the cataloguer's mark of a redundant anusvāra.
review: p1 roles changed from commissioner+owner to scribe+owner. 'alīlikhat' is formally a causative aorist, but Nepalese scribes routinely use it for their own copying. 'nijadarśanārtham' with himself as subject and the catalogue's 'Scribe' field both point to self-copying. Confidence lowered to medium.
date.nakshatra_yoga filled: 'bhage' = Bhaga-nakṣatra (Pūrvaphalgunī); 'dvandvabhage' = sun in Mithuna (Gemini).
date.month normalised to Śuci (= Āṣāḍha); era kept as ŚS but flagged as uncertain; chronogram discussed in notes; ce_approx left empty.

notes rewritten.

title: Dānakelikaumudī
subject: Nāṭaka (Bhāṇikā)
colophon: dānakelikaumudī nāma bhāṇikā samāptā grathitā sumanaḥsukhadā yasya nideśena bhāṇikāsrag iyaṃ || tasya mama priyasuhṛdaḥ kaṃṭhataṭīkṣaṇam alaṃkurutāṃ || naṃdīśvare nivasatā bhāṇikeyaṃ vinirmmitā || gate manuśate śāke caṃdrasvararamanvite (!) || atha bhāṇikālakṣaṇaṃ || bhāṇikā ślākṣṇa(!)nepathyā mukhanirbbahaṇānvitā || kaiśikī bhāratīvṛttiyutaikāṃkavinirmmitā|| etc. (fol. 33v)
notes: The colophon gives nothing about the copy itself: no scribe, commissioner, owner, copying date or copying place. All of it is the author's own closing text. It says the bhāṇikā was written at the command of an unnamed dear friend ('yasya nideśena ... tasya mama priyasuhṛdaḥ'). It was composed while living at Nandīśvara ('naṃdīśvare nivasatā bhāṇikeyaṃ vinirmmitā'), the hill at Nandgaon in Braj. The composition date is 'gate manuśate śāke caṃdrasvara(sa)manvite' (the cataloguer marks 'ramanvite' as corrupt with (!)). This reads as Śaka 1471, i.e. about 1549 CE. The work is Rūpa Gosvāmin's Dānakelikaumudī, but he is not named here. After this comes a definition of the bhāṇikā genre ('atha bhāṇikālakṣaṇaṃ ...'), quoted only in part (etc.), so a scribal colophon may follow on fol. 33v without being quoted.
review: Date fields cleared (era 'none'): 'gate manuśate śāke candrasvara-samanvite' is the author's composition verse, not a copying date. Its reading is Śaka 1471 (manu 14 hundreds + candra 1, svara 7 read right to left = 71), about 1549 CE. That reading is correct and is kept in the notes.
Place cleared: Nandīśvara is where the work was composed ('naṃdīśvare nivasatā bhāṇikeyaṃ vinirmmitā'), not where it was copied. It is moved to the notes.
Persons left empty. The author (Rūpa Gosvāmin) is not named in the colophon, and the 'priyasuhṛd' at whose command the work was written is anonymous.

colophon: mālatīprāptir nāma daśamoṃkaḥ | || smāptaṃ ceda (!) mālatīmādhavābhidheyaṃ prakaraṇaṃ || || idaṃ pustakam liºº kadhaiyālāla kāestha kāśīmadhe vāsa || ❁ || ❁ || saṃvat 1852 mīti phālgumāse sukla pakṣe puranavāsī 15 bhoma vāsare || || jo deṣā solōṣā mama doṣa nadīyate || (fol. 57v6–58r1)
notes: The colophon reads 'kadhaiyālāla'; the catalogue gives 'kahnaiyālāla'. Both are probably the common name Kanhaiyālāla, with nh/hn misread or miswritten as dh. 'liºº' abbreviates likhitam, so this person is the scribe. 'kāestha' = kāyastha. 'kāśīmadhe vāsa' = resident in Kāśī, which is taken here as the place of copying as well. subject: Nāṭaka
colophon: itiśrī śrījayabhūpatīndramalladeva, mahārājādhirāja, viracitaṃ nalacaritanāma nāṭake (!) pañcamoṅka (!) || śubham astu || || śloka 1601 || samvat [ 808 . . .] śudi 2 roja 2 śrīśivarājopādhyāyale banāyāko pustakam idaṃ bhūyāt || ❁ || (fol. 4v10–12)
notes: The year is uncertain. The cataloguer put '808' in square brackets and it is followed by lacunae. The catalogue itself gives 'NS 808?', and the month is lost. NS 808 (1688 CE) is earlier than Bhūpatīndra Malla's reign in Bhaktapur (c. NS 816–842 / 1696–1722 CE), yet the colophon calls him mahārājādhirāja. So either the reading is wrong (e.g. 818 or 828) or the title was given to him retrospectively. Bhūpatīndra appears here only as the author of the play. The scribe's name 'śivarājopādhyāya' can be split as Śiva + Rājopādhyāya (the usual Newar Brahmin title) or as Śivarāja + Upādhyāya. The catalogue's 'Śivamarājopādhyāya' might point to Śivarāma. 'banāyāko' (Nepali, 'made') most likely means he copied the book, but it could also mean he had it made. 'pustakam idaṃ bhūyāt' is a garbled Sanskrit ending.

title: Vṛttaratnākara
subject: Chandaḥśāstra
colophon: iti vṛttaratnākare ṣaṣṭhodhyāya || ❁ || (fol. 45v8) iti śrīmadvidvnmu(10)kuṭaratna śrīmadbhaṭṭarāmeśvarasūnunārāyaṇabhaṭṭaviracitāyāṃ vṛttaratnākaravyākhyāyāṃ prastārādhyāyaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ || ❁ || gaṃthaś ca samāptaḥ (11) || ❁ || nīlalohitatanu svaraśailabhūmitavikramasamā sugatā surasāsuralikhitam idaṃ vṛttaratnākaranāmakaṃ chaṃdaḥ || śubham bhūyāt || śrī | (fol. 46r9–11)
notes: The chronogram is a bhūtasaṃkhyā: nīlalohita-tanu = 8 (Śiva's eight forms), svara = 7, śaila = 7, bhū = 1. Read right to left this gives Vikrama year 1778, about 1721 CE. The catalogue gives SAM 1878 (about 1821 CE). It may have read śaila as 8 or simply be wrong, so the catalogue date conflicts with the colophon. 'sugatā' is unclear: it may be corrupt for a month or pakṣa word, or simply mean 'elapsed'. 'surasāsuralikhitam' is corrupt. It might hide a scribe's name (e.g. Sura..., Sureśvara?), but that cannot be read with confidence, so no scribe is recorded. The colophon names the commentator Nārāyaṇabhaṭṭa, son of Rāmeśvarabhaṭṭa. Kedārabhaṭṭa, who wrote the root text, is not named.
review: Date: chronogram re-read. nīlalohita-tanu = 8 (Śiva's aṣṭamūrti), svara = 7, śaila = 7, bhū = 1. Read right to left this gives VS 1778, not 1878. ce_approx changed from 1821 to 1721.
Notes: recorded that the chronogram conflicts with the catalogue's SAM 1878, and that 'surasāsuralikhitam' may hide a scribe's name.
Persons and relations confirmed.

title: Vṛttaratnākara
subject: Chandaḥśāstra
colophon: iti śrīmadbhārabdāvā(!)ṣṭhakṛṣṇabhaṭṭātmaja do bhasūnu dinakarakṛte vṛttaratnākaraṃdarśaḥ samāptim aphāṇīt śrīmārṇastu saṃvat 1864 māse caitra sule(!) pakṣa 11 graṃthasamāvate subham astu pustakam idaṃ śrīkṛṣṇajośī || rāmanagara bālo (fol. 102r4-6)
notes: The commentary is the Vṛttaratnākarādarśa ('vṛttaratnākaraṃdarśaḥ'). The author's genealogy is corrupt: 'śrīmadbhārabdāvā(!)ṣṭha' = Bhāradvāja gotra? 'kṛṣṇabhaṭṭātmaja do bhasūnu' most likely means 'son of [?de]vabhaṭṭa, the son of Kṛṣṇabhaṭṭa'. The father's name is lost; it may be (Mahā)devabhaṭṭa, i.e. the Pāyaguṇḍe family (Bālakṛṣṇa → Mahādeva → Divākara/Dinakara), but this is unverified. 'samāptim aphāṇīt' is a corruption of 'agamat', and 'śrīmārṇastu' of 'śrīr astu'. The era is a bare 'saṃvat', taken as VS. 'rāmanagara bālo' (Hindi -vālā) marks Kṛṣṇa Jośī as being from Rāmanagara (possibly the one near Vārāṇasī). It is not explicitly the place of copying. The catalogue fields (scribe Padmanābhadvija; ŚS 1701 ≈ 1779 CE) do not match this colophon, which names no scribe and gives saṃvat 1864. These fields may belong to another colophon in the same MS or be a cataloguing error.
review: p3 name corrected from 'Śrīkṛṣṇa' to 'Kṛṣṇa': śrī is an honorific and is dropped.
p2 name changed to stem 'Kṛṣṇa', with bhaṭṭa kept as a title.

Relation p1→p2 changed from son_of to grandson_of. 'kṛṣṇabhaṭṭātmaja do bhasūnu' reads as 'son of [X]bhaṭṭa, who is the son of Kṛṣṇabhaṭṭa'. The garbled 'do bha' probably hides the father's name, perhaps (Mahā)devabhaṭṭa.
p1 confidence lowered to medium. The name may be a corruption of Divākara, and the genealogy is garbled.
Place of copying cleared. Rāmanagara is stated only as the owner's residence ('rāmanagara bālo' = 'of Rāmanagara'). It is kept in p3's residence field.
Era basis explained in notes. The colophon has a bare 'saṃvat'; it is taken as VS, so 1864 = 1807 CE (Caitra śukla 11, spring 1807).
Notes expanded.

purpose: svapāṭhārtham: for the (unnamed) scribe's own study
notes: The verb 'lilekha' has no expressed subject, so the scribe is not named in this colophon. Devarāma may have copied his own commentary with the text, but the wording does not show this. The catalogue's scribe, Rādhākṛṣṇa, is absent from the quoted colophon and may be named on another folio. Śivalāla Pāṭhaka is described as devoted to the feet of Jānakīramaṇa (Rāma). He is Devarāma's teacher ('pādānuyāyi'), so he is linked to the commentary, not to the act of copying. The commentary is the Rāmāyaṇīya Viṣamapadavyākhyāna. 'āleye' should be read 'ālaye': the copy was made at a Śrī Rāmacandra temple or house in Kāśī. The '1' before 'samvat' is probably a punctuation mark or a stray numeral. Saṃvat 1900 Kārttika vadi 2 is taken as VS, giving about October/November 1843 CE.
review: Purpose normalised to 'svapāṭhārtham: for the scribe's own study'. The scribe is not named in the colophon.

Notes expanded: the subject of 'lilekha' is unexpressed. Devarāma may be both compiler and copyist, but this is unproven. Rādhākṛṣṇa (from the catalogue) is not in the quoted text. Śivalāla is Devarāma's teacher, not the teacher of the scribe of this copy. Place = a Rāmacandra temple (ālaya) in Kāśī. The stray '1' before 'samvat' is noted.

colophon: ityārṣe vālmīkiye śrīmaduttarakāṇḍe svargārohaṇaṃ . . . . . . . . . . || samāpta . . . . samvat 805 kārtikaśuklatrayodaśī śrī śrīsumati jitāmitra malladevasa ājñāna surata . . . . . rāmacandrāya namaḥ || || śrī śrī śrīrāmalakṣmaṇasītābharataśatrughnabhyo namaḥ || || || || śubhaṃ || || . . . . . . . . . . . . . gira pradhānāṅgayā . . . . saṃpūrṇa yāṅādina juro || || . . . (fol. 108r)
purpose: completed by order (ājñā) of King Jitāmitramalla
notes: The colophon is damaged in several places. The king is written 'sumati jitāmitra malladeva'. 'Sumati' is the usual epithet in Jitāmitra Malla's name (Bhaktapur, r. c. 1673–1696 CE). The catalogue's 'Jayajitāmitra' does not match the colophon. NS 805 Kārttika falls in Oct/Nov 1684 CE, which is within his reign. 'ājñāna surata . . .' may contain the start of another person's name (lost). Only the end of the pradhānāṅga's name survives ('…gira'). Newari 'saṃpūrṇa yāṅā dina' means 'the day it was completed'. It names him as the person who completed the copy, probably by royal order, but does not say clearly whether he wrote it or had it written, so he is not tagged as scribe or commissioner.
review: p2: name kept as regnal name Jitāmitramalla; removed 'sumati' and 'deva' from titles. 'Sumati' is an epithet that forms part of this king's name, and '-deva' belongs to the regnal form. Both are recorded in notes.

p3: role changed from 'scribe' to 'minister' + 'other'. 'pradhānāṅga' is a ministerial office, and 'saṃpūrṇa yāṅā' (Newari: 'made complete') does not show that he wrote the copy himself. Name reduced to the surviving fragment '…gira'.
notes: added the fragment 'surata . . .' after 'ājñāna' (possibly a lost name) and the mismatch with the catalogue's 'Jayajitāmitra'.

title: Kavikalpalatā
subject: Sāhitya
colophon: iti śrīvāgbhaṭasūnumahā(10)kavideveśvaraviracitā kavikalpalatā samāptā || || || rasavedādricaṃdre ʼbde 1746 ūrjjasyāsitapakṣa(11)ke || paṃcamyāṃ caṃdradivase nakṣatre brahmadaivake || 1 || sukhārāmeṇa cālekhi kavikalpalatābhidhaṃ || mitrarāmadvi(12)jo (!) kāśyāṃ pustakaṃ cālikhan mudā || 2 || lekhakapāṭhakayor vai śubhaṃ bhūyāt tu sarvadā || || śrīr astu || śubhakṛti(13)navaśāstrādrikṣamāsaṃkhyavarṣe sahasi kavilatākhyaṃ kalpamadhyaṃ hi pustaṃ || (fol. 49v9-13)
notes: The era is not named ('ʼbde' only). VS is inferred because the copy was made in Kāśī and the catalogue gives SAM 1746. If the era were ŚS, the date would be about 1824 CE. The weekday and nakṣatra have not been checked against an ephemeris. Two people are said to have written the manuscript: Sukhārāma ('sukhārāmeṇa cālekhi') and Mitrarāma dvija ('kāśyāṃ pustakaṃ cālikhan'). They may have been co-scribes, or one of the verbs may mean something else. The catalogue names only Mitrarāma. The (!) after 'dvijo' marks the irregular form in the original. The final half-verse gives a second date: 'śubhakṛti … navaśāstrādrikṣmā-saṃkhya-varṣe sahasi'. Read right to left, nava 9, śāstra 6, adri 7, kṣmā 1 = 1769, in the Jovian year Śubhakṛt, month Sahas (Mārgaśīrṣa). If this is VS, it is about 1712 CE, 23 years after the main date. It may record a later event in the book's history (e.g. a re-copying or acquisition). This verse is fragmentary and its relation to the main colophon is unclear. The blessing for the lekhaka and pāṭhaka is a formula and names no one.
review: p4 Mitrarāma: residence 'Kāśī' removed; the colophon only says he copied the book in Kāśī (kāśyāṃ … cālikhan), which goes in place, not residence

Date: chronogram checked (rasa 6, veda 4, adri 7, candra 1, read right to left = 1746, matching the figures). Ūrja = Kārttika, asita = kṛṣṇa, caṃdradivasa = Monday, brahmadaivaka = Rohiṇī are all confirmed. The era is not stated and VS is only inferred; this is now said in notes

title: Kāvyapradīpa
subject: Sāhitya
colophon: iti srīmahomahopādhyāya (!) śrīgoviṃdaviracite kāvyapradīper ʼthālaṃkāranirṇayo nāma daśama ullāsaḥ samāptaḥ || || 10 || || saṃvat 1738 śamaye nāma phālguna māṃśe (!) kṛṣṇapakṣe prathmādīnāṃ śubhavāśare tādināṃ pustakaṃ śaṃpurnaṃ (!) jādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ maā jadi śūddha a[[śu]]ddhaṃ vā mama doṣo na dīatām|| (!) likhitaṃ bhojarā[[ja]] kāesta (!) (fol. last page r7–9)
notes: The colophon names no era, only 'saṃvat 1738'. I read it as Vikrama because of the Devanagari script, the Kāyastha scribe, and the year itself. NS 1738 is impossible, and ŚS 1738 (1816 CE) is possible but less likely. VS 1738 minus 57 gives 1681, but Phālguna kṛṣṇa of that year falls around February–March 1682 CE. 'mahomahopādhyāya' is a corrupt spelling of mahāmahopādhyāya. The author is Govinda (Ṭhakkura), who wrote the Kāvyapradīpa. 'śubhavāśare' (= śubhavāsare, 'on an auspicious day') is a formula and names no weekday. 'kāesta' = kāyastha, 'maā' = mayā, and 'prathmādīnāṃ' = prathamā tithi. The 'ja' of Bhojarāja is a cataloguer's addition, but the reading is secure.

The place phrase is corrupt: 'vyapāla' may stand for 'nepāla' (…rāṣṭrasya nepāla…), and 'vāhinīpariveṣṭite' means 'surrounded by rivers'. The place has not been identified.

(fol. 26v1–4)
notes: Chronogram: vahni (3), dvīpa (7), surataru/kalpataru (5), brahma (1), read right to left = 1573. The era word 'śateke' is corrupt. It is read as 'śāke', which gives ŚS 1573 ≈ 1651 CE. VS 1573 ≈ 1516 CE would be earlier than the composition of the Śaradāgama under Vīrabhadra of Bāndhava/Rewa (late 16th century), so the era is uncertain but ŚS is preferred. 'rāmacaṃdradevātmaja' (son of Rāmacandradeva) must refer to the royal patron Vīrabhadra, whose name seems to have dropped out of this copy (the catalogue lists 'Vīrabhadra Bhūpati' as King). The catalogue wrongly gives Pradyotana as scribe: he is the commentator, and the copyist is Mathurānātha ('alikhan mathurānātho').

title: Khaṇḍapraśasti
subject: Kāvya
colophon: iti śrīmadasanamad viracitāyāṃ khaṃḍapraśasti samāpṭā || || (fol. 21v7) miti asādḥa vadi 8 maṃ. saṃvat 1856 || likhitaṃ (kṛṣṇanamaṣnorā) (!) brāhmaṇasya || khaṃḍa praśasti || śrī rāma padma (fol. 22v4–5)
notes: 'śrīmadasanamad viracitāyāṃ' is a corruption of 'śrīmad-dhanumad-viracitāyāṃ': the text is traditionally attributed to Hanumat, a mythical author, so he is left out. The scribe's name is corrupt. The most plausible reading is 'kṛṣṇanāmno brāhmaṇasya' ('of the brāhmaṇa named Kṛṣṇa'), which fits the catalogue's 'Kṛṣṇa‥‥brāhmaṇa'; the leftover 'rā' may be a dittography of the following 'brā'. The era is given only as 'saṃvat'. VS is assumed (as in the catalogue), giving 1799 CE. 'śrī rāma padma' at the end is an invocation or a stray note, not a person.
review: Scribe's name re-read: 'kṛṣṇanamaṣnorā' is most likely a corruption of 'kṛṣṇanāmno' ('of the one named Kṛṣṇa'), so the name is Kṛṣṇa, not 'Kṛṣṇanamaṣnora'. Confidence raised to medium.

Note on the author refined (śrīmadasanamad < śrīmad-dhanumad, i.e. Hanumat).

notes: The colophon gives only 'saṃvat 1920', with no era named. VS is inferred: NS 1920 is impossible, and the 'mi.' (miti) formula is typical of Nepali VS dating. The catalogue also gives VS 1920. VS 1920 Kārttika kṛṣṇa 13 falls around October/November 1863 CE. The catalogue names Keśavadatta as scribe, but no personal name appears in the quoted colophon. The name may come from elsewhere in the manuscript, so it is not recorded here. The colophon names both the kāvya and its ṭīkā ('ghaṭakarparaṭīkā samāptāḥ' (!), an ungrammatical plural), so the manuscript has the text with a commentary. The commentator is not named.

title: Caurapañcāśikā
subject: Kāvya
colophon: iti dhaṭakarparakāvyaṃ samāptam || || 22 || || 22 || oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya || 22 || (fol. 6r5) iti ghaṭakarparaṭīkā samāptāḥ || 22 || sampūrṇam || 22 || śubhaṃ bhūyāt || śrīr astu || śubhaṃm astu || saṃvat 1920 || mi. kā. kṛ. 13 caṃ || śubhaṃbhūyāt || śubhaṃm || (fol. 6r7-8)
notes: The colophon belongs to the Ghaṭakarparakāvya and its ṭīkā ('dhaṭakarpara' is a slip for 'ghaṭakarpara') and names no persons. The era is not stated. I read it as Vikrama because of the Nepali-style abbreviation 'mi. kā. kṛ.' (miti kārtika kṛṣṇa) and because reading it as NS 1920 (about 2800 CE) is impossible. That gives VS 1920 kārtika kṛṣṇa 13, a Monday ('caṃ' = candravāra), around October–November 1863 CE. This does not match the catalogue fields (title Caurapañcāśikā, Samvat 1678 kārtika vadi 12 maṅgalavāra, donor Netrānanda miśra). Those fields probably describe a different manuscript or another part of the reel. Netrānanda is not in this colophon, so I have not recorded him.
review: No substantive changes. Notes now say that the era is inferred rather than stated, and that 'dhaṭakarpara' is a scribal slip for 'ghaṭakarpara'.

subject: Kāvya

notes: Umāpati(rāja), called mahārājādhirāja, is the patron under whom Bhaṭṭa Keśava composed (udyotita) the campū. He is not attested as the reigning king at the time of this copy. The chronogram 'munikumadakuvājiḥ' is corrupt. It is read tentatively as muni (7), kumada for kumuda, one of the elephants of the quarters (8), ku (1), vāji (7). Read right to left this gives Śaka 1787, about 1865 CE. If 'mada' is not a number word, the reading fails, so treat the year as uncertain. 'nayanahutāśana' (2, 3) in the second hemistich may encode a further date element, such as a tithi or another year figure, but the context is too corrupt to decode. 'amanaṃgaraṅgabhaṅge' (= anaṅgaraṅgabhaṅga?) may be a descriptive phrase or a Śiva-related date term, so it was not interpreted. The place 'sadvalesa pūryām' (some '…purī') is corrupt and unidentified. No scribe, commissioner or owner is named. The colophon ends the 5th stavaka.

title: *Ghaṭakarparakāvyaṭīkā
subject: Kāvya
date_raw: āṅgirā nāmasaṃvatsare kārtikemāse śukravāsare ʼṣṭamyāṃ tithau ... saṃvat 1920 || mi. kā. kṛ. 13 caṃ
colophon: iti śrinandītaṭakṣetrastha mālavadetyupanāmaka vyeṃkaṭeśa sūri viracitā ghaṭakharparakāvyavyākhyā samāptim agamat || śrī || idaṃ pustakaṃ sātāra nagare sānayiti upanāmaka gaṇeśa sūnunā gopālenaāṅgirā nāmasaṃvatsare kārtikemāse śukravāsare ʼ ṣṭamyāṃ tithau sakalaṃ śrī śaṃkaraputra siddhivināyakānugraheṇā mayā llihitam || || ❁ || ❁ || śrīhari || (fol. 6r5) iti ghaṭakarparaṭīkā samāptāḥ || 22 || sampūrṇam || 22 || śubhaṃ bhūyāt || śrīr astu || śubhaṃm astu || saṃvat 1920 || mi. kā. kṛ. 13 caṃ || śubhaṃbhūyāt || śubhaṃm || (fol. 6r7–8)
notes: The colophon has two dates that conflict. (1) The scribe's own date: Āṅgiras saṃvatsara, Kārtika, Friday, aṣṭamī (the pakṣa is not stated; 'śukra' is the weekday, Friday). Āṅgiras is year 6 of the 60-year cycle, so in the southern reckoning used at Satara this is 1872 CE (ŚS 1794); 1812 CE is also possible. (2) 'saṃvat 1920 mi[ti] kā[rtika] kṛ[ṣṇa] 13 caṃ[dravāra]', a Monday. Read as VS this gives 1863 CE, which is not an Āṅgiras year. Read as ŚS it would be impossible. Line (2) follows a second ending ('iti ghaṭakarparaṭīkā samāptāḥ') on fol. 6r7–8 and is probably a later addition, perhaps a Nepalese VS note. The copying itself most likely dates to about 1872. 'śaṃkaraputra siddhivināyaka' is the deity Gaṇeśa, not a person. Mālavade and Sānayiti are upanāmas (family surnames). Satara is in Maharashtra.
review: Gopāla: residence emptied — Sātāra is only stated as the place of copying, not his residence

title: Naiṣadhadīpikā
subject: Kāvya
colophon: iti śrīpaṃḍitacāṃdraviracitāyāṃ naiṣadhadīpikāyāṃ śrīānaṃdāṃke mahākāvye śrīśrīharṣakṛtau śaśāṃkasaṃkīrtanaṃ nāmā dvāviṃśaḥ sarggaḥ || samāptaḥ || || śubhaṃ bhavatu śrīr astu || śrīḥ || || iti || saṃvat 1582 varṣe śrāvaṇa śudi navamyām 9 tithau bhṛhu | sadine yathā nakṣatra yogesamaye | adyeha śrīdevadārūvana vāstavya ācāryamāṇikāsuta kānhākhena pustakām alikhi || (!) paropakārārthaṃ cātmanaḥ paṭhanārthaṃ || (fol. 295r6–11)
purpose: for others (paropakārārthaṃ) and for the scribe's own study (ātmanaḥ paṭhanārthaṃ)
notes: The scribe's name 'kānhākhena' is best read as kānhākhyena, 'by the one named Kānhā'. The catalogue's 'Kāhnā' is probably a metathesis. 'cāṃdra' is probably corrupt for Cāṇḍū Paṇḍita, the usual author of the Naiṣadhadīpikā. Neither the era nor the place is named. VS is assumed because a Devanagari manuscript with Śrāvaṇa śudi uses the 'saṃvat' formula, and it gives c. 1525 CE (ŚS would give 1660 CE). The weekday has not been checked against the date. Devadāruvana ('deodar forest') may be a hermitage or locality; its location is not identified. 'adyeha … vāstavya' suggests the book was copied there. The formula 'yathā nakṣatra yogesamaye' names no specific nakṣatra.
review: Scribe's name: 'kānhākhena' read as kānhā-ākhyena ('named Kānhā'), so the name is Kānhā, not Kānhākha. The catalogue's 'Kāhnā' is probably a metathesis.
Scribe given roles scribe + owner, because he copied it 'ātmanaḥ paṭhanārthaṃ' (for his own study).
Author name changed to Śrīharṣa: here 'śrī' is part of the personal name ('śrīśrīharṣa' = honorific śrī + Śrīharṣa).
Commentator 'Cāndra' kept as written, with confidence lowered to medium. The Naiṣadhadīpikā is usually ascribed to Cāṇḍū Paṇḍita, so 'cāṃdra' is probably corrupt.
Residence removed from Māṇika: 'devadārūvana vāstavya' grammatically describes the scribe.
nakshatra_yoga emptied: 'yathā nakṣatra yogesamaye' is a stock formula and names no nakṣatra or yoga.
Weekday spelled out: 'bhṛhu' is a mistake for bhṛgu (Friday).
Purpose field condensed.

title: Bhaṭṭikāvya
subject: Kāvya
colophon: iti vallabhīvāstavyasya śrīsvāmisūnoḥ bhaṭṭamahāvrāhmaṇasya mahāvaiyākaraṇasyakṛtau bhaṭṭikākāvye rāvaṇavadhe tiṅantakāṇḍe luḍavilasitaṃnāma navamaḥ paricchedaḥ kāvyasyāyodhyā pratyāgamanaṃnāma dvāviṃśaḥ sarggaḥ samāptaḥ samāptam idaṃ bhaṭṭikāvyaṃ dvāviṃśasargātmakaṃ 22 || (fol. 149r7–8) iti śrīvallabhīvāstavyasyaisya śrīsvāmisūnor bhaṭṭamahābrāhmaṇasyaḥ (!) vaiyyākaraṇasyakṛtau rāvaṇavadhe mahātiṅaṃtakāṃḍe ludvilasitanāmno navamaparicchedasya jaṭīśvarojayadevo jayamaṃgala iti + + māstribhi prasiddhasya anekaśāstrānukṛtau ṭīkāyāṃ kāvyasyāyodhyāgamanaṃ nāma dvāviṃśaḥ sargaḥ jayamaṃgalaṃ samāptaṃ || śrīr astu śubham astu saṃkhyā 1500 saṃvat 1830 + + + śāke 1694 mītī pauśa (!) śudi 2 (fol. 149r9–12)
notes: The date gives two eras that differ by one year. VS 1830 Pauṣa śukla 2 falls around December 1773 or January 1774 CE. ŚS 1694 would correspond to VS 1829, which is about December 1772 or January 1773 CE. The equivalent of VS 1830 is ŚS 1695. Possible causes are a scribal slip or a mix of expired and current years. VS is taken as primary. Three characters are lost between the two years ('+ + +'). 'saṃkhyā 1500' is the granthasaṃkhyā. The commentator is given as 'jaṭīśvaro jayadevo jayamaṃgala iti ... prasiddhasya', which is partly lacunose. Jayamaṅgalā is the name of the well-known Bhaṭṭikāvya commentary, which is traditionally ascribed to Jayamaṅgala or Jaya(deva). Here the commentator is taken to be Jayadeva, also called Jaṭīśvara, but the alternative reading 'Jayamaṅgala' as a personal name cannot be excluded. The author's father 'śrīsvāmin' could also be read as the proper name Śrīsvāmin; tradition calls Bhaṭṭi 'Śrīsvāmisūnu' or the son of Śrīdharasvāmin. The catalogue gives King: Narendradeva and Donor: Śrīkṛṣṇajośī Rāmanagara, but neither appears in the quoted colophon; they may come from another part of the MS. The catalogue's 'Place of Copying: Vallabhī' is the author's residence, not the place where this copy was made. The colophon names no scribe or commissioner.

p1: confidence lowered to medium, since the name Bhaṭṭi is inferred from the work's title; the colophon itself gives only 'bhaṭṭa-mahābrāhmaṇa'

title: Meghadūtakāvyam
subject: Kāvya
colophon: || iti śrī mahākavi kālidāsa kṛtau meghadūtākhyaṃ kāvya samāptaṃ || || śubhamastu idaṃ pustakaṃ deva divākarena likhisvārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca || || yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṣṛṭvā tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā yadi śuddhamaśuddhaṃ vā mama doṣo na vidyate1 || || || || saṃvat 1521 bhādrapada śuddhatrayodaśi kāśyāṃ likhyate || ❖ || ❖ || ❖ || saṃvat || 1751 || || śrīmukhāsaṃvatsare dakṣIṇāyane vasaṃtattau bhādrapade bhaśi (!) śukla pakṣe trayośiṃ (!) meghadūtākhyaṃ kāvyaṃ vāsudeva bhaṭṭa devatsuta deva divākarenanalekhitaṃ || || ❖ || ❖ || || || rāma || ❖ || ❖ || sadā śiva || || ❖ || kāśyāṃ viśvarasaṃnidhau pustakaṃ likhyate || ❖ || ❖ || ❖ || || || (fol. 21v4–22rv)
purpose: svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca (for himself and for others)
notes: The colophon gives two dates. The first, 'saṃvat 1521 bhādrapada śuddhatrayodaśi kāśyāṃ likhyate' (VS 1521 = c. 1464 CE), was probably copied over from the exemplar. The second is the actual date of copying: VS 1751, Śrīmukha year, Bhādrapada śukla 13 = August/September 1694 CE. A Śrīmukha year around 1693/94 is consistent with that date. 'dakṣiṇāyane' fits Bhādrapada, but 'vasantartau' (spring) does not: the scribe made a mistake there. 'bhaśi (!)' is unclear; it may be a garbled weekday or a corruption of a word for the month, so no weekday is recorded. The scribe's name reads 'deva divākarena' (= Divākaradeva in the catalogue). 'Deva' is taken here as a family name or honorific, shared with the father 'vāsudeva bhaṭṭa deva(t)'. The 'na' in 'divākarenanalekhitaṃ' is a dittography. 'viśvarasaṃnidhau' is probably 'viśveśvarasaṃnidhau', i.e. near the Viśveśvara temple in Kāśī. 'rāma' and 'sadā śiva' are invocations, not persons.

title: Praśastiratnāvalī
subject: Bhakti
colophon: iti śrīmadgorṣādhīśvarabhūpālanarabhūpālapautraśrīmanmahoddāmakī(3)rttikumāraśrīmacchrīkṛṣṇasāhakāritā (!) śrīmadrājakulaśiromaṇipravila(4)satpādāravindadvandvaśrīmadrāmahṛdayapaṇḍitaśiromaṇisūnuvāṇīvilāsa(5)kaviviracirā praśastiratnāvaliḥ samāptā || || śrīśāke 1706 śubham || (fol. 17r2-5)
notes: The colophon concerns the composition of the text: the poet Vāṇīvilāsa, son of Rāmahṛdaya, composed it (viracirā, read viracitā) at the behest of Prince Kṛṣṇasāha (kāritā), grandson of Narabhūpāla (Śāha) of Gorkhā. 'kāritā' is marked (!) by the cataloguer. No scribe, commissioner or reigning king of this copy is named. The catalogue's 'King: Kṛṣṇasāha' is doubtful: he is called kumāra, and in ŚS 1706 (1784/85 CE) the reigning Śāha king was Raṇabahādura. The date ŚS 1706 may be the date of copying (as the catalogue says) or carried over from the exemplar.

title: Praśastiratnāvalī
subject: Kāvya
colophon: iti śrīmad gorṣādhīśvara bhūpālanarabhūpālapautra śrīman mahoddāmakīrti kumāra śrīmacchrīkṛṣṇasāhakāritā śrīmad rājakula śiromaṇi pravilasat pādāravindadvanda śrīmad rāmahṛ(!)yaḥ paṃḍitaśiromaṇi sūnu vāṇīvilāsa kaviviracitā praśastiratnāvaliḥ samāptā || śubhaṃ (fol. 7v9–11) svasti śrī girirājacakracūḍāmaṇi naranārāyaṇetyādi vividhavirudhāvalīvirājamāna mānonnata śrīmanmahārājādhirāja śrī śrī śrīmahārāje gīrvāṇayuddhavikramasāha bahādūrasamser jaṅdevānām sadāsamaravijayinām || || (fol. 8r1–3) svasti śrīśvara caraṇasmaraṇapūrvaka rūpanārāyaṇetyādi vvidhavirudhāvaḷīvirājamāna mānonnata śrīmanmahārājādhirāja śrī śrī śrīman + + + + sena bahādūra devānām sadāsamaravijayināṃ || || (fol. 8r3–5)
notes: The colophon is undated. 'Kṛṣṇasāhakāritā ... kaviviracitā praśastiratnāvaliḥ' makes Kṛṣṇasāha, grandson of Narabhūpāla of Gorkha, the patron of the composition. Nothing says he commissioned or donated this copy, so the catalogue's 'Donor' field is doubtful. Fol. 8r1–5 has two praśasti formulae in honorific genitive plural (devānām ... sadāsamaravijayinām). The first is for Gīrvāṇayuddhavikramaśāha (r. 1799–1816). The second is for a Sena ruler styled Rūpanārāyaṇa, whose name is lost in the lacuna; he is probably of the Palpa/Makwanpur Senas, perhaps Pṛthvīpālasena, but that is unverified. Since this is a manual of praśastis, these may be specimen formulae rather than a statement of the reigning king. If they are contemporary, they put the copy roughly in 1799–1806 CE. That is an inference only. 'rāmahṛ(!)yaḥ' is read as Rāmahṛdaya. 'vāṇīvilāsa' could be the poet's name or an epithet.

p2 Kṛṣṇasāha: role changed from 'commissioner' to 'other'. '-kāritā' goes with 'kaviviracitā praśastiratnāvaliḥ', so he paid for the composition of the text, not for this copy. The catalogue calls him 'Donor', but the colophon does not support that.
Removed the relation p2 under_reign_of p5. Nothing in the colophon ties the patron of the composition to Gīrvāṇayuddha's reign.

p5 Gīrvāṇayuddhavikramaśāha: confidence lowered to medium, and bahādura/śamśera/jaṅga added to titles. The fol. 8r praśastis may be sample formulae added to this praśasti manual rather than a statement of the reigning king.
p6: the name is lost in the lacuna, so 'Sena' alone is not a usable name. The name field now marks the gap, and the role is changed to 'other' (addressee of a sample praśasti), low confidence.
p4 Vāṇīvilāsa: confidence lowered to medium, because 'vāṇīvilāsa' could be an epithet of the poet rather than his name.
p3: confidence for the reading Rāmahṛdaya kept at medium. The epithet 'rājakulaśiromaṇi-pravilasat-pādāravindadvanda' added to evidence.

title: Meghadūta
subject: Kāvya
colophon: iti śrīkālidāsakṛtau meghadūtākhyaṃ mahā(2)kāvyaṃ samāptaṃ || śubham astu || itthaṃ bhūtaṃ sucaritam idaṃ meghadū(3)taṃ ca nāmnā kāmakrīḍāvirahitajane viprayoge vinodi (!) prema(4)ś cāsmin nitinipuṇatāṃ buddhibhāvaṃ kavīnāṃ natvāryāyāś ca(5)raṇayugalaṃ kālidaś cakāra || 1 || || śrī || śrī || saṃvat 1737(6) varṣa āśvinamāse kṛṣṇapakṣe pratipaddine sarojapuṭabhedane (7) likhitam idaṃ kāvyaṃ bhaṭṭagiridhareṇa svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca || (fol. 22v1–7)
purpose: svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca (for himself and for others)
notes: The catalogue gives the scribe as Girirājabhaṭṭa and the date as VS 1732. The colophon clearly reads 'bhaṭṭagiridhareṇa' and 'saṃvat 1737', so either the catalogue is wrong or the cataloguer misread the manuscript. The era is not named, but 'saṃvat' in a Devanagari manuscript points to VS. VS 1737 = CE 1680 (Āśvina, so September–October 1680 if the year starts in Caitra). It would be 1681 if the year starts in Kārttika. 'sarojapuṭabhedane' = 'in the town (puṭabhedana) of Saroja'. Saroja means 'lotus', so this may be a Sanskrit rendering of a place name like Kamala-/Padma-pura. It cannot be identified, so normalized is left empty. The verse after the colophon ('itthaṃ bhūtaṃ sucaritam ...') is an addition with errors ('vinodi (!)', 'nitinipuṇatāṃ' for nīti-, 'kālidaś' for Kālidāsa). It names only the author, not any other person.

Added the second spelling of the author's name in the closing verse (kālidaś, corrupt for Kālidāsa) to the notes; Kālidāsa stays as author only.
Expanded the notes: the catalogue's scribe name (Girirājabhaṭṭa) and date (VS 1732) conflict with the colophon; possible reading of the place name; how ce_approx was worked out.

title: Meghadūtaṭīkā
subject: Kāvya
colophon: iti śrīcaritravardhanaviracitā meghadūtākhyakāvyaṭīkā saṃpūrṇā (8) || || || śubham astu || || samāptaḥ || nabhorasābdhyaikamite śakebde saṃvatsare caiva parābhaākye ṛtau śarannāmni karāhvayetho sadosvije (9) māsi ca somavāre|| 1 || ādimāyāṃ tithau caiva site pakṣe ca vaidhṛtau prayoga likhitaṃ hyetat jo(ga)devasya sūnunā || 2 || ...(10) (fol. 29v7–10)
notes: Chronogram: nabhas 0, rasa 6, abdhi 4, eka 1. Read right to left this gives ŚS 1460 (c. 1538 CE), which matches the catalogue. The saṃvatsara is named Parābhava. In the southern 60-year cycle Parābhava falls in ŚS 1468 (1546/47), and ŚS 1460 would be Vilambin. Under northern Bārhaspatya reckoning the name may differ by a few years, so the year and the saṃvatsara do not fully agree. 'sadosvije' is probably a corruption of 'sad-āśvije' (Āśvina). 'karāhvaye 'tho' is taken as the nakṣatra Hasta. 'prayoga' may be a corruption of 'prayāge' (written at Prayāga), but this is uncertain. Both readings fit the anuṣṭubh metre. The scribe is identified in the quoted text only as the son of Jogadeva (reading of 'jo(ga)' uncertain). The name Rāmeśvarabhaṭṭa is the catalogue's tentative suggestion, perhaps from the omitted line 10, so it is not verified. Caritravardhana is the author of the commentary, not connected with this copy.

notes: This is a chapter colophon inside the text, at the end of sarga 15 of Cāritravardhana's Śiśuhitaiṣiṇī commentary on the Raghuvaṃśa ('rāghavīyaṭīkā'). The catalogue spells the title 'Śiṣuhitaiṣiṇī' and the colophon has 'śuṣuhitaiṣiṇyāṃ'; both stand for Śiśuhitaiṣiṇī. It gives no scribe, date or place for this copy. Everyone named here belongs to the composition of the commentary, not to this copy. Araḍakamalla, of the Śrīmāla lineage, asked for the commentary to be written ('sabhyārthita', probably meant as 'abhyarthita'), so he is the patron of the original work. 'taranija(4)prābhācārya' is corrupt. Possible readings are Taruṇaprabhācārya or (kharatara-gacchīya-)Jinaprabhācārya. Other sources give Cāritravardhana's teacher as Kalyāṇarāja, which this colophon does not confirm. 'prapādapadmopajīvi' probably stands for '-pada-padmopajīvi' (living at the lotus feet of). 'naraveśasarasvatī' is probably an epithet meaning 'Sarasvatī in human form' ('naraveṣa-'), not an office.
review: p3: name given as best reading 'Taruṇaprabha' instead of the non-name 'Taranijaprabha'; confidence lowered to low (corrupt form; 'Jinaprabha' is also possible)
p1: 'naraveśasarasvatī' kept in titles but flagged in notes as an honorific epithet ('Sarasvatī in human guise'), not an office
notes: added that all persons belong to the composition of the commentary, not to this copy, and that the catalogue title 'Śiṣuhitaiṣiṇī' should read Śiśuhitaiṣiṇī

notes: The primary copying took place in Pāṭalīputra (Patna, Bihar) in Saṃvat 1612 (cataloguer assumes Śaka = 1690 CE, but it could also be Vikrama = 1556 CE). A secondary dated entry mentions that Mahīdhara acquired or dealt with the manuscript in Kāśī: 'samvat 1635 varṣe māghavadi 11 bhṛgau mahīdhareṇa kāśyāṃ kṛtaṃ pustakaṃ'.

colophon: || iti dhenupūjā || || iti śrīvarāhavivāhakhaṇḍa pustakaḥ samāptaḥ || || || śaśiyamābhṛtābdā tu kṛṣṇāśvinapratipadā || bhṛgurevativyāghātaṃ śubhalagne ca samāptam || || bhaktyāpurīnagaryā ca trayorājā virājate || dharmajyotiś ca kīrtiś ca jyeṣṭhamadhya kaniṣṭhayoḥ || || ity atra likhitāt prācīna tāḍapatrapustakāt svakīyabhāratibhavanārthaṃ śrīmadrājaguruhemarājavidvadvareṇa pūrṇaprasādaśarmadvārā vaikramābda 85 āṣāḍhaśuklapañcamyāṃ śukravāsare likhitam iti śabh (!) || || (fol. 16r7–10)
purpose: svakīyabhāratibhavanārtham (for his own library, Bhāratī Bhavana)
notes: The manuscript quotes an earlier palm-leaf exemplar colophon mentioning the joint reign of the three brothers Jayadharmamalla, Jayajyotirmalla, and Jayakīrtimalla in Bhaktapur ('bhaktyāpurīnagaryā ca trayorājā virājate || dharmajyotiś ca kīrtiś ca jyeṣṭhamadhya kaniṣṭhayoḥ'). The cataloguer recorded Bhaktapur as place of copying based on this exemplar colophon. The present paper copy was prepared in VS [19]85 (1928 CE) by Pūrṇaprasāda Śarmā for Rājaguru Hemarāja Śarmā's collection (Bhāratī Bhavana).

title: Sārasvataṭīkā
subject: Vyākaraṇa
colophon: iti śrīmālīmarakulaśrīmārabhāraśrīmālajñātikulatilakasakalakṣitipālānaṃdanāyaka- śrīmālave(teśā)dhipatimaṃḍalapācalamahānagaralaṃkaraṇapātasāhaśrīgayāsadīnasamastasaptāṅgarājyasakalaṣaḍbalasakalaśrīkaraṇādhiśvaramaṃtrīvaraśrījīvānātmajamahāpuruṣamaṃtrivaraśrīpuṃjarājasāhaviraviracitā sārasvatīṭīkā saṃpūrṇasamāptā || || atha graṃthakarttā viṣṇukaviḥ kam api viśeṣam āha || garvvaṃ parihartuṃ | vyākhyāviśeṣonnayanaprasaṃgāt śrīpuṃjarājo yad (ihāmyaghattā) āvistaraṃ cāru viniścitārthaṃ sarvvaṃ samūlaṃ samapekṣitaṃ tat || || ātmayuktibalaśālināṃ bacovistarān mama bibheti bhāratī | tena durnayanivāraṇocitepūrvakovidamatevilīyate || || cāvījñānatamonimīlitatayā mālinyam artheṣu ye saṃśuddheṣṭāpi tanvate na tadhīkāraḥ parīkṣāvidhau || kiṃ tv ete guṇadoṣayoḥ samadēśor vairāgyaniṣṭhā iva śreṣṭhāhaṃtaparoktinispṛhadhiyas tasmād amībhyo namaḥ || || || iti śrīmaṃḍapācalamahādurgādhipatipātisāhaśrīgayāsadīnasakalamaṃtrī śvarasāhaśrīpuṃjarājasya sakalabhūlokakīrtiprasiddhaye puṃjarājadraviṇasudhāsiktamahākavitvasūktamahākavivaraviṣṇukavikṛtā puṃjarājasahitā puṃjarājīnāmasārasvatīṭīkā samāptā || || ❁ || || saṃvat 843 vaiśākhaśuklacaturddaśī budhavāra (thvakuhnu) vatāgṛhanivāsaka śrībhavānīśaṃkarasyaputra śrīgaurīśaṃkara(ṇathva) ṭīkā (kaṣṭana coyā juro) || (fol.202r3-202v8)
notes: The original work (Puñjarājī / Sārasvataṭīkā) was composed by Viṣṇukavi under the patronage of minister Puñjarāja (son of Jīvāna) during the reign of Sultan Ghiyāsuddīn of Māṇḍū (Māṇḍapācala). The copyist Gaurīśaṅkara, son of Bhavānīśaṅkara, completed copying in NS 843.

notes: Although the era is stated as 'śrīśāke 1939', 1939 is almost certainly a Vikrama Saṃvat date (VS 1939 Kārttika śukla 15 corresponds to Thursday, 26 October 1882 CE, matching 'guruvāsare'). Bāhula designates the month of Kārttika. 'Kavardāra' corresponds to the administrative title kapardāra (storekeeper/steward).

title: Sārasvatavyākaraṇa

date_raw: phālguṇe ca site pakṣe saptamyāṃ jīvavāsare | bhalanī brahmayoge ca ... aṣṭau śataśathīsaptai ete saṃkhyāsamvatsare
colophon: iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakā ʼnubhūtisvarūpācāryyaviracitāyāṃ sārasvatīprakriyā samāptāḥ(!) || || ❁ || || ❁ || || śubham astu sadā sarvvadā kālaṃ śubha || || ❖ yadu śuddham aśuddham vā leṣako nāsti diṣaṇaṃ | yathā dṛṣṭa tathā likhitaṃ mama doṣo na dīyate || || ❖ phālguṇe ca site pakṣe saptamyāṃ jīvavāsare | bhalanī brahmayoge ca taddine pūrṇṇasiddhayet || aṣṭau śataśathīsaptai ete saṃkhyāsamvatsare | puṣṭakaṃ likhitaṃ caiva manidharatapodhanāt || || ❖ pādacchāyā dviguṇaṃ kīrtvā caturddaśasamaṃnvita | pakṣe navakare bhāgalabdhau danta tataḥ paraṃ || (dinavāhana || gādhu arthahāni1 || śalaratnarābha 2 || kiśistrī rābha 3 || phasi maraṇa 4 || dhdhal mṛtyu 5 || siṃhaśatrunāśa 6 || kāka dhanahani 7 || haṃsa artharābha 8 || thava nakṣatradinadinayā nakṣatrato dviyabhā 9 || (fol.157r1-157v2 )

date_raw: abde lakṣmaṇabhūpate ṛtusaridyo(gīmahe)śānanair bbhavye bhāskaravāsare sugaṇite māghe dvitīyāśite
colophon: iti śrībhaṭṭōjadīksītaviracitāyāṃ siddhāṃtakaumidyām pūrvvārddhāṃ saṃpūrṇṇaṃ || oṃ || śubham astu (jayatu)/// abde lakṣmaṇabhūpate ṛtusaridyo(gīmahe)śānanair bbhavye bhāskaravāsare sugaṇite māghe dvitīyāśite | siddhāntādyanukaumudīṃ sama[likhat sū]trārtham āvaśyakaṃ grāme maithilasaṃsthitau surahike | [pu]sta[[ka]]lekhanapariśamavettā vidvajjno nānyaḥ| sāgaralaṃgha(na)/// (fol. 95r11-13)
notes: The manuscript was copied in the village of Surahikā in Mithilā. The colophon breaks off at the end (sāgaralaṃgha(na)///), where the scribe's name was likely recorded. The chronogram for the Lakṣmaṇasena era (LS) year is difficult to reconstruct with certainty due to damaged akṣaras.

colophon: iti saskṛtama(!)maṃjaryyāṃ dayitayoḥ saṃvāde śṛgārasa(!)saṃgrahe dvitīyām kusumaṃ || [Artha] iti saṃskṛtamaṃjaliko bhāṣāṭīkā mahā dayitayoḥ savāde(!) bhannu duvai strīpuruṣako saṃvādamagāśṛgārasa(!)saṃgrahe bhannu śṛgārasa(!)saṃgraha bhannugaryākā dvitīyaṃ kusumaṃ duvai cāhi phula ho || śubha || saṃmvat 1006 mārga śudi 8 roja 2 mā saṃpurṇa bhayo tejaratnaṃ gubhājuko pustaka ho (thva saṃskṛtamaṃjalipustaka svāvāhālayā tejaratnayā gujula , thvasaphu suyāta viyasadu, miyanaṃ madu , lobhayāyaṃ madu, davāya savāya yāyaṃ madu, davāyā sāmaṃ lobhayā sāmaṃ , tadhaṃgupāpa, paṃca māhāpāpalāyu, bhiṃnakaṃ svāhāke vakṣayā pāpisaṃnidānayā nāsatamā ) (fol.75r3-75v4)

title: Nṛtyeśvaramahābhairavapūjāpaddhati
subject: Karmakāṇḍa
colophon: iti śrīśrīśrīnāṭeśvara mahā(2)(bhai)ravapūjāpaddhati samāptaḥ || || śrī 3 sveṣṭadevatā prīnātu sarvvadā || || śubhaṃ || || (3) /// (yā)dṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭā, tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā | yadi śuddham aśuddhaṃ vā, mama doṣo nadiyate (4)/// || || śrīnepālasamvat 805 || śrīkarigata samvat 4785 || śrīvikramāditya samvat (5) 1741 || śrīśake samvat 1606 || māghamāse, śuklapakṣa || śrīpaṇcamyāyātithai || reva(6)ti nakṣete || śubhayoge || yathākarana mūhūtake || bṛhaspativāśale || kubhaṃrāsi gate śa(1)(vita)rī || mīnarāśi gate candramaśi || || thvakuhnu śrīśrīsumati jaya jitāmitramallava(2)rmmaṇā svakarena likhitaṃ saṃpūrṇṇaṃ || || aneka karmmanā sveṣṭhā, devī prīnātu siddhidā (3)/// ta kṛtaṃ karma, kṣatu marhasi me sadā || jitāmitrasya bhūpasya, tvāṃ vinā nāsti (4)/// gati .. tvadbhakti tatparā śaktir mmatirbhūyāt kulāmbike || || śrī 3 bhavānīśaṃkrarābhyaṃ (5) namaḥ || || śrīśrīsumati jaya jitāmitramalladevasana śrīśrīśrīnāṭeśvara mahābhaira(6)(va)sake tavagvaḍa ghaṃsthā duṃtāyā thva padhati juroṃ || bhāgīrāmayā verasa juroṃ || || (1) nānā granthasa soyāva pūjāpaddhati saṃphuḍi mahākastana dayakā anahelā yāya mateva ya(2)(tna)pūrvvakana nidāna yāya mālaḥ || || e || || śrīśrīśrīnāṭeśvara prīnātu || śubhaṃ || || (exp. 16b1-17b2)
purpose: pūjāpaddhati prepared in connection with offering a large bell (tavagvaḍa ghaṃṭā) to Nāṭeśvara Mahābhairava
notes: King Jayajitāmitramalla of Bhaktapur wrote the manuscript with his own hand (svakarena likhitaṃ) and compiled the paddhati from multiple texts (nānā granthasa soyāva pūjāpaddhati saṃphuḍi mahākastana dayakā). Bhāgīrāma was the prominent minister/administrator in Bhaktapur under his reign.

title: Svayambhūpurāṇa

colophon: iti dharmmadhātusvayabhūtpattidharmmamāhātmyasubhāṣitasūtraṃ daśamādhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || ○ || ye dharmmā hetuprabhā(!)vā, hetu(!) teṣāṃ tathāgataḥ | hy avadat teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ || ○ || śreyo stu saṃvat 813 dita rāthoke pūrṇṇamāśi kunhu, likhitasaṃpūrṇṇaṃ kṛtvā, gṛhasthāpitā bhavanti | /// ⁅de⁆vācāryeṇa svārthaputrapautrādiśikṣāya (!) hetunārthaṃ likhitaṃ kṛtaṃ || etatpuṇyānubhāvena jajamānasya āyurārogyajanadhanamakānalakṣmīvṛddhir astu | paratra sukhāvatīm āpnuyāt || ○ || śubham astu sarvvadā kāla(!) kalyāṇam astuḥ(!) || (fol. 92r6–92v4)
purpose: svārthaputrapautrādiśikṣārtham (for the instruction of oneself, sons, and grandsons)
notes: The name of the scribe/owner is preceded by a lacuna (/// ⁅de⁆vācāryeṇa), possibly representing a longer name ending in -devācārya. The month expression 'dita rāthoke' likely refers to dvir-āṣāḍha (intercalary Āṣāḍha) or similar corrupt reading.

title: Kāśīmāhātmya

notes: The cataloguer marked Scribe as '??'. The syntax 'śrīrāma likhitaṃ motirāma vidyārathi(!)putrasya haranārāyaṇa' opens with the invocation śrīrāma, followed by 'likhitaṃ motirāma' (written by Motirāma) and the genitive phrase for the owner/patron 'vidyārathi(!)putrasya haranārāyaṇa' (of Haranārāyaṇa, son of Vidyārathi). 'vidyārathi(!)' may be corrupt for Vidyārthī or Vidyāratha.

notes: The chronogram 'rasa' (6), 'abhra' (0), 'śruti' (4) gives NS 406 during the reign of King Anantamalla/Ānandamalla. The phrase 'nelālabhūpāṇānandamallābhipārvati' stands for 'nepālabhūpāle ānandamalle 'bhipālayati'. The title 'kāyachā' is a scribal corruption of kāyastha; 'pujadine' may be an error for 'kujadine' (Tuesday) or 'budhadine' (Wednesday).

title: Kulārṇavatantram
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: || iti śrīkulārṇavamahārahasye sapādalakṣagranthe pañcamakhaṇḍe nāmavāsanādikathanaṃnāma saptadaśollāsasamāptaḥ || || śrībhavānīśaṃkaraprītir astu || || dvitīyanāgābdhiyute gate nepālavatsare | māghamāsya site pakṣe ekādaśāttithau (!) śubhe || pūrṇṇarājadivjasyājñāṃ dhṛtvāśirapico(?) kutulilekha daivajñaḥ pustakaṃ ca kulārṇṇavaṃ || || samvat 782 māghakṛṣṇa ekādaśyāṃ tithau kutujosina saṃpūrṇṇa coyā || || (fol. 198r4–6 and v1–2)
notes: The chronogram in verse reads 'dvitīyanāgābdhi' (abdhi = 4? likely a corruption of adri = 7, since the prose confirms NS 782). The verse gives the pakṣa as sita, whereas the prose colophon specifies māghakṛṣṇa. 'divjasya' in the verse is likely an error for daivajñasya or dvijasya. The scribe is called 'kutu ... daivajñaḥ' in Sanskrit and 'kutujosi' (Josi = Jyotiṣī/Daivajña) in Newari.

title: Kulārṇavatantram
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: || iti śrīkulārṇṇavamahārahasye sapādalakṣagranthe pañcamakhaṇḍanāmavāsanādikathanaṃnāma saptadaśamollāsaḥ || 7 || śrīmatanyaṃpāla (!)samvat bhuvanākāśabhairavaṃ | jyeṣṭhakṛṣṇacaturthe tu saṃpūrṇṇaṃ ravivāsare || likhārddhaṃ tasisiṃhena darddhaṃ bhavāniśaṃkarau | kulācārasya mahātmyaṃ mokṣārthaṃ likhitaṃ mayā || || || śubha || (fol. 128r5–8)
notes: The phrase 'śrīmatanyaṃpāla (!)samvat' is almost certainly a scribal error or misreading of 'śrīmannepālasaṃvat'. The chronogram bhuvanākāśabhairava represents 803 (bhuvana = 3, ākāśa = 0, bhairava = 8). Two scribes divided the copying: Tasisiṃha wrote one half and Bhavānīśaṅkara the other (likhārddhaṃ tasisiṃhena [ta]darddhaṃ bhavāniśaṃkar[eṇa]).

notes: Chronogram 'randhra-bhuja-phaṇīndra' yields 9-2-8 = NS 829. 'Īṣa' stands for Āśvina; 'sudhāṃsukṣaya' for kṛṣṇapakṣa; 'girijātmajatithi' refers to Gaṇeśacaturthī (4); 'jīvāhna' indicates Thursday. The scribe's name may be Naiṣṭhika, or 'naiṣṭhikī' (for naiṣṭhikaḥ) may merely be an adjective (perpetual student / brahmacārin) qualifying an unnamed son of Nepālasura.

colophon: samāptā caiyam (!) bhagavaty āryāṣṭasahasrikā prajñāpāramitā | dharma|| ||mudrā dharmāṅkā dharmanābhir ddharmabherī dharmanetrī sarvatathāgatajananī sarvabodhisatvapraryekajinaśrāvakāṇāñ ca mātā dharmaratnanidhānam akṣayo dharmakośo cintyādbhutadarśananakṣatramālā sarvasukhasampattihetur iti || ○ || sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvvalokavanditāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ samyag udgṛhya paryavāpya dhārayitvā pravartyaināṃ viharantu sadārthina iti || ❁ || ye dharmā hetuprabhavā etc. deyadharmo yaṃ mahāyānayāyi(nyāḥ) para .. .. .. .. śrīdharmadhātuvihāravāstavyaḥ śākyabhikṣuprajñāśrījñānasya yad atra puṇyan tad bhavatv ācāryopādhyāyamātāpitṛpūrvaṃgamaṅ kṛtvā sakalasatvarāśer anuttarajñānaphalāvāptaya iti || rājñaḥ śrīmadarimalladevasya vijayarājye | samvat 321 kārttikaśukladaśamyām | śaniścaravāsare | pūrvabhadranakṣatre || bodhau ye 〈na〉 kṛtamānasā jinasutā strātuṃ samastañ janaṃ pratyekām api samyabodhim (!) atulān dhyāyanti bhūyo pi ye śiṣyāḥ śiṣyapathānugā jagad idaṃ kleśābhibhūtaṃ ca yat | saddharmaśravaṇāya te sumanasaḥ sarve samāyāntv iha || lokaṃ prāpayituṃ sukhena padavīṃ sampaddvayāvāhinīṃ kāruṇyāhitacetasā bhagavatā buddhena sandīpitam | śrutvā te ʼkhiladharmatatvanilayaṃ sūtraṃ samādhānato gatvā sthānam aharniśan nijam alan dhyāyantu ye ʼbhyāgatāḥ || kāle smin bahudṛṣṭisaṃkulakalau pāde pi dūraṃgate nānābhedam anekapustakagatan dṛṣṭvādhunā śraddhayā | kupyadvādigajendrakumbhadalane bhadreṇa yā śodhitā lokārthaṃ hariṇā mayā suvu(di)taiḥ sarvaṃ budhair gṛhyatām iti || ○ || (fols. 379v3–
purpose: yad atra puṇyan tad bhavatv ācāryopādhyāyamātāpitṛpūrvaṃgamaṅ kṛtvā sakalasatvarāśer anuttarajñānaphalāvāptaya iti
notes: The corrector states he collated multiple manuscripts (anekapustakagataṃ dṛṣṭvā) and corrected the text: 'bhadreṇa yā śodhitā lokārthaṃ hariṇā mayā' (name could be Hari or Haribhadra). A female title/epithet 'mahāyānayāyi(nyāḥ)' precedes a lacuna before Prajñāśrījñāna's name.

title: Vasudhārādisaptadhāraṇī
subject: Bauddhadhāraṇī
colophon: ’’ āryagrahamātṛkānām adhāranīparisamāptā || ye dharmmāhetu prabhāvāhetu 〈〈vā〉〉 heṣāṃ tathāgatahevadatteṣā ca yā nirodha evaṃ vādimahāśravaṇaṃ || ❁ || samvat 910 phārguṇaśuklatṛtiyā buddhavāra kunhu ṅatabhucchayātor ādharadhana ‥‥ siṃyātacosyaṃ viyājuhā … (fol.31v1–5)
notes: The clause 'ṅatabhucchayātor ādharadhana ‥‥ siṃyātacosyaṃ viyājuhā' indicates the copy was written and given to someone ending in -siṃha (‥‥ siṃyāta). The role of 'ādharadhana' is unclear due to the lacuna: it may be a personal name (perhaps a father whose son received the manuscript, or an agent/scribe), hence assigned role 'other' with low confidence. 'ṅatabhucchayātor' refers to a neighborhood (tol) in the Ṅata (Nardevi) quarter of Kathmandu.

colophon: iti yathoktakalpadvayātmako mahāś cāsau tantrarājaś ceti mahātantrarājo hevajro yathoktārthaḥ samāptaḥ samyag āptaḥ || ❁ || mahāpaṇḍitaśrīkamalanāthasya mañjuśrīparanāmno hevajrapañjikāyāṃ dvitīyaḥ kalpaḥ || hevajravajrapadaratnakaraṇḍam etad udghāṭya puṇyam uditam yad atulyam adya | akṣuṇṇam akṣayam acintya guṇañ ca ratnam tenaitadekajagadābharaṇī karotu || samāptā ceyaṃ ratnāvalī nāma hevajrapañjikā | kṛtir iyaṃ mañjuśrīparanāmno mahāpaṇḍitaśrī kamalanāthasyeti || likhāpiteyaṃ pustikā paṇḍitabhikṣujinaśrīmitreṇa sarvasatvārthahetor iti || || || ❖ yoginīnāṃ bījāni : ase | ā vajrī | i gaurī | ī vāri | u vajraḍākinī | ū pukkuśī | ṛ śaarī | ṝ cāṇḍālī | lṛ ḍomvī | lṝ gauryāyā | e caurī | ai vetālī | o ghasmarī | au bhūcarī | aṃ khecarī || ○ || ā sihhanī | ī vyāghriṇī | ū jambukī || ṝ ulūkinī | lṝ rājendrā | ai dīptateje | au vūṣaṇī | aṃ kambojī || || || (fol. 40r1–5)
notes: The author Kamalanātha also bears the name/alias Mañjuśrī (mañjuśrīparanāman).

notes: Bhavānīśaṃkara / Umeśa refers to the divine couple Bhavānī and Śaṅkara (Umā and Īśa) for whose pleasure the manuscript was collected (saṃcita).

colophon: iti śrīmadādidevād vinirggate paṃcāśatkoṭivistīrṇāt śrīmatkubjikāmahāmatottame śrīmatkularatnodyote prayāgādicakrapūjāpratiṣṭhānānākarmmakaraṇakarmmāraṃbhācāryābhiṣekayoginām aṃteṣṭividhāno nāma caturddaśamaḥ paṭalaḥ || 14 || || śrīmatkulāgamaṃ hy etat paścimāmnāyasaṃbhavaṃ | sūcakaṃ sarvvamārggāṇāṃ bhaviṣyavidhinā sphuṭaṃ || || pakṣe śite(!) cāśvinanāmadheye tithau tṛtīyāṃ (!) dharaṇīsuteʼhni | śrīharṣadevasya ca varddhamāne rājye mahānaṃdakare vrajānāṃ || 1 || nepāladeśaṃ samupāgatena kāṣṭhābhidhamaṃḍapasaṃsthitena | svaśiṣyavarggasya vibodhanāya paropakārāya kṛtaprayatnaḥ || 2 || bhaktyā svayaṃ śrīkularatnapūrvvam udyotasaṃtaṃ bṛhadāgamedaṃ |(!) śrīmatkulācāryavivekaratnake- nāpi saṃlekhita (!) paṃḍitena || || || samāptam idaṃ śrīkularatnodyotam itiḥ(!) || || saṃkhyāsahasradvitayaṃ ca sārddhaṃ siddhyākaraṃ śrīkularatnadīpaṃ | śrīmatparākhyena vibodhanāya devyā(!) parāyāḥ kathitaṃ samastam itiḥ(!) || || naṃdaṃtu kulayoginyo naṃdaṃtu kulaputrakāḥ | naṃdaṃtu śrīkulācāryā ye cānye kuladīkṣitāḥ || || śubham astu sarvvajagatāṃ caturāśramāṇāṃ || (fol. 138r1–138v3)

title: Vaidyajīvana
subject: Āyurveda
date_raw: śāke 1714 saṃvat 18〈〈8〉〉90āśvī dvitīyā 2 mamgalavāra , [ṭikā: VS khaṃ vahni siṃdubhir (!) jeṣṭakṛṣṇa 7 bhṛguvāra] (!)
colophon: iti śrīman manohara sūnunā gosvāminā harinātha kṛtāyāṃ vaidyajīvanaṭīkāyāṃ praṃcamo (!) vilāsaḥ || śrīmad bhūpati vikramādgaṇanā khaṃ vahni sindhubhisindubhi(!)r || māse jeṣṭa (!) asi saptamī tithai (!) vāre bhṛguśoriyaṃ || ṭīkā || vaidyajivanasya(!)racī || śrīnātha gosvāmibhīr cautastvaṃṭamārithe śarayure dhāryā bhiṣagbhiḥ || sadā || likhiṃ[[ta]] puruṣottama bhrāmhana (!) paṃḍītasya (!) chaganajīvrane pustakalītaṃ (!) pustakaṃ || miti āsvī dvitīyāṃ 2 maṃgalavāsare || || saṃvat || || 1890 || || vṛṣe śākha || || 17 || 14 || || śubhaṃ bhūyāt || śrī mutharaśa (!) || ❁ || ❖ ❁ śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ || ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ ❁ (fol.67r1–67v3)
notes: The colophon first records the composition date of the ṭīkā in a chronogram (VS 1730 or similar: khaṃ vahni sindhu..., Jyeṣṭha kṛṣṇa 7, Friday). The copy date gives both Saṃvat 1890 and Śākha (Śāke) 1714 (which are discordant: ŚS 1714 = c. 1792 CE, VS 1890 = c. 1833 CE). The commissioner's name 'chaganajīvrane' likely represents 'Chaganajī-[kāraṇe]'. 'śrī mutharaśa (!)' at the end might be Mathurā or a name/scribal remark.

title: Yogataraṅgiṇī
subject: Āyurveda
colophon: iti śrītrimallabhaṭṭagrathitāyāṃ yogataraṃgiṇyāṃ sarvarogacikitsākathanaṃ nāmas (!) taraṃgaḥ || || śrīvaikrame grahaśaśinavacaṃ māsavaiśāṣaśīte || punyatithau hastānakṣatre vyāghātayoge ravidine ca || yogataraṅgiṇīnāmākhyā bhaiṣajaṃ sārasarvaprakāraṃ || kāṇtipūram aṣanavihāravāstavyaṃ ṭhākurmanena hastaṃ || likhitvām idaṃ ca (9) paropakārārthe. saṃcitā gṛhe mayā || darsanena pāpaṃ pracāreṇa tāpaṃ. haraṃtī śaukhyaṃ pradaṃ || || jādistaṃ pustakaṃ dṛstvāt tādṛṣṭaṃ li(10)liṣitaṃ mayā. yadi suddho maśuddho vā mama dokho na diyate || || yo pustaka leṣadāmā śrīrājakulamā. maile †śrīarjavegī† bhai va(11)sdā sāthi varṣakā umerakā velāmā atidharmmaceṣṭā bhaiḥ paropakāra garnā nimitta āphnā hastākṣarale yoḥ yogataraṅgiṇī nā(12)mā graṃṇṭha saṃpūrṇa samāptī garyāko ho || || subham astu sadā sarvvadā kalyāṇaṃ dṛrgham āyur astu || || śubham || ❁ || (fol. 292r6-12)
notes: The chronogram 'graha-śaśi-nava-caṃ' indicates VS 1919 (graha=9, śaśi=1, nava=9, caṃ/candra=1). In the vernacular Nepali section, the scribe mentions copying the text at the age of sixty ('sāthi varṣakā umerakā velāmā') while serving at the royal palace ('śrīrājakulamā') as an 'arjavegī' (arz-begī).

title: Itihāsasamuccaya
subject: Itihāsa
colophon: || itihāsasamuccaye nāradapuṇḍarīkasaṃvādo nāma dvātriṃśatitamoʼdhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || || lasannākanāthā layenopamāne, mahīmaṇḍāsmin pure bhaktasaṃjñe | nṛpe śāsati śrījitāmitra malle, kaniṣṭhogramalle virājatpratāpe || nepāle hāyanesmin grahanidhi turage caitramāse tamiśre, vaidhṛtyāṃ revatī divasakara śaśina saṃgame somavāre | devīprītyā sudhīmān śivahari dharaṇī daivatoyetihāsaṃ, vyāsoktaṃ pustakātryāṃ vitarāte śivasiṃhaḥsma daivajñe dhīraḥ || (fol. 161r2–5)
notes: The catalogue gives NS 997, but the chronogram 'graha-nidhi-turage' (graha=9, nidhi=9, turaga=7) interpreted in reverse order yields NS 799 (c. 1679 CE), which corresponds to the reign of Jitāmitramalla of Bhaktapur (r. 1673–1696 CE). 'divasakara-śaśina-saṃgame' denotes the conjunction of sun and moon (amāvāsyā).

title: Itihāsasamuccaya
