purpose: śrī3 bhavānīśaṃkaraprītina / umeśaprītaye (for the pleasure of Bhavānīśaṃkara / Umeśa)
notes: The Newari verb form 'coyakāvadayākā' (coyakāva dayakā) literally means 'having had [it] written and prepared', which points to commissioning, though the cataloguer identifies Kālidāsa as the scribe.

title: Kavikalpalatā
subject: *Sāhitya
colophon: iti kavikalpalatā samāptā || || śubhaṃ bhavatu lekhakapāṭhakayoḥ || || (3)❖ varṣe bhujebhaturage (dharaṇīja) vāre, ‥ ‥ stithāvi(ti ‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ ’ryamarthkṣe | śrī‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ 'sya ‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ (4)‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ ‥ likhata śivahariḥ kavi[[ka]]lpavallīṃ || saṃvat 782 āśvinamāse (5) kṛṣṇapakṣe caturddaśyāṃ tithau aṃgā[[ra]] vāsare uttaraphālguṇinakṣatre brahmayoge sampūrṇ〈ṇ〉aṃ likhitaṃ (6) kavikalpalatāpustakaṃ †yaśalache† śrīśivaharivipreṇa svapāṭhārthaṃ || śubham astu sarvvadaiva || || (fol. 90r2–6)
notes: The chronogram 'bhujebhaturage' (bhuja = 2, ibha = 8, turaga = 7) confirms NS 782, and dharaṇījavāra matches aṅgāravāsara (Tuesday). The phrase '†yaśalache†' is likely a tole (locality) name where Śivahari resided or copied the text. A heavily damaged name preceded by 'śrī... sya' in line 3 may have referred to a reigning monarch or patron, but it is too broken to identify.

notes: Both VS 1734 and ŚS 1599 are given, corresponding to 1677 CE. Śaṃkarapurī is likely a Daśanāmī saṃnyāsī scribe, though grammatically it could alternatively denote a place (Śaṃkarapurī).

colophon: iti śrīmadanantabhaṭṭaviracite vidhānapārijāte gaṇahomavidhānaṃ || || śrīmatkaṇvakulādhiśītakiraṇo vidyākalānāṃ nidhiḥ śrīmadviṇupadāśritaḥ sarasagur vvidvaccakorapriyaḥ || yalhaṃbhaṭṭa ity hy abhut pṛthupaśās tasyātmajo būn hahāṃś candrāc candravalevasu ‥ ‥ guṇabhṛc chrīnāgadevābhidhaḥ || tasmāc chrīmadanaṃta āvir abhavad yajjñānabhaktyādike- ṣveto (!) nāsti guṇeṣu yasya ca hariḥ prṣṭho varīvarttate (!) || tenāyaṃ carito vidhānadiviṣadvṛkṣo rthisarvapradaḥ || kāle dvyaṣaṭaṣa(ḍe) kalāṃkakamite 1682 kāśyām agāt pūrṇatāṃ || || saṃti graṃthasahasrāṇi vidvadbhi (!) racitāny api || ko py sya mahimā vedyo bhijñair jayati sarvataḥ || na pāṃḍityābhimānena na ca vittasya lipsayā || graṃtho yaṃ racitaḥ kiṃtur (!) hareḥ prītyai satām api || (fol. 211v10-212r2) … iti śrīmadvidvajjanakṛpāpātrībhūtena śrīmadanaṃtabhaṭṭenāvacaritastavakaṃpaṃcakasaṃyuto (!) vidhānapārijātākhyo nibaṃdhaḥ samāptaḥ ❁ vidhānapārijāto yaṃ paṃcastavakasaṃyutaḥ || nānāvidhānagaṃdhāḍhyaḥ sasevyo vibudhir iha || ❁ || śubham astu sarvadā ❁ (fol. 212r6-8)

title: Viṣṇurudrī
subject: Krmakāṇḍa
colophon: īti(!) śrīviṣṇurudrisamāptam || || || guṇāganande śaśivikramābde jyaṣṭhaś ca kṛṣ(kvakṣye)tṛtīyā ca mandai || dolāgirīcampakavṛkṣamūle virājamānaś ca lakṣmīpatīṣu || 1 || abhiṣeṣakāmāgaruḍadhvajasyāliṣya pustakapuruṣaś ca sūktaṃ || viṣṇuś ca kailāśa ānandasarmmā samarpitaṃ (saśrītṛ)vikramāya || 2 || || || || || (x.50b3-51a1)
purpose: for the abhiṣeka of Garuḍadhvaja (Viṣṇu), offered to Trivikrama (samarpitaṃ Trivikramāya)
notes: The catalogue conflates the names and surroundings into 'Viṣṇukailāśānandarāja upādhyāya'. The meter and sandhi reveal three individuals: Viṣṇu (viṣṇuś ca), Kailāśa (kailāśa[ḥ]), and Ānandaśarman (ānandaśarmmā), described as 'abhiṣekakāmā[ḥ]' (plural). 'Dolāgiri campakavṛkṣamūle' refers to the famous champak tree shrine of Viṣṇu at Dolādri/Dolāgiri (Changu Narayan); Garuḍadhvaja, Lakṣmīpati, and Trivikrama are epithets of the deity Viṣṇu worshipped there.

colophon: iti bhairavasrotasi mahātaṃtre vidyāpīṭhe brahmayāmale navākṣaravidhā(6)ne dvādaśasāhasrake ekottaraśatimaḥ (!) paṭalaḥ samāptam (!) || || śubham || ❁ || ❁ || (fol. 439v5–6)

title: Phetkariṇītantra
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: || iti śrībhairavācāryaviracitaṃ phetkāriṇītaṃtraṃ dvāviṃśatiḥ (!) paṭalaḥ samāptam || 22 || || yad akṣarapadabhrṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ ca yad bhavet || (13) tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ devi prasīda parameśvarī (!) || śrīśāke 1779 śrīsaṃvat 1914 sāla miti śrāvaṇavadi 1 roja 3 etad dine samāptam || || (fol. 42r12–13)
notes: The catalogue lists the scribe as Jitānanda, but this name does not appear in the quoted colophon extract.

title: Bhuvaneśvarītantra
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: || iti śrībhuvaneśvaritaṃtre(2) kālikramanirṇayasūtraṃ trayaḥcatvāriṃśaḥ (!) paṭalaḥ samāptam || śubam || (fol. 108v1–2)

title: Phetkariṇītantra
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: iti śrībhairavācāryaviracitaṃ phetkariṇītaṃtraṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ || śrīkrodhabhairavaḥ śaraṇaṃ || śubhaṃ || śrīsveṣṭadevatāyai namaḥ || (5) śāke śareṣu pṛthivīpatibhir mite hi yugmasthite dinamaṇau gurūvāsare ca śrībhaktapattanapure likhad iṣṭadevyāḥ prītyai (6) idaṃ dvijavaro rāmānamdasaṃjñaḥ (!) yādṛśaṃ pustake dṛṣṭaṃ tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā yadi śuddham aśuddhaṃ vā mama doṣo na dīyatāṃ || (7) kaṣṭēna likhitaṃ graṃthaṃ yatnena paripālayed iti vijñaptidvayaṃ satsu || || śrīgaṇapataye namaḥ || || śubham astu || śrīr astu || (fol. 70v4–8)
notes: The chronogram 'śara' (5), 'iṣu' (5), 'pṛthivīpati' (16) indicates Śaka 1655. The position of the sun in Mithuna ('yugmasthite dinamaṇau') indicates solar Mithuna.

title: Phetkāriṇītaṃtra
subject: Tantra
colophon: iti śrībhairavācāryaviraci(41r1)taṃ phetkāriṇītaṃtraṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ || || śrīkrodhabhairavaḥ śaraṇam || śubhaṃm (!) || ❁ || ❁ || ○ || ○ || ○ || ❁ (fol.40v9–41r1)

title: Bhūtaḍāmaratantra
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: || iti śrībhūtaḍāmare mahātantre yakṣasiddhisādhanavidhiḥ pañcadaśaḥ paṭalaḥ || samāptaś cāyaṃ granthaḥ (fol. 37v4)

title: Bālatantra
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: || iti śrīkalyāṇena kṛte bālataṃtre nānāprayogakathanaṃ nāma caturdaśaḥ paṭalaḥ || śrīśrīśrīśrīśrīsaṃvat 171 varṣe kārttikamāse kṛṣṇāpakṣa ṣaṣṭīcaṃdravāreṇa vareśvareṇa liṣitaṃ bhaṭalakṣmaṇasya putreṇa || (fol. 64v10–11, 64r1–2)
notes: The catalogue records the scribe as Vīreśvara (text reads vareśvareṇa) and the date as SAM 1713 (text reads saṃvat 171 varṣe, where the final digit 3 was likely dropped in transcript).

title: Paradevatārādhanavidhi
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: ...mudrāṃ ca sampūjya || sarvonmādanamudrāṃ darśayet || iti pañcamāvaraṇaṃ ... antardaśāre sarvaśaktidaṃ- (exp.1.fol.32v1,2)

title: Mantramahodadhi
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: iti śrīmanmahīdharaviracite maṃtramahodadhau ṣaṭkarmādinirū(6)paṃam paṃcaviṃśas taraṃgaḥ || samvat 1760 māse vaiśākhe śūbham ||(fol. 29r5–6)
notes: The text Mantramahodadhi was composed in VS 1645 (referred to in the catalogue card's 'SAM 1645?'); the copy date is saṃvat 1760 (VS).

title: Bhāvacūḍāmaṇi
subject: Śaivatantra
colophon: iti tantracūḍāmaṇy antarggatabhāvacūḍāmaṇau bhāvanirṇṇayaḥ paṭalaḥ samāpto yaṃ granthaḥ || || ○ || (fol. 22r6–22v1)

title: Tarkarahasya
subject: Nyāya
colophon: iti tarkarahasyaṃ saṃpūrṇatām agāt || || (fol. 91v10)
